ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
Requirements: For the B.S. degree in Accounting, a minimum of 120 credits is required. Entrance to the major requires a minimum cumulative grade-point average (GPA) and the completion of specific core courses with a grade of C or better, including: Financial and Managerial Accounting (ACCTG 211), Introductory Microeconomic Analysis and Policy (ECON 102), Rhetoric and Composition (ENGL 15 or ENGL 30), Techniques of Calculus I (MATH 110 or MATH 140), and Introduction to Statistics (SCM 200 or STAT 200). First-year applicants must submit a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: Accounting is often called 'the language of business.' It is the primary means of communicating financial information about a business entity to its stakeholders. The Accounting major provides an opportunity for students to learn the concepts, procedures, and analytical skills that are used in the practice of accounting. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in public accounting, corporate accounting, government, and non-profit organizations. The major provides a strong foundation for students who plan to pursue professional certifications such as the CPA (Certified Public Accountant), CMA (Certified Management Accountant), and CIA (Certified Internal Auditor).
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting
Requirements: Entrance to the Acting major is by audition. Enrollment in the B.F.A. Acting program is limited. To be considered for admission, students must first apply to the University by completing the Penn State undergraduate application and also schedule an audition with the School of Theatre. For some programs, a pre-screening is required.
Description: The B.F.A. Acting program is a pre-professional training program intended for students who wish to pursue a career as a professional actor. The curriculum is based on a sequence of courses in acting, movement, and voice and speech. The first two years provide a foundation in various techniques. The final two years are focused on the application of these techniques in both the classroom and the production program. Students are required to take courses in theatre history, dramatic literature, and technical theatre. Admission to the program is by audition. Learning Outcomes: 1. Students will demonstrate the basic principles of the acting process: concentration, imagination, observation, and personalization. 2. Students will demonstrate proficiency in movement for the stage. 3. Students will demonstrate proficiency in voice and speech for the stage. 4. Students will demonstrate professional audition techniques. 5. Students will demonstrate an understanding of dramatic literature, theatre history, and the various technical aspects of theatre production.
Accredidation: The School of Theatre is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science
Requirements: Entrance to Major (ETM) Requirements: For entrance to the Actuarial Science major (ACTSC_BS), students must: (1) meet with an academic adviser and establish a plan of study; (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 3.20; and (3) complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H, MATH 140, MATH 141, and STAT 200.
Description: Actuarial Science is the study of the financial implications of uncertain future events. Actuaries study how to evaluate and manage financial risk. They use their specialized knowledge of mathematics, statistics, and business to design and manage programs that control risk. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for the professional examinations required for professional status as an actuary.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Advertising and Public Relations
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Advertising/Public Relations major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00; (3) have completed COMM 160 and COMM 180 with a grade of C or better.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Concentration: Advertising Option, Public Relations Option
Description: This major is designed to prepare students for careers as advertising or public relations practitioners. Students learn how to create and execute effective advertising and public relations campaigns, and they develop the research, writing, and creative skills necessary for success in these fields. The program offers two options: Advertising and Public Relations. The Advertising option focuses on the creative and strategic aspects of advertising, including copywriting, art direction, and media planning. The Public Relations option focuses on the strategic communication process that builds mutually beneficial relationships between organizations and their publics.
Accredidation: The Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Aerospace Engineering major, a student must: (1) have completed MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better; (2) have completed at least two of the following: EMCH 211, EMCH 212, and/or MATH 220, MATH 230, MATH 231, MATH 250, MATH 251 with a grade of C or better; (3) have earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 3.00. This GPA requirement may change each year.
Description: Aerospace engineering is the primary field of engineering concerned with the design, development, testing, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems and equipment. The field has traditionally been focused on atmospheric and space flight, with two major and overlapping branches: aeronautical engineering and astronautical engineering. Aerospace engineers develop new technologies for use in aviation, defense systems, and space exploration, often specializing in areas such as structural design, guidance, navigation and control, instrumentation and communication, or production methods. They also may specialize in a particular type of aerospace product, such as commercial transports, military fighter jets, helicopters, spacecraft, or missiles and rockets. Aerospace engineers may become experts in aerodynamics, thermodynamics, celestial mechanics, propulsion, acoustics, or guidance and control systems.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: First-year applicants to Penn State must submit the following for admission: an application (MyPennState or Common App), the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR), and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional through the Fall 2025 semester. High school unit requirements include: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a World Language.
Description: African American Studies is a multidisciplinary field of study that explores the experiences of people of African descent in the United States and throughout the African Diaspora. The Department of African American Studies offers a major and a minor in African American Studies. The major is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the history, culture, and social and political experiences of African Americans, and of the historical and contemporary relationships between African Americans and other people of African descent. The department's faculty members represent a wide range of disciplines, including history, literature, sociology, political science, and the arts. The major in African American Studies is an excellent foundation for careers in a variety of fields, including education, law, social work, public policy, and the arts. It also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in African American Studies or in any of the disciplines represented by the department's faculty.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the African Studies major, a student must: have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. For the Bachelor of Arts degree in African Studies, a minimum of 123 credits is required, 24 of which must be at the 400 level.
Description: The African Studies major is a multidisciplinary program that provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the African continent and its diverse peoples, cultures, and histories. Students explore the complexities of Africa's past and present through various perspectives, including history, political science, sociology, literature, and the arts. The program is designed to develop students' critical thinking, analytical, and cross-cultural communication skills. Graduates are prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including international development, diplomacy, education, law, public service, and business, as well as for advanced graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness Management
Requirements: Entrance to the Agribusiness Management major requires a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 and the completion of at least 29.1 credits. For first-year admission, applicants must meet the following high school unit requirements: four units of English, three units of mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), three units of science, three units of social studies, and two units of a single world language. Applicants must submit a high school transcript or Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: Agribusiness Management (AGBM) is a management and business-focused program that applies the principles of economics, business, and management to the food and fiber system. This system includes the industries and organizations involved in the production, processing, distribution, and marketing of food and fiber products. The program provides students with a strong foundation in business and economics, as well as an understanding of the unique characteristics of the food and fiber system. Students learn how to apply economic and management principles to address the challenges facing the food and fiber system, such as food safety, environmental sustainability, and international trade. The program also offers students the opportunity to participate in internships and other experiential learning activities to gain practical experience in the industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biorenewable Systems Management
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average. The first two years of the program are designed to provide a sound foundation in the mathematical, physical, and biological sciences. During the third and fourth years, students complete the core requirements and select technical electives in their areas of interest. General undergraduate admission requires a completed application and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: The Agricultural and Biorenewable Systems Management (ABSM) major provides students with a solid foundation in the physical and biological sciences and the application of those sciences to management and business in the agricultural and biorenewable systems industries. Students are prepared to solve problems in the production, processing, and marketing of agricultural and biorenewable products. The curriculum is flexible and allows students to choose from a wide variety of technical electives and business courses to tailor the program to their individual interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Extension Education
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Agricultural and Extension Education major, students must: 1. have completed at least 29 credits; 2. have a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.00; 3. have completed ENGL 15 or ENGL 30; 4. have completed 3 credits of Mathematics (GQ).
Concentration: Agricultural Education Option; Leadership and Civic Engagement Option
Description: The Agricultural and Extension Education major is a multidisciplinary program of study that prepares students for careers in formal and non-formal agricultural education. Students in the Agricultural Education option are prepared for teacher certification in agriculture and related areas in Pennsylvania and other states. They also are prepared for careers in the Cooperative Extension Service, agribusiness, and international agriculture. Students in the Leadership and Civic Engagement option are prepared for careers in non-formal education settings such as extension, non-profit organizations, and leadership and management roles in industry. All students in the major are provided with a broad background in the agricultural sciences and their choice of a minor to complement their program of study.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Science
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Agricultural Science major, a student must: 1) have completed at least 29 credits; 2) have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00.
Description: The Agricultural Science major provides a broad-based education in the agricultural sciences. The program of study is developed by the student in consultation with an adviser. Students can use the Agricultural Science major to prepare for a wide variety of careers in agriculture. The flexibility of the major allows students to focus their studies in one or more areas of agricultural science by selecting a minor from the College of Agricultural Sciences or another college. The major also provides a good foundation for students who plan to pursue graduate study in an agricultural discipline. Students are encouraged to participate in internships and other experiential learning opportunities to gain practical experience and to explore career options.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: First-year students are evaluated based on: High school GPA, Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for students applying for admission through the fall 2025 semester, High school courses, Personal statement (optional). For Penn State University Park, the following high school units are required: 4 units of English, 3 units of math, 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of the same world language. For all other campuses, the world language is not required but is recommended.
Description: American Studies is a multidisciplinary program that encourages students to examine American culture and society from several perspectives. Students learn to integrate insights from history, literature, the arts, the social sciences, and other fields to understand the American experience in all its complexity. The program offers a flexible curriculum that allows students to tailor their studies to their own interests and career goals. Students may choose to focus on a particular period, region, or theme in American history and culture, or they may take a more general approach. American Studies provides students with a solid foundation in critical thinking, research, and communication skills that are valuable in a wide range of careers, including law, business, education, government, and the arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animal Science
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Animal Science major, a student must have completed at least 29.1 credits and have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. First-year applicants are evaluated on the basis of their high school record, including GPA and rigor of coursework. Penn State is currently test-optional, meaning standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are not required for admission but may be submitted if the applicant chooses.
Concentration: Science, Business/Management, Production/Management
Description: Animal Science is the study of the biology and management of animals. The Animal Science major is a science-based program that prepares students for careers in the animal and allied industries. It provides students with a broad knowledge of animal biology, management, and production. The curriculum includes courses in genetics, nutrition, physiology, reproduction, and animal behavior. Students can choose from three options: Business/Management, Science, and Production/Management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropological Science
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Anthropological Science major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average; 2. complete ANTH 21 GN(4) and ANTH 45(3) with a grade of C or better.
Description: Anthropology is the study of humans and our ancestors through time and across the world. It is a broad field that encompasses the biological, social, and cultural aspects of human life. The Bachelor of Science in Anthropological Science is designed for students who are interested in the application of scientific methods and perspectives to the study of human biological and cultural diversity, evolution, and the archaeological record. Students in this major gain a strong foundation in the natural and social sciences, and develop skills in data analysis, laboratory methods, and field research. The program prepares students for graduate study in anthropology or related fields, as well as for careers in a variety of sectors including health, forensics, cultural resource management, and international development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Anthropology major, a student must: 1. have completed at least 29.5 cumulative credits; 2. have a cumulative grade point average of at least 2.00.
Description: Anthropology is a multifaceted discipline that explores the diversity of human life across time and space. Anthropologists study the origins and evolution of our species, the development of human societies, and the richness of contemporary cultures. By integrating perspectives from the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities, anthropology provides a holistic understanding of what it means to be human. The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology offers a broad-based education in the major subfields of the discipline: archaeology, biological anthropology, and cultural anthropology. Students develop critical thinking skills, cross-cultural awareness, and a deep appreciation for human diversity. This program prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as international development, cultural resource management, public health, education, and business, as well as for graduate study in anthropology and related disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, applicants must submit the Penn State application or the Common App, and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional for first-year students applying through the 2025-26 academic year. For entrance to the Anthropology BS major, students must have completed at least 29 credits with a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00.
Concentration: Archaeology Option; Biological Anthropology Option; Cultural Anthropology Option
Description: The B.S. degree in Anthropology provides a strong foundation in the four subfields of anthropology (archaeology, biological anthropology, cultural anthropology, and linguistics) and also provides students with the opportunity to gain more in-depth training in the analytical and quantitative methods used in anthropology. The B.S. degree offers three options: Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, and Cultural Anthropology. All options provide students with a solid background in the theories and methods that anthropologists use to understand humans and our ancestors. The B.S. degree is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in a field that requires a strong background in science and mathematics, such as forensic science, medicine, or public health, or for students who are interested in pursuing a graduate degree in anthropology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architectural Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Architectural Engineering major, a student must satisfy the following requirements: 1. Be enrolled in the College of Engineering or the Division of Undergraduate Studies. 2. Have completed at least 29 graded Penn State credits. 3. Have completed with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211. 4. Have earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.60.
Concentration: Construction, Lighting/Electrical, Mechanical, or Structural
Description: Architectural engineering focuses on the scientific and engineering aspects of planning, designing, and constructing buildings. The Penn State Architectural Engineering (AE) program is one of the oldest and most respected AE programs in the world. It provides students with a unique combination of broad professional education and specialized skills. Students choose one of four areas of specialization: construction, lighting/electrical, mechanical, or structural. The curriculum is designed to provide a solid foundation in mathematics and the physical sciences, while also developing an understanding of the relationship between architecture and engineering. The program is a five-year program, leading to a Bachelor of Architectural Engineering (B.A.E.) degree.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Architectural Engineering in Architectural Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Architectural and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Architecture in Architecture
Requirements: Admission to the professional B.Arch. degree program is based on high school rank and SAT (or ACT) scores. High school students apply during their senior year for admission into the five-year B.Arch. program. There is no portfolio review for admission to the first-year of the B.Arch. program. Transfer students apply to the department for admission to the program after they have applied to Penn State. The admissions procedure for transfer students into the Architecture program is based on a review of the student's college records and a portfolio of creative work.
Description: The Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.) degree program is a five-year, NAAB-accredited professional degree. The core of the program is the design studio, where students learn to integrate the complex variety of factors that must be considered in the design of buildings and the built environment. The curriculum also includes courses in architectural history, theory, technology, and professional practice. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in the art and science of architecture, preparing them for leadership in the profession. Architecture students at Penn State have access to state-of-the-art facilities, including design studios, fabrication labs, and computer labs, as well as opportunities for study abroad and internships.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.) is a five-year professional degree program accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Architecture
Requirements: Admissions requirements for the Architecture major are listed on the Undergraduate Admissions website. To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Architecture, students must have a minimum of a high school diploma and meet the following high school unit requirements: 4 units of English, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Math (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), and 2 units of a single world language. Applicants to the architecture program are not required to submit a portfolio of work.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S. in Arch.) program is a four-year pre-professional program. The program is intended to be a broad-based, pre-professional degree that allows students to continue in a variety of graduate-level professional programs (architecture, landscape architecture, urban design, etc.) or enter into many other related fields (graphics, real estate development, construction, etc.). The program is flexible and allows students to choose from a wide variety of elective courses in architectural and other topics throughout the university. The program provides the foundational skills and concepts of architecture within a broader liberal arts context. Because it is a four-year, pre-professional degree, this degree does not lead to professional licensure as an architect. Students who wish to pursue professional licensure must pursue an accredited professional degree (a five-year B.Arch. or a 2- or 3-year M.Arch.). Architecture is a multi-disciplinary field that requires students to be proficient in many areas, and the curriculum is designed to reflect this complexity. The core of the program is the design studio, where students learn how to apply the knowledge from their other courses into a comprehensive design project. Studio projects are based on the integration of history, theory, building technology, and representation, and range from small-scale buildings to complex urban environments.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Architecture is a pre-professional degree and is not an accredited professional degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Art (B.A.) major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed at least 24 credits. First-year students are admitted to the College of Arts and Architecture and typically apply for entrance to the major during their sophomore year. A portfolio is not required for admission to the B.A. in Art. Penn State is test-optional through the fall 2025 semester; first-year applicants can choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree in Art is a liberal arts-oriented program that provides a broad foundation in the studio arts, art history, and general education. It is designed for students who want to study art in the context of a broad-based education. The B.A. degree in Art allows students the flexibility to pursue a minor or second major in another field. Students in the B.A. program work with their advisers to select a program of study that meets their individual interests and goals.
Accredidation: The School of Visual Arts is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Requirements: The B.F.A. in Art is a professional degree program that requires a portfolio review for admission. Portfolios are reviewed once each semester by a committee of the Art faculty. To be eligible for the portfolio review, students must have completed or be currently enrolled in ART 110, ART 111, ART 122Y, and ART 201 or ART 202, and have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Concentration: Ceramics, Drawing and Painting, New Media, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture
Description: The B.F.A. degree is a professional degree that focuses on intensive work in the visual arts supported by a program of general studies. This degree is intended to provide a foundation for those students who intend to pursue careers as professional artists or who wish to pursue graduate study in the visual arts (M.F.A.).
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Art Education
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Art Education major, a student must have: attained at least a 3.00 cumulative grade-point average; completed at least 48 collegiate-level credits; completed ENGL 15 or ENGL 30; 3 credits of literature (GH); and 6 credits of quantification (GQ); passed the PAPA or CORE exams or had them waived by qualifying SAT/ACT scores; submitted a portfolio of 10-12 pieces of original work for review by the Art Education faculty; participated in a personal interview with the Art Education faculty; submitted a one-page, typed statement of their professional goals.
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Art Education (A ED) provides students with the required courses and experiences to qualify for the Pennsylvania Instructional I certificate for Art (PK-12). This program prepares students for positions as art teachers in public and private schools, and for work in other educational settings, such as museums and community centers. The curriculum includes courses in art education, studio art, art history, and general education, as well as clinical experiences in schools.
Accredidation: The Art Education program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). The teacher education program is approved by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. The Pennsylvania State University is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History
Requirements: Admission to the Art History major is based on the university’s standard undergraduate admission requirements. To be eligible for entrance to the Art History major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; and 2) satisfy any other requirements that may be established by the academic department. Standardized test scores are optional for first-year undergraduate applicants through the 2025-2026 academic year. Required high school coursework includes 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Art History is a program designed to give students a broad knowledge of the history of art in various parts of the world. It provides training in the skills of visual analysis and interpretation of the meanings of works of art and architecture in their historical and cultural contexts. The major provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue careers in museums, galleries, art publishing, and other art-related fields, as well as for those who intend to go on to graduate study in Art History or related disciplines. Many students also find Art History an excellent liberal arts major that prepares them for a variety of professions, including law, business, and education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Asian Studies major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) be enrolled in or have completed at least 24 credits. Admissions to all undergraduate programs are processed by the Undergraduate Admissions Office. First-year and transfer students may apply for admission to the College of the Liberal Arts. For a Bachelor of Arts degree in Asian Studies, a minimum of 123 credits is required.
Concentration: Asian Studies; Global Asia
Description: Asian Studies is an interdisciplinary major that provides students with a broad knowledge of the history, cultures, and languages of Asia. The program is designed to give students a deep understanding of the diverse societies of Asia and the ability to analyze the region from a variety of perspectives. Students can choose from two options: Asian Studies or Global Asia.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Astronomy and Astrophysics
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and 2) satisfy the following course requirements: ASTRO 291, MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211. For first-year admission, applicants to the Eberly College of Science must have completed the following high school units: 4 units of English, 3.5 units of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language.
Concentration: Astronomy and Astrophysics Option, Computer Science Option, Graduate Study Option
Description: Astronomy is the study of the universe and its constituent parts, including stars, planets, and galaxies. Astrophysics is the application of the laws of physics and the techniques of mathematics to the study of the universe and its contents. The Astronomy and Astrophysics major provides a strong foundation in physics and mathematics, and a comprehensive program of study in the concepts and techniques of modern astronomy and astrophysics. The curriculum includes courses in observational astronomy, planetary science, stellar and galactic astrophysics, and cosmology. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research projects and to gain experience with astronomical instrumentation and data analysis.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biobehavioral Health
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Biobehavioral Health major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. have completed BBH 101 with a grade of C or better.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Biobehavioral Health major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the integration of biological, behavioral, psychological, socio-cultural, and environmental factors as they cross-cut and influence health and disease. Students examine the scientific study of the fundamental physiological, behavioral, and environmental mechanisms that affect health across the life span. This program is designed for students interested in health-related careers in research, clinical practice, public health, health promotion, and human services. Biobehavioral Health (BBH) offers students a broad perspective on health and disease, including physiological, psychological, and social factors. Students develop a strong foundation in the life sciences and social sciences, as well as the specialized skills needed to address complex health issues from a multidisciplinary perspective. The program prepares students for graduate study in the health and behavioral sciences, as well as for entry-level positions in health research and health-related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Requirements: First-year applicants to Penn State must submit a completed application and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). High school unit requirements include: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a World Language. For the Eberly College of Science, additional emphasis is placed on math and science performance. Applicants can choose to submit SAT or ACT scores, but Penn State is test-optional through 2025.
Concentration: Biochemistry Option, Molecular and Cell Biology Option
Description: Biochemistry and Molecular Biology is the study of the molecular basis of life. That is, biochemistry uses the concepts and terminology of chemistry to describe the structure, organization, and functions of living matter in molecular terms. Molecular biology is the study of the molecular basis of gene structure and function. The Biochemistry and Molecular Biology major is a program that allows students to focus on these two areas. The major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the chemical and physical sciences, and then to build on that foundation with specialized coursework in biochemistry, molecular biology, and related fields. Students in the BMB major also have the opportunity to participate in research, which provides them with hands-on experience in the laboratory and the chance to contribute to the advancement of scientific knowledge. Graduates of the BMB major are well-prepared for a variety of careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and other related fields. They are also well-prepared for graduate study in biochemistry, molecular biology, and other related fields.
Accredidation: The Biochemistry and Molecular Biology program at University Park is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: pass the following courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211; have completed at least 29 earned Penn State credits (excludes transfer and AP credits); have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.60.
Department: College of Agricultural Sciences and College of Engineering
Concentration: Agricultural Engineering Option, Food and Biological Process Engineering Option, Natural Resources Engineering Option
Description: Biological Engineering is a versatile and diverse engineering major that integrates the engineering sciences with biology to design, develop, and manage biological systems for sustainable production and use of energy, food, fiber, and other natural resources. Graduates apply engineering principles to the design of processes, machines, and structures that improve the efficiency and quality of biological production and processing while protecting the environment and natural resources. The program provides a broad foundation in basic sciences and engineering, which prepares students for careers in the private and public sectors as well as for graduate study. Students can choose from three options: Agricultural Engineering, Food and Biological Process Engineering, or Natural Resources Engineering. Each option allows students to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Biological Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Biological and Similarly Named Engineering Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biology
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Biology major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed BIOL 110 GN(4), CHEM 110 GN(3), and MATH 140 GQ(4) with a grade of C or better. Undergraduate admission also requires the completion of specific high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of social studies, 3 units of science, 3 units of math (algebra, geometry, trigonometry, or higher), and 2 units of a single world language.
Concentration: Ecology Option, General Biology Option, Genetics and Developmental Biology Option, Neuroscience Option, Plant Biology Option, and Vertebrate Physiology Option
Description: The Biology major provides students with a broad background in modern biology. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for admission to graduate school or professional schools of medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, or other health-related fields. It also prepares students for careers in research, industry, government, or secondary education. The Biology major offers six options: Ecology Option, General Biology Option, Genetics and Developmental Biology Option, Neuroscience Option, Plant Biology Option, and Vertebrate Physiology Option. These options allow students to specialize in their areas of interest while ensuring a strong foundation in the biological sciences and the supporting fields of chemistry, physics, and mathematics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: For the B.S. degree in Biomedical Engineering, a minimum of 129 credits is required. Entry to the Biomedical Engineering major occurs during the spring semester of the sophomore year. Students must complete the following entrance-to-major requirements: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211 with a grade of C or better. At least a 3.00 cumulative Penn State grade-point average is required. High school students should have a minimum of 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of science, and 3 units of social studies/art/humanities.
Concentration: Biochemical Option, Biomaterials Option, Biomechanics Option, Medical Imaging and Devices Option
Description: Biomedical Engineering is a multi-disciplinary field that combines engineering principles with biological sciences and clinical practice to improve human health. It is one of the fastest growing fields in engineering today. Graduates of our program are well-prepared to work in the medical device industry, pharmaceutical companies, and biotechnology firms, or to pursue further studies in graduate school, medical school, or other professional programs. The Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering at Penn State is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of engineering, biology, and chemistry. Students then build on this foundation through a series of core courses and specialized electives in areas such as biomaterials, biomechanics, medical imaging, and tissue engineering. The program also emphasizes hands-on learning through laboratory experiences and a senior design project, where students work in teams to solve real-world problems in biomedical engineering.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Bioengineering and Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biorenewable Systems
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Biorenewable Systems major, a student must have: 1) attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average.
Concentration: Agricultural Systems Management, Bioproducts
Description: This major is designed for students who want to apply their interest in business and technology to the sustainable management of agricultural and biological systems. The curriculum is a blend of technology, business, and natural sciences. The program prepares students for careers in the management of systems related to food, agriculture, and bio-based products. Students can choose between two options: Agricultural Systems Management or Bioproducts. The Agricultural Systems Management option focuses on the technology and management of systems in food and agriculture. The Bioproducts option focuses on the processing and marketing of bio-based materials and products. Graduates are prepared for careers in production management, sales and marketing, technical services, and systems management with a variety of industries and government agencies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology
Requirements: For entrance into the Biotechnology major, there are no additional requirements beyond those for admission to the University. The first-year admission process is based on a variety of factors, including high school grades and coursework, standardized test scores (SAT/ACT), and other information provided in the application. For transfer students, applicants who have completed at least 18 credits may be considered for admission.
Concentration: General Biotechnology Option, Genetics and Developmental Biology Option, Microbial Biotechnology Option, Molecular Biology and Biochemistry Option, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology Option
Description: Biotechnology is a field of applied biology that uses living organisms or their components to create or modify products or processes for specific use. The major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the biological and chemical sciences and to prepare them for careers in the biotechnology industry, research, and development. The curriculum emphasizes the application of molecular and cellular biology, genetics, and biochemistry to solve problems in areas such as human health, agriculture, and the environment. Students can choose from five options to customize their education: General Biotechnology, Genetics and Developmental Biology, Microbial Biotechnology, Molecular Biology and Biochemistry, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology. All students in the major complete a core of courses in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics, and then take specialized courses in their chosen option. Many students also participate in research projects or internships to gain hands-on experience in the field.
Accredidation: The Molecular Biology and Biochemistry option is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB).
ScholarshipType: Academic achievement, financial need, and/or diversity

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Business major, a student must: 1) have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better: MATH 110 GQ(3) or MATH 140 GQ(4), ACCTG 211(4), ECON 102 GS(3), SCM 200 GQ(4) or STAT 200 GQ(4); 2) have achieved a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Concentration: Accounting, Business Analytics, Entrepreneurship, Financial Services, Health Services, Individualized, Management and Marketing, Supply Chain Management
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Business (BSB) is a professionally oriented business degree program that combines the core business disciplines of management, marketing, finance, and supply chain management with applied study in a practical setting. Through the choice of a formal 18-credit option, students can specialize in a specific business area. The degree’s interdisciplinary focus helps to prepare students for a variety of careers in business and government, or for graduate study. The BSB program at Penn State Abington, Penn State Altoona, Penn State Berks, Penn State Brandywine, Penn State DuBois, Penn State Fayette, Penn State Greater Allegheny, Penn State Harrisburg, Penn State Hazleton, Penn State Lehigh Valley, Penn State Mont Alto, Penn State New Kensington, Penn State Schuylkill, Penn State Scranton, Penn State Shenango, Penn State Wilkes-Barre, Penn State York, and World Campus offers concentrations in accounting, business analytics, entrepreneurship, financial services, health services, individualized, management and marketing, and supply chain management. Students develop skills in reporting and explaining financial data, creating marketing plan, implementing growth strategies, managing supply chains, and evaluating the ethical and professional responsibilities of business and organizations.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Business (BSB) program is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Chemical Engineering major, a student must: 1) have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better in each: CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211; 2) have achieved a cumulative grade-point average (GPA) of 2.60 or higher.
Concentration: Bioengineering Option
Description: Chemical engineering is the study and practice of transforming matter and energy into forms that are useful to society. Particular attention is given to chemical as well as physical processes and to the process of scaling up from the laboratory to the industrial plant. The chemical engineering profession has its foundations in the mathematics, physics, and chemistry that are common to all engineering. But its distinctiveness derives from the study of the separation and analysis of complex mixtures and of chemical reactions. These involve not only the kinetics of the reaction, but also the challenges of heat and mass transfer, and fluid mechanics. Chemical engineering is a diverse field that has an impact on most of the things we use in our daily lives. Chemical engineers are involved in the manufacture of everything from paper and plastics to pharmaceutical products and microelectronics. They help to protect the environment and work to find new sources of energy. They work in a variety of industries, including petroleum, chemical, pharmaceutical, food, and nuclear. Chemical engineering is an exciting and challenging field that offers a wide range of career opportunities.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Chemical, Biochemical, Biomolecular and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; completed CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, MATH 140, and MATH 141 and earned a grade of C or better in each of these courses. General high school requirements for Penn State include: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a World Language.
Concentration: Analytical, Biological, Environmental, Materials, or Physical
Description: Chemistry is the study of the structure and composition of matter and the changes that matter undergoes. These changes are studied by monitoring and measuring the physical properties of substances and by observing the interaction of different types of matter. All other sciences have their roots in chemistry. The Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry is the appropriate program for students who are planning for careers in the chemical industry or in government laboratories, or for graduate study in chemistry. The program is accredited by the American Chemical Society. All students in the Bachelor of Science program take the same core courses in general, analytical, organic, physical, and inorganic chemistry, as well as in physics and mathematics. In addition to these core courses, each student chooses one of five options: Analytical, Biological, Environmental, Materials, or Physical.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the American Chemical Society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Chinese major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed CHNS 1, CHNS 2, and CHNS 3 or equivalent. For the B.A. degree in Chinese, a minimum of 123 credits is required. For more information about the admission process, students should visit the Office of Undergraduate Admissions website.
Description: The Chinese major is designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in Chinese language and culture. Students will achieve a high level of proficiency in the Chinese language (Mandarin) and develop a deep understanding of Chinese literature, culture, and society. They will learn to communicate effectively in Chinese and analyze Chinese texts and cultural products from a variety of historical and contemporary perspectives. The major also prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, government, business, and international relations, as well as for further study in graduate or professional school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Civil Engineering major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.60 cumulative grade-point average; completed the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211. Students must apply for entrance to the major during the semester in which they are completing their entrance-to-major requirements, typically the spring of the sophomore year.
Description: Civil engineering is the oldest and broadest of the engineering professions. It focuses on the built environment and its impact on the natural environment. Civil engineers are responsible for the planning, design, construction, and operation of the infrastructure that supports modern society. This infrastructure includes buildings, bridges, highways, airports, railways, tunnels, dams, canals, water supply systems, and wastewater treatment plants. Civil engineers also play a key role in protecting the environment by developing sustainable solutions for waste management, pollution control, and resource conservation. The mission of the Civil Engineering program is to provide students with a high-quality education that prepares them for a successful career in the civil engineering profession. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the physical sciences and mathematics, as well as the engineering sciences and design. Students also have the opportunity to specialize in one or more of the following areas: environmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, transportation engineering, and water resources engineering.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Civil and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria. The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering at Penn State Harrisburg is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Civil and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. First-year students who wish to start at University Park are admitted to the DUS (Division of Undergraduate Studies) or to the College of the Liberal Arts. Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies requires only that students are admitted to the College of the Liberal Arts and meet the criteria for entrance to the major.
Concentration: Ancient Languages Option; Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies Option
Description: The Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies (CAMS) major is an interdisciplinary program of study. It is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible, yet also rigorous, background in the history, literature, archaeology, and languages of the Mediterranean world from the earliest civilizations through the end of antiquity. The focus of the program is on the development of the several civilizations and diverse cultures of the ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece, and Rome, as well as on their influence on later civilizations and cultures. Students can pursue several different options within the major. The Ancient Languages option provides students with the linguistic training necessary to read the literature and documents of the ancient world in their original languages, and is particularly designed for students who are planning for graduate study in the field or in a related discipline. The CAMS option provides students with a broader range of study in ancient Mediterranean history, archaeology, and literature in translation, and allows for greater concentration in one or more of these areas. In either option, the primary goals of the major are for students to learn how to analyze and evaluate different types of evidence and how to integrate that evidence into a coherent understanding of the societies that produced it.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Arts and Sciences
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Communication Arts and Sciences major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. 2) have completed CAS 101 with a grade of C or better. 3) have completed CAS 201 or CAS 202 with a grade of C or better.
Description: Communication Arts and Sciences (CAS) is a discipline that dates back to the ancient Greeks and Romans, who studied the art of rhetoric to participate in the democratic life of their era. Today, CAS students study how people use symbols, spoken and written, to shape their world. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in the history and theory of communication and offers a wide range of courses in areas such as interpersonal communication, organizational communication, public speaking, rhetoric, and social influence. Students learn to analyze and evaluate communication in various contexts and to develop their own communication skills to become effective and ethical communicators in their personal, professional, and civic lives.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Arts and Sciences
Requirements: Admission to the Communication Arts and Sciences major (CAS) is available to any student who has been admitted to the University and who is in good standing. Entering students are typically admitted to the College of the Liberal Arts and then apply for the CAS major during their sophomore year when they have completed 29 credits and earned a 2.0 or higher cumulative GPA. In addition to a cumulative 2.0 GPA, students must have completed CAS 101.
Description: The Communication Arts and Sciences (CAS) major is for students who want to understand the role of communication in their personal, professional, and civic lives. CAS students study the theories and practice of communication. Through their coursework, students learn how people communicate in different contexts (such as in personal relationships, in groups and organizations, and across cultures) and via different media (such as face-to-face and via digital platforms). They also learn how to create and analyze messages, solve communication problems, and use communication to promote positive change. The B.S. degree focuses on the social and psychological processes of communication and the systematic study of communication in various contexts. The B.S. degree requires students to complete a minor or a second major in another field of study. Because the B.S. degree focuses on scientific and social scientific research, it is well suited for students who want to understand human communication from a scientific or data-driven perspective. Students in the B.S. program also develop skills that are valued by employers, such as public speaking, teamwork, and critical thinking.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Sciences and Disorders
Requirements: First-year students can apply to Penn State through the Undergraduate Admissions Office and can choose Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) as their major on the application. Evaluation for admission is based on a variety of factors, including high school GPA, high school coursework (specifically completion of required high school units), and standardized test scores if the student chooses to submit them. Required high school units include four units of English, three units of mathematics, three units of science, and three units of social studies, arts, or humanities.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD); Deafness and Hearing Studies (DHS)
Description: The undergraduate major in Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) provides students with a broad-based education in the basic physical, biological, and social sciences; the processes of normal and disordered communication; and an introduction to the clinical processes for individuals with communication disorders. Our undergraduate students learn the fundamental science and developmental processes of human communication, including the anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing, acoustics, linguistics, and child development. They also learn about the disorders that can affect communication and the latest techniques for clinical assessment and treatment.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Community, Environment, and Development
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. For general undergraduate admission, applicants must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. Required high school coursework includes 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Concentration: Community and Economic Development Option; Environmental Economics and Policy Option; International Development Option; Social Thought and Change Option
Description: Community, Environment, and Development (CED) is a multidisciplinary major that provides students with the skills and knowledge to understand and solve complex problems at the intersection of communities, the environment, and the economy. The major is designed to help students understand the social, economic, and environmental impacts of development and the processes of change in communities. Students learn to apply the tools of economics and sociology to address real-world challenges, such as sustainable development, land use planning, environmental protection, and community economic development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Comparative Literature major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average. For the B.A. degree in Comparative Literature, a minimum of 120 credits is required.
Description: Comparative Literature is the study of literature and culture across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. By drawing on various languages and cultures, students examine the ways in which literature and other media reflect and shape human experience. The major provides a broad, international perspective on literature and culture, while also allowing students to focus on specific areas of interest. Students develop skills in critical thinking, writing, and analysis, as well as proficiency in at least one foreign language. The program prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, publishing, international relations, and business, as well as for graduate study in literature, cultural studies, and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for first-year admission to Penn State, applicants must provide their high school records (official transcripts or Self-Reported Academic Record). General high school unit requirements include 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, and 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities. For the Computer Engineering program in the College of Engineering, a minimum of 1/2 unit of trigonometry or higher-level math is specifically required. Penn State is currently test-optional through the Fall 2025 semester.
Description: Computer engineering is the study of the design, analysis, and implementation of computer systems. Computer engineering is a balanced study of both hardware and software. The computer engineering curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in mathematics, physics, and computer science. In addition, it provides the student with specialized knowledge in computer hardware, software, and systems. Students learn about digital logic, computer architecture, operating systems, networking, and software engineering. They also gain practical experience through laboratory courses and a senior design project.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Computer Engineering Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Computer Science major, a student must: have completed MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and CMPSC 121 or CMPSC 131 with a grade of C or better; have earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average. General first-year admission requires high school graduation or GED, and the completion of specific high school units including 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of World Language.
Description: Computer science is the study of the theoretical foundations of information and computation and their implementation and application in computer systems. Computer science is a broad discipline that encompasses many areas such as: algorithms, data structures, programming languages, software engineering, computer architecture, operating systems, database systems, artificial intelligence, computer graphics, and computer networks. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in computer science and to prepare them for careers in the computer industry or for graduate study. The program includes a core of computer science courses, as well as courses in mathematics, statistics, and the natural sciences. Students also complete a capstone design project that provides experience in the design and implementation of a large-scale software system.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science at University Park is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Computer Science Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Computer Science major, students must: 1. Have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: CMPSC 121 or CMPSC 131, CMPSC 122 or CMPSC 132, MATH 140, MATH 141. 2. Have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher. General first-year admission requirements include the completion of the following high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language.
Department: School of Science, Engineering, and Technology
Description:
The B.A. in Computer Science provides students with a strong foundation in Computer Science and also permits students to explore another area of study through a minor or a group of courses in another department. Students who choose this major are prepared for a career in software development, but their coursework also provides a background for other careers, such as technical writing or positions that require both computer science and another area of expertise.

What is Computer Science?
Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. It is a broad field that covers everything from the theoretical study of algorithms to the practical challenges of implementing them in hardware and software. Computer science is a vital part of our modern world, and it is used in everything from our smartphones to our cars to our medical devices.

You Might Like This Program If...
- You are interested in computer science but also want to explore other areas of study.
- You plan to pursue a career in a field that requires a combination of technical skills and a broad understanding of the world.
- You want to work in a variety of industries, including software development, data analysis, and web development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Requirements: Entrance to the Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship major is competitive and based on specific criteria including successful completion of administrative requirements, credit count, grade-point average, and specific courses. To be eligible for entrance to the Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship major, students must: (1) have completed at least 44 cumulative credits at Penn State but not more than 59 cumulative credits at Penn State (this includes current-semester credits in progress) at the time of application for entrance to the major; (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of 3.20 or higher; (3) have completed the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H, FIN 301, MATH 110 or MATH 140, MGMT 301, MKTG 301, SCM 301, and STAT 200.
Description: The Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE) major is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to lead innovation and create new business opportunities within existing corporations (corporate innovation) and to start new ventures (entrepreneurship). The major provides a broad-based education in business, with a focus on identifying and evaluating opportunities, developing business models, and leading innovation projects. Students learn how to manage the innovation process, from ideation to implementation, and how to create a culture of innovation within organizations. The CIE major prepares students for careers as innovation managers, product managers, business development managers, and entrepreneurs.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Creative Writing
Requirements: To be considered for first-year admission to Penn State, applicants must have completed a minimum of 15 high school units, including: 4 units of English (including 1 unit of composition or rhetoric), 3 units of mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and a second year of algebra), 3 units of science (including 2 units of natural science), 3 units of social studies (including 1 unit of world history or geography), and 2 units of the same world language. Additionally, to be eligible for entrance to the Creative Writing major, a student must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and completed at least 29.1 credits. The B.F.A. in Creative Writing requires a total of 120 credits for graduation. Penn State is test-optional through Fall 2025.
Concentration: poetry, fiction, nonfiction, or playwriting
Description: Writing is a passion. It’s a craft. And it can be a career. If you want to develop your voice as a writer, explore a variety of genres, and gain professional experience in the publishing industry, the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Creative Writing at Penn State Behrend is for you. The B.F.A. in Creative Writing is a professional degree that focuses on the craft of writing. You will work in a small-group workshop environment with published authors and gain hands-on experience by working on the staff of Lake Effect, our international literary journal, or with the Smith Visiting Writers Series, which brings distinguished writers to campus for readings and master classes. You’ll choose to focus your studies in poetry, fiction, nonfiction, or playwriting. Penn State Behrend has a vibrant and supportive creative writing community. You will work with faculty members who are themselves published, award-winning authors, and you’ll have the opportunity to participate in workshops and master classes with writers who have attained national and international acclaim.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Criminology
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Criminology major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; (2) have achieved at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; (3) have completed CRIM 100(3), SOC 110(3) or STAT 200(4), and one of the following: CRIM 249(3), CRIM 250W(3), or CRIM 406(3), all with a grade of C or better.
Description: The Criminology major is designed to provide students with an understanding of the causes of crime, the role of law in society, and the criminal justice system. The program is based in the social sciences and emphasizes the use of research and theory to understand crime and justice. Students learn about the nature and causes of crime, the behavior of criminals, and how the legal system and other social institutions respond to crime. The curriculum provides a foundation for students interested in careers in the criminal justice system, social services, law, or research, as well as for students planning to pursue graduate study in criminology, sociology, law, or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminology
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Criminology major (CRIMB_BS), a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average. For general undergraduate admission to Penn State, applicants must provide a completed application, the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR), and meet high school unit requirements including 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Description: The B.S. degree in Criminology is intended for students who have an interest in studying crime and the criminal justice system from a social science perspective. The curriculum focuses on both the development and application of knowledge and skills related to criminology. Students take a core of criminology and criminal justice courses, and then select from a wide range of elective courses in criminology and other disciplines. The B.S. degree is designed for students who want a more mathematically and scientifically oriented program of study than is provided by the B.A. degree in Criminology. The curriculum includes more requirements in the areas of research methods, statistics, and science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations major, students must satisfy the following requirements: 1. Attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. 2. Complete the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: MATH 110 GQ or MATH 140 GQ; IST 210, IST 220, IST 242 (or CMPSC 122 or CMPSC 132), and STAT 200 GQ or SCM 200 GQ.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Description: The Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations (CYAOP) major is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers as cybersecurity professionals. The program provides students with a solid foundation in the technical, legal, and social aspects of cybersecurity, and focuses on the development of skills needed to analyze, protect, and defend computer systems and networks. Students will learn how to identify and mitigate cyber threats, perform forensic investigations, and develop and implement cybersecurity policies and procedures. The program also emphasizes the importance of ethics and professional responsibility in the field of cybersecurity. Cybersecurity analytics and operations is a field that involves the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data to support the detection, prevention, and response to cyber threats. It involves the use of specialized tools and techniques to analyze network traffic, system logs, and other sources of data to identify patterns and anomalies that may indicate a cyber attack. Cybersecurity professionals in this field also work to develop and implement strategies to protect an organization's computer systems and networks from cyber threats, and to respond to and recover from cyber attacks when they occur.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations at University Park, Altoona, Beaver, Berks, Brandywine, Greater Allegheny, Harrisburg, Lehigh Valley, Schuylkill, Scranton, World Campus, and York is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Cybersecurity Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Sciences
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Data Sciences, first-year applicants must submit an online application (via MyPennState or the Common App) and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Penn State is test-optional through 2025, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required for admission. The most important factor in the review of an application is the high school academic record, specifically grades and course rigor.
Department: College of Engineering, College of Information Sciences and Technology, and Eberly College of Science
Concentration: Applied Data Sciences, Computational Data Sciences, Statistical Modeling Data Sciences
Description: Data Science is the field of study that focuses on the lifecycle of data, including data acquisition, data management, data analysis, and data communication. Data scientists use a variety of tools and techniques from computer science, statistics, and mathematics to extract insights from data and to solve complex problems. The Data Sciences major is an interdisciplinary undergraduate degree program spanning the College of Information Sciences and Technology, the College of Engineering, and the Eberly College of Science. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the computational and statistical aspects of data science, while also allowing them to specialize in a particular application domain. Students will learn how to manage, analyze, and visualize large and complex datasets, and will gain experience in using data science to solve real-world problems.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Design in Digital Arts and Media Design
Requirements: Entrance to the Digital Arts and Media Design (DART) major is a two-step process. Step 1: All students must first apply to the university through the Penn State Undergraduate Admissions Office. Step 2: Applicants must also complete a portfolio review for the Digital Arts and Media Design major. Information regarding the portfolio review process and deadlines is available on the program's website. For the B.Des. degree in Digital Arts and Media Design, a minimum of 120 credits is required.
Description: The Digital Arts and Media Design program is for students who want to become creative leaders in fields such as interactive media, games as art and design, and the digital arts. It is a four-year professional degree leading to a Bachelor of Design (B.Des.). The program is a vibrant community of creative practice and research across several Penn State units, providing students with unique access to faculty and facilities for cross-disciplinary study and experimentation. Students engage in the design and creation of expressive, meaningful, and purposeful digital media experiences for humans and with computers. They learn to be versatile and adaptable as technology and culture change around them. Digital Arts and Media Design students are encouraged to seek and develop their own paths through the program based on their specific goals and interests. The curriculum is flexible, with numerous electives and choices throughout the four years.
