This allows students to take advantage of the breadth of digital media offerings at the University while developing depth in areas of their choosing. Graduates are prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including entertainment, education, advertising, and the arts, or for further study in graduate school.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Design in Digital Arts and Media Design (B.Des.) is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Design in Digital Multimedia Design
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Design in Digital Multimedia Design, students must meet the general University admission requirements, which include a high school diploma or equivalent and the completion of specific high school units. This program is available to both first-year and transfer students. Notably, a portfolio review is not required for admission to this major.
Description: The Bachelor of Design (B.Des.) in Digital Multimedia Design is a cross-disciplinary program offered by the College of Arts and Architecture, the Bellisario College of Communications, and the College of Information Sciences and Technology. Digital Multimedia Design (DMD) is a degree that will prepare students to be creative leaders in a variety of digital media professions. Students in DMD will learn the fundamentals of design and the various ways that it relates to creating digital objects, and will then develop higher-level skills in communication and Information Technology (IT) that will allow them to create and manage digital media projects and collaborate with others in these fields. Students will develop skills in collaborative work and critical thinking, which are the foundations of design, and learn to apply these to projects in digital communications, information technology, and media production. They will also learn how to create and curate digital content for multiple platforms, including mobile, web, and social media. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to adapt to the rapidly changing landscape of digital media.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth Science and Policy
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. have completed at least 29.1 credits and be at least a third-semester student. Students must apply for admission to the college by following the procedures described on the Penn State Admissions website.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: Climate Change Option, Energy and Geosciences Option, Water Resources Option
Description: The Earth Science and Policy major is designed for students who want to address environmental problems from an interdisciplinary perspective. The program provides a solid foundation in the Earth sciences—the study of the Earth’s atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere—while also providing a strong background in the social sciences, including policy analysis, economics, and ethics. The Earth Science and Policy major prepares students to address issues such as climate change, energy resources, and water quality and quantity. Students learn to analyze environmental problems, evaluate policy options, and communicate scientific information to diverse audiences. The curriculum is flexible, allowing students to focus on areas of interest such as climate, energy, or water. Graduates are prepared for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector, as well as for graduate study in fields such as environmental science, policy, and law.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth Sciences
Requirements: For the B.S. degree in Earth Sciences, a minimum of 120 credits is required. In order to be eligible for entrance to the Earth Sciences major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: EARTH 100, GEOSC 1, GEOSC 20, or METEO 3. First-year applicants to Penn State must submit: Penn State application, Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR) or high school transcript, and optional SAT or ACT scores.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Earth Sciences is a broadly based major in the geosciences. It is designed to provide students with a broad background in the earth sciences and is especially appropriate for students intending to become secondary school teachers in earth and space sciences. Because of its breadth, it is also a suitable major for students who wish to use the earth sciences as a vehicle for a career in business, law, or public policy. The program is designed to be flexible; it includes no specific concentrations or options, but can be tailored to a student's interests through choosing appropriate selections from the list of Earth Science Electives. Students may focus their Earth Science Electives in a single area, such as geology, or may choose a more diverse set of electives.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to Penn State as a first-year student, you must have graduated from high school or have a GED. The following high school units are required for all students: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (Algebra 1, Algebra 2, and Geometry), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Art/Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language. Admission to the East Asian Studies major is available to students who have been admitted to the College of the Liberal Arts.
Description: The major in East Asian Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, culture, politics, and languages of East Asia (China, Japan, and Korea). The program seeks to prepare students for careers in government, business, and education, as well as for graduate study in East Asian Studies or related fields. Students in the major are required to attain proficiency in an East Asian language and to complete a core of courses in history, literature, and the social sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Economics major, a student must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and completed and earned a grade of C or better in ECON 102 GS(3), ECON 104 GS(3), MATH 110 GQ(4) or MATH 140 GQ(4). For the Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics, a minimum of 120 credits is required.
Description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to employ scarce resources to produce goods and services and to distribute them among various groups and individuals. Economists study such things as the role of prices and markets, the effects of government policies, the causes of unemployment and inflation, the determinants of economic growth, and the distribution of income. The economics major provides students with a solid foundation in economic theory and its applications. It is designed to prepare students for a wide range of careers in business, government, and non-profit organizations, as well as for further study in law, business, and public policy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Economics (ECNBS) major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed and earned a grade of C or better in: ECON 102 GS(3), ECON 104 GS(3), MATH 110 GQ(4) or MATH 140 GQ(4).
Description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to use scarce resources. The B.S. degree in Economics provides students with a strong foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods. It is designed for students who want to develop their analytical skills and apply them to the study of economic issues. The B.S. degree requires more coursework in mathematics and statistics than the B.A. degree, and it is well-suited for students who are interested in pursuing graduate study in economics or related fields, or who want to work in careers that require strong technical and data analysis skills. Learning Outcomes: Students will be able to explain and apply the core models of microeconomics and macroeconomics. Students will be able to use statistical methods and econometric analysis to evaluate economic relationships and test economic theories. Students will be able to communicate economic analysis and research results effectively in written and oral forms.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Electrical Engineering major, a student must: 1. have completed the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, PHYS 212. 2. have attained at least a 2.60 cumulative grade-point average (on a 4.00 scale) and at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits). Additionally, applicants to the College of Engineering must have completed 1/2 unit of trigonometry or higher level math (pre-calculus, calculus) in high school.
Description: Electrical engineering is one of the broadest of all engineering professions. It involves the design and development of modern systems for communication, control, and power. Electrical engineers work with everything from tiny microchips to massive power grids. The mission of the Electrical Engineering program is to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of electrical engineering, together with an understanding of the impact of engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context. Students learn to design, conduct experiments, analyze and interpret data, and function on multidisciplinary teams. The educational objectives of the program are to produce graduates who, within a few years of graduation, are: successful in professional careers as electrical engineers or in related fields; engaging in professional development through graduate study, professional registration, or other means of continuing education; and contributing to the profession and society through leadership and participation in professional organizations.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria. The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering at Penn State Harrisburg is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering Technology
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: 1. Completed the requirements for the Associate in Engineering Technology in Electrical Engineering Technology degree or its equivalent. 2. A minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.00. For the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering Technology degree, a minimum of 127 credits is required.
Description: The Electrical Engineering Technology (EET) program provides graduates with the skills necessary to work as technologists in a variety of industries. The program's goal is to produce graduates who are technically competent, can work effectively in a team, and can communicate their ideas clearly. The curriculum covers areas such as circuit analysis, electronics, digital systems, microprocessors, control systems, and communications. Students also gain hands-on experience through laboratory work and projects. The program prepares graduates for careers in various industries, such as power systems, telecommunications, manufacturing, and electronics design.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering Technology at Penn State Harrisburg is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Program Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical/Electronic(s) Engineering Technology and Similarly Named Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology
Requirements: Entrance to the Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology major requires the completion of at least 29 credits and a minimum 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology (EMET) program provides the curriculum required for students to develop a broad foundation in the areas of electrical and electronic circuits, mechanical systems, microprocessor controls, automation and robotics. This synergy of electrical and mechanical disciplines is particularly appropriate for the modern automated manufacturing and production industry where a single machine or production line is an integrated system of mechanical and electrical components. The EMET program prepares students to apply their knowledge to a wide variety of industrial problems and to be productive from the first day of employment. The program emphasizes the use of industrial equipment and software to prepare students for the workplace. The Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to design, develop, and implement electro-mechanical systems. The program's curriculum includes courses in engineering technology, mathematics, and the physical sciences. Students also have the opportunity to participate in hands-on laboratory experiences and design projects.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology at Penn State Altoona, Penn State Berks, Penn State Fayette, and Penn State New Kensington is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Electromechanical Engineering Technology and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Elementary and Early Childhood Education
Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed undergraduate application and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are currently optional for undergraduate admission. To be formally admitted into the Elementary and Early Childhood Education major, students must meet 'Entrance to Major' requirements, which typically occur after completing 48-60 credits at Penn State. These requirements include a minimum 3.00 cumulative grade-point average and the completion of specific core courses in English and Mathematics.
Concentration: Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 4 (PK-4) Option; Education in Volunteer and Community Settings (EVCS) Option
Description: The Elementary and Early Childhood Education (CEAED) major is a teacher education program for students who wish to work in schools and other educational settings with children from birth through fourth grade. The program prepares students to meet the requirements for the Pennsylvania Instructional I certificate for Pre-Kindergarten-Grade 4 (PK-4). Through the PK-4 Option, students are prepared to teach in preschool and elementary school settings. Through the Education in Volunteer and Community Settings (EVCS) Option, students are prepared to work with children and their families in non-school settings.
Accredidation: The program is approved by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. The College of Education at Penn State is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Energy and Sustainability Policy
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Energy and Sustainability Policy major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed no fewer than 29.1 cumulative credits. General first-year admission requires a high school diploma or equivalent and the completion of required high school units including 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics, 3 years of science, 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of a single world language.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Energy and Sustainability Policy (ESP) program is one of a few online programs in the nation that focuses specifically on policy within the realms of energy and sustainability. As the world’s energy needs continue to increase, so does the demand for professionals who understand the complex variables that influence energy policy and sustainability. The ESP program is designed for students who want to be at the forefront of this transition. The interdisciplinary curriculum provides a strong foundation in the science, technology, policy, and business of energy. Students learn to analyze energy systems, evaluate policy options, and develop strategies for a sustainable future. The program's online delivery makes it accessible to students around the world, and its flexible curriculum allows students to tailor their studies to their interests and career goals. ESP graduates are prepared for careers in a variety of fields, including energy analysis, policy development, sustainability management, and renewable energy development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Energy and Sustainability Policy
Requirements: Incoming first-year students who meet the current Penn State admission criteria will be admitted directly into the major. Penn State undergraduate students may be admitted to the major after they have satisfied the following requirements: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits and (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The B.A. in Energy and Sustainability Policy (ESP) is an online degree program offered through Penn State World Campus. The program is designed for students who seek a career in the rapidly growing fields of energy and sustainability. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing on courses in energy and environmental policy, social sciences, and the humanities. Students in the B.A. program develop a broad understanding of the energy industry and the social, economic, and environmental factors that influence energy policy. The program emphasizes global perspectives and communication skills, and includes a foreign language requirement. Graduates are prepared for a variety of roles in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector, where they can apply their knowledge of policy and sustainability to address complex energy challenges.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Energy Business and Finance
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Energy Business and Finance major, a student must: (1) have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better in each course: ECON 102 GS(3), MATH 140 GQ(4) and (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: General Option, Energy Land Management (ELM) Option
Description: The Energy Business and Finance (EBF) major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the business and social science aspects of the energy and minerals industries. It focuses on the application of economics, finance, and business management to the problems of energy and mineral resource development and use. Students will learn about the science and technology of energy production, and the environmental impacts of energy use, while developing analytical skills in economics, finance, and risk management. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in the energy and minerals industries, financial institutions, and government agencies, as well as for further study in graduate or professional programs.
Accredidation: The Energy Land Management option is accredited by the American Association of Professional Landmen (AAPL).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Energy Engineering
Requirements: For the B.S. degree in Energy Engineering, a student must be granted admission to the major. Entrance to the Energy Engineering major requires that the student has: 1. completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211; 2. earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Energy Engineering is a broad field that encompasses many different energy sources (fossil, solar, wind, and biomass) and various energy industries (electric power, fuel production and processing, and energy policy). The Energy Engineering (ENEG) major is a multidisciplinary program that provides students with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of energy science and engineering. The curriculum includes courses in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and reaction kinetics, as well as specialized courses in renewable energy, fuel processing, and energy systems. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in the energy industry, government agencies, and research institutions, or for further study in graduate school. Students learn to analyze energy systems, evaluate energy resources, and develop sustainable energy solutions.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Energy Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the English major, a student must: 1. have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. have completed ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H with a grade of C or better.
Concentration: Creative Writing; Literature, Criticism, and Culture; Professional and Media Writing; Rhetoric and Composition
Description: The major in English provides students with a program of study in British, American, and Anglophone literatures and cultures, as well as in creative writing, professional writing, and rhetoric and composition. Students in the English major develop the ability to read with precision and to write with clarity and imagination. They study how the English language is used in various historical periods and across different media, and they explore the ways in which literature and other forms of writing reflect and shape cultural values and social structures. The major prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as education, publishing, journalism, law, business, and public service, as well as for graduate study in English and other disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Enterprise Technology Integration
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. For the Bachelor of Science degree in Enterprise Technology Integration, a minimum of 120 credits is required.
Description: The Enterprise Technology Integration (ETI) major is designed to provide students with the theoretical and practical foundations of how to leverage information technology to help organizations achieve their strategic goals. Modern businesses rely on a complex ecosystem of software applications, platforms, and data sources that need to be seamlessly integrated to provide a unified view of the organization's operations. The ETI major equips students with the technical skills and business knowledge needed to design, develop, and manage such integrated systems. The curriculum of the ETI major covers a wide range of topics, including systems integration, database management, cloud computing, enterprise architecture, and business process modeling. Students also gain hands-on experience through project-based courses and internships, where they work on real-world problems and develop solutions that address the needs of businesses and other organizations. Graduates of the ETI major are well-prepared for careers in a variety of fields, including information technology consulting, systems analysis, software development, and project management. They are also well-equipped to pursue advanced degrees in information technology, business administration, and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Resource Management
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Environmental Resource Management major, a student must: 1. have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements: BIOL 110 or CHEM 110 or ECON 102, MATH 110 or MATH 140; 2. have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. Additionally, freshman applicants must meet high school unit requirements: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language.
Concentration: Environmental Science, Soil Science, Water Science
Description: The Environmental Resource Management (ERM) major is designed for students who want to study the science and management of natural resources, with a focus on their protection and sustainable use. ERM is a science-based, interdisciplinary major that provides students with a strong foundation in the biological, chemical, and physical sciences, and the social sciences. The program emphasizes an integrated approach to environmental problem-solving, incorporating elements of ecology, soil science, hydrology, and environmental policy and law. Students can tailor their education by choosing one of three options: Environmental Science, Soil Science, or Water Science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Systems Engineering
Requirements: Entrance to the Environmental Systems Engineering major requires the completion of at least 29 credits and a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. Additionally, students must complete MATH 140, MATH 141, CHEM 110, and PHYS 211 with a grade of C or better.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Environmental systems engineering is the application of engineering and scientific principles to manage environmental impacts from human activities. At Penn State, the Environmental Systems Engineering (ENVSE) program is specifically focused on environmental issues associated with the extraction, processing, and use of energy and mineral resources. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics, which is then applied to the study of air pollution, water quality, and solid and hazardous waste management. The program also emphasizes the importance of environmental health and safety and the social and ethical responsibilities of engineers. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in environmental consulting, industry, and government agencies, as well as for further study in graduate or professional programs.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Systems Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Environmental Engineering and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film Production
Requirements: Admission to the Film Production major is a two-step process. First, students must be admitted to the Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications. Second, enrollment in the Film Production major is limited. Students apply for admission to the major after completing at least three semesters of study at Penn State and the two prerequisite courses: COMM 150 and COMM 242. Admission to the major is competitive and based on a review of the student's creative work and academic record.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The Film Production major is for students who want to develop their own creative voices as filmmakers and who are interested in pursuing a career in the film industry. The major provides students with a solid foundation in the history, theory and practice of film production. Students learn all aspects of the filmmaking process, including screenwriting, directing, cinematography, editing and sound design. The program emphasizes the importance of both individual artistic expression and collaborative teamwork. Throughout the program, students have the opportunity to work on a variety of film projects, ranging from short experimental films to longer narrative or documentary works. The curriculum is designed to help students develop their technical skills while also encouraging them to explore their own unique perspectives and styles. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a wide range of careers in the film and television industry, as well as for further study at the graduate level.
Accredidation: The Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Finance major, students must enroll in the Smeal College of Business or the Division of Undergraduate Studies and must complete the following entrance-to-major requirements: ACCTG 211(4) or ACCTG 211H(4), ECON 102(3) or ECON 102H(3), ENGL 15 GWS(3) or ENGL 30 GWS(3) or ENGL 137H GWS(3) or CAS 137H GWS(3), MATH 110 GQ(4) or MATH 140 GQ(4) or MATH 110H GQ(4) or MATH 140H GQ(4), STAT 200 GQ(4) or SCM 200 GQ(4) or SCM 200H GQ(4). All these courses must be completed with a grade of C or better. Students must have a minimum cumulative grade-point average that is set annually.
Description: Finance is the study of how people and organizations raise, allocate, and use money over time. It is a diverse field that includes such areas as corporate financial management, investment analysis, and the operation of financial markets and institutions. The Finance major is designed to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge needed to understand the design and operation of financial markets and the types of financial decisions made by corporations and other organizations. The curriculum includes courses in corporate finance, investment analysis, financial modeling, and international finance. Students develop analytical and quantitative skills that are essential for success in the financial industry. The program prepares students for careers in areas such as corporate finance, investment banking, asset management, and financial consulting.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
ScholarshipType: Federal Grants, State Grants, University Scholarships, Private Scholarships, Loans, and Student Employment

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food Science
Requirements: Graduates of a high school or those who have earned a GED may be eligible for admission to the first-year class. Requirements for admission to the University are a high school diploma or GED and the following high school units: 4 units of English; 3 units of mathematics (algebra, geometry, trigonometry, or higher math); 3 units of science; 3 units of social studies; 2 units of the same second language. In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; completed the following courses and earned a grade of C or better in each: CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, MATH 110 or MATH 140.
Description: Food Science is the study of the biological, physical, and chemical nature of food and food ingredients and the changes they undergo during processing and storage. It is a multifaceted discipline based on the chemistry, physics, biology, and math of food and food ingredients. In the Food Science major, students learn to apply these fundamental principles to the manufacturing, distribution, and consumption of safe, healthy, and high-quality food. At Penn State, students choose from a variety of courses to tailor their education to their interests. The curriculum includes courses in food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering, food processing, and sensory evaluation. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research, internships, and study abroad programs. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in the food industry, government, and academia.
Accredidation: The Food Science major is approved by the Higher Education Review Board of the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Forensic Science
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Forensic Science major, a student must: 1. have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, FRNSC 210, and MATH 140; 2. have earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00
Concentration: Biology Option, Chemistry Option
Description: Forensic Science is the application of scientific principles and techniques to the investigation of crime. This major is an interdisciplinary program that includes courses in the fields of biology, chemistry, and physics, as well as forensic science. It is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, as well as an understanding of the legal system and the role of forensic science in the criminal justice system. Students choose one of two options: Biology or Chemistry. The Biology option is designed for students interested in careers in forensic biology, DNA analysis, or related fields. The Chemistry option is designed for students interested in careers in forensic chemistry, toxicology, or related fields. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in local, state, and federal crime laboratories, as well as private forensic laboratories and research institutions.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Forensic Science is accredited by the Forensic Science Education Programs Accreditation Commission (FEPAC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French and Francophone Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the French and Francophone Studies major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. For first-year admission, applicants are evaluated on their high school GPA and completion of required high school coursework (including 4 units of English, 3 units of Math, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language).
Description: The major in French and Francophone Studies provides students with the opportunity to study the French language and the literatures and cultures of France and the Francophone world. The program is designed to help students develop a high level of proficiency in the French language, as well as a broad understanding of the historical, social, and cultural contexts of the French-speaking world. Students can choose from a variety of courses in literature, linguistics, film, and culture, and they are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in France and other Francophone countries. The major prepares students for a wide range of careers in international business, government, education, and many other fields, and it also provides a solid foundation for graduate study in French or related areas.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geography
Requirements: Admissions requirements for the Bachelor of Science in Geography are consistent with the requirements for the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. To be eligible for admission to the Geography major, students must be enrolled in the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences or the Division of Undergraduate Studies (DUS). For admission to the University, first-year applicants must have a high school diploma or its equivalent and have completed a minimum of 15 units of preparatory work, including 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a single world language other than English.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: General Geography Option, Geographic Information Science Option, Human Geography Option, Nature-Society Geography Option, Physical Geography Option
Description: Geography is the study of the spatial patterns of human and physical phenomena, the processes that form those patterns, and the relationships between them. It is an integrative discipline that explores the relationships between people and their environments. The Bachelor of Science in Geography provides students with a strong foundation in both the physical and social sciences, as well as technical skills in geospatial analysis. Students can choose from several options to specialize in areas such as physical geography, human geography, geographic information science, or nature-society geography.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Geography is the study of the earth as the home of humanity. Geography is a diverse discipline that explores the spatial distributions of human and physical phenomena and the interactions between them. Geography is an integrative discipline that is uniquely positioned to help us understand and solve the world's most pressing problems, such as climate change, poverty, and inequality. The Geography B.A. program provides a broad liberal arts education and prepares students for a wide range of careers in both the public and private sectors.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geosciences
Requirements: Entrance to the Geosciences major requires that a student have: (1) completed at least 29 credits; (2) earned a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00; and (3) completed GEOSC 1, GEOSC 20, or GEOSC 71; and CHEM 110 and MATH 140, each with a grade of C or better.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: Geosciences Option, Hydrogeology Option, Paleontology Option
Description: The Geosciences major is for students interested in Earth's history, its resources, and the processes that shape its surface and interior. Students in this major gain a broad background in the geosciences, which provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers or for graduate study. The major offers three options: Geosciences Option, Hydrogeology Option, and Paleontology Option.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Requirements: For entrance into the major, students must have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher.
Description: The German major provides a well-rounded education in German language, literature, and culture. The program is designed to develop students’ proficiency in the four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing) and to provide them with a comprehensive understanding of the history, literature, and culture of the German-speaking world. The major also prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as education, business, government, and international relations, as well as for graduate study in German or related fields. The program offers a range of courses in language, literature, culture, and linguistics, and students are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Germany or Austria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global and International Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Global and International Studies major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed at least 27.5 credits. For Penn State's general admission requirements, freshman applicants must submit Penn State’s undergraduate application, official high school transcripts or GED, and SAT or ACT scores (optional through 2025).
Concentration: Culture and Identity; Global Conflict; Global Health; Global History; Human Rights; International Political Economy and Development; Migration and Diaspora; Sustainability and Development; Wealth and Inequality; Urbanization; Africa; Asia; Europe; Latin America and the Caribbean; Middle East
Description: The Global and International Studies (GLIS) major is an interdisciplinary program designed to help students understand the complex processes of globalization that are transforming our world. The major offers students the opportunity to study global issues from a variety of perspectives, including those of the humanities and social sciences. Students in the GLIS major choose both a global theme (such as human rights, global health, or global conflict) and a world region on which to focus their studies. The major also requires students to develop proficiency in a foreign language and encourages them to study abroad. The goal of the major is to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to live and work in an increasingly interconnected world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Global and International Studies
Requirements: Applicants must apply to the University through the Undergraduate Admissions Office. In addition to the University's high school graduation requirements, the College of the Liberal Arts requires two units of a single world language other than English. To be eligible for entrance to the Global and International Studies major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits and be enrolled in or have completed his/her fourth semester; (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00; and (3) have completed GLIS 101 or GLIS 102 with a grade of C or better.
Concentration: African Studies, Asian Studies, Culture and Identity, Global Conflict, Global Education, Global Health, Global Humanities, Human Rights, International Affairs, International Business, International Political Economy and Development, Latin American Studies, Middle Eastern Studies
Description: The Global and International Studies major (GLIS) is designed to help students better understand the complex, interconnected world of the twenty-first century. Drawing upon the resources of multiple departments and programs in the College of the Liberal Arts and the University, the GLIS major helps students think across traditional boundaries and allows them to design a course of study that reflects their own interests and goals. Core courses introduce students to the diverse field of global and international studies, and encourage them to view issues from multiple disciplinary perspectives. Students choose one of several tracks: African Studies, Asian Studies, Culture and Identity, Global Conflict, Global Education, Global Health, Global Humanities, Human Rights, International Affairs, International Business, International Political Economy and Development, Latin American Studies, Middle Eastern Studies. Students in the GLIS major are also required to achieve proficiency in a foreign language and to participate in a global experience (education abroad or a domestic internship with a significant global/international focus).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Design in Graphic Design
Requirements: Admission to the Graphic Design major is a two-step process. First-year students must first apply to Penn State and then submit a portfolio to the Stuckeman School via SlideRoom. Admission is based on a review of the student’s academic record and the portfolio.
Description: Graphic design is a professional program that provides students with a sequence of courses that emphasize the development of concepts and the application of methods to solve problems in visual communication. These courses address issues of strategy, research, branding, information design, systems, typography, image making, and storytelling. Students gain proficiency in the use of traditional and digital tools and develop an understanding of the historical, social, and cultural context of design. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in design, including brand identity, user experience, interaction design, motion graphics, and print and digital publishing.
Accredidation: The graphic design program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Policy and Administration
Requirements: First-year applicants must complete a minimum of 15 units of high school coursework, including 4 units of English, 3 units of Social Studies, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Math (specifically Algebra 1, Algebra 2, and Geometry or Trigonometry), and 2 units of a single world language. Evaluation for admission is primarily based on the student's high school academic record (GPA) and the completion of these required subjects. Penn State is currently test-optional through the fall 2025 semester.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The B.S. in Health Policy and Administration (HPA) program prepares students for management and policy positions or graduate study in the health care field. Students in the major develop the skills and knowledge needed to understand the complex societal problem of providing access to quality health care at reasonable cost. HPA students study a multidisciplinary curriculum that integrates health care services, public health, health policy, and business/management. Students gain an understanding of the business of health care, including: Management, Finance, Marketing, Economics, Policy, Ethics, Public health, Law. The program also focuses on the role of government in health policy and the healthcare industry, and on providing students with the skills they need to lead and manage healthcare organizations.
Accredidation: The HPA undergraduate program is a member of the Association of University Programs in Health Administration (AUPHA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: To be considered for first-year admission to Penn State, applicants must complete high school course requirements, which include four units of English, three units of social studies, three units of science, and three units of math (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry). Applicants must also submit a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional. For entrance to the History (B.A.) major specifically at Abington, students must satisfy a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The major in History is intended for students who wish to study history for its own sake or as part of a broad liberal arts education. It also serves as preparation for graduate study in history and related fields or for careers in law, government, business, journalism, or other areas where the ability to research, analyze, and communicate is valued. The major provides students with the opportunity to study the history of various parts of the world and to explore different historical approaches and methods. The program is designed to develop students’ critical thinking, research, and writing skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) satisfy the third semester classification; 3) complete the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, HM 201. Standard Penn State undergraduate admission requirements also apply, including the submission of a high school transcript and optional standardized test scores.
Description: The Hospitality Management (HM) major is designed to prepare students for management positions in the various segments of the hospitality industry. The program provides a broad-based education in the basic business disciplines, followed by advanced courses in hospitality management. Students gain practical experience through internships and other hands-on learning opportunities. The Hospitality Management program is one of the oldest and most respected programs of its kind in the nation. It provides students with a solid foundation in the liberal arts and sciences, along with a strong background in business and a specialized education in hospitality management.
Accredidation: The Hospitality Management program is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration (ACPHA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. be in at least their third semester (at least 27.1 credits). For the Bachelor of Science degree in Human Development and Family Studies, a minimum of 120 credits is required.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Life Span Development Option, Life Span Human Services Option
Description: Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) is a multidisciplinary major that focuses on the study of individuals, families, and communities with the goal of improving the lives of others. In this major, students will learn about: the fundamental biological, psychological, and sociological processes of human development from conception through old age; how social and cultural contexts, such as families, peers, schools, and workplaces, influence individual development; how individuals and families can better adapt to changes and challenges across the lifespan; how to develop, implement, and evaluate programs and policies that promote healthy development and well-being; how to use research and evidence to understand and address human development and family issues. Students in HDFS also gain practical experience through a required internship in a human services setting, which allows them to apply their knowledge and skills in a real-world setting. This major prepares students for careers in a variety of fields, including: human services, such as social work, counseling, and case management; education, such as early childhood education and youth development; health-related fields, such as public health and health administration; research and policy analysis.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Resource Management
Requirements: Entrance to Major: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Human Resource Management major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. have completed ECON 102 GS(3), PSYCH 100 GS(3), and STAT 200 GQ(4) or SCM 200 GQ(4), and earned a grade of C or better in each of these courses. To be eligible for admission to the College of the Liberal Arts, an applicant must have completed: 2 units of a single world language other than English.
Description: The Human Resource Management major is a multidisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in the human resource management field. Human resource management involves the recruitment, selection, training and development, compensation, and evaluation of employees in organizations. The major provides students with a broad understanding of the legal, social, and economic environment in which organizations operate, as well as the specialized knowledge and skills needed to manage people effectively. Students in the major take courses in a variety of areas, including labor and employment law, staffing and development, compensation and benefits, and organizational behavior. The major also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, communication, and interpersonal skills. Graduates of the Human Resource Management major are prepared for a variety of careers in human resource management, including human resource generalist, recruiter, compensation analyst, and training and development specialist. They are also prepared for graduate study in human resource management, labor and employment relations, and other related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Industrial Engineering major, students must have completed 29-55 cumulative credits at Penn State; have an overall cumulative grade-point average of 2.60 or higher; and have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211.
Description: Industrial engineering is the study of how to make things better. Industrial engineers design, analyze, and manage complex systems that involve people, technology, and information. They use their knowledge of mathematics, science, and engineering to improve the efficiency, quality, and safety of these systems. Industrial engineers work in a variety of industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, and logistics. They may be involved in designing new products, improving production processes, or managing supply chains. The mission of the Harold and Inge Marcus Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering is to provide a high-quality education in industrial engineering that prepares students for successful careers in a global environment and for further study at the graduate level. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the mathematical, scientific, and engineering principles of industrial engineering, as well as the communication and teamwork skills necessary for success in the profession.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Information Sciences and Technology
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Information Sciences and Technology major, a student must: 1) attain a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher; and 2) complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: IST 110, IST 140 (or CMPSC 101 or CMPSC 121), IST 210, and IST 220. General first-year admission to the university requires the completion of specific high school units, including four units of English, three units of Mathematics (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry/pre-calculus), three units of Science, three units of Social Studies, and two units of a World Language.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Concentration: Information Systems Design and Development Option; Information Technology: Integration and Application Option; Information Context: People, Organizations, and Society Option
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Information Sciences and Technology (ISTBS) provides students with a theoretical framework and the skill sets to compete in a field that is heavily dependent on information technology. As the use of technology continues to expand, it is increasingly important for students to have a firm understanding of information technology’s impact on people and organizations. This degree explores the design, development, and use of information technology to address problems for individuals, organizations, and society.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Information Sciences and Technology at University Park is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Integrated Social Sciences
Requirements: Our Bachelor of Science in Integrated Social Sciences is a flexible degree program that gives you the tools to explore how the world works across a variety of social science disciplines. Working with a dedicated program director, you can customize your coursework to match your specific interests while following a rigorous academic path. Students will gain knowledge in research methods, ethics, and critical thinking. They will also be able to communicate effectively in a variety of formats.
Description: The Integrated Social Sciences (ISS) major provides an opportunity for students to study the social sciences through a multidisciplinary approach. Students in this major gain a comprehensive understanding of how humans behave, interact with one another and their environment, and organize themselves into complex social, political, and economic systems. ISS students choose courses from a wide range of disciplines, including anthropology, communication arts and sciences, economics, political science, psychology, and sociology. They also engage in research and practical applications of social science concepts, preparing them for a variety of careers in fields such as business, law, public policy, and social services. Overall, the ISS major provides a unique and flexible way for students to explore their interests in the social sciences and develop critical thinking and analytical skills that are highly valued in today's workforce.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Integrative Science
Requirements: Entrance to the Integrative Science major (ISCI_BS) requires the following: Cumulative grade point average of at least 2.00. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are not required for students applying for undergraduate admission through the 2025-26 academic year.
Concentration: General Science Option; Biological Sciences and Health Professions Option; Legal Studies, Government Service, Public Policy Option
Description: The Integrative Science major is a multidisciplinary science program. It is designed for students who want a broad education in the natural sciences. The program offers three options: General Science, Biological Sciences and Health Professions, and Legal Studies, Government Service, Public Policy. Students in all options take a core of courses in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. They then choose additional science courses and electives based on their chosen option. The General Science option allows students to explore a variety of scientific disciplines. The Biological Sciences and Health Professions option is designed for students interested in careers in the health sciences. The Legal Studies, Government Service, Public Policy option is for students interested in the intersection of science and law, government, or policy. The Integrative Science major provides students with a strong foundation in the natural sciences and prepares them for a variety of careers in science, healthcare, law, government, and policy, as well as for further study in graduate or professional school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interdisciplinary Business with Engineering Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Interdisciplinary Business with Engineering Studies major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and completed: MATH 140, ECON 102, CHEM 110 and ACCTG 211 with a grade of C or better.
Department: Black School of Business and School of Engineering
Concentration: Accounting/Finance, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, Product Development, Quality Control, and Systems Analysis
Description: Interdisciplinary Business with Engineering Studies (IBE) is designed to meet the needs of students who want to bridge the gap between business and technology. This major provides students with a foundational understanding of both business and engineering, preparing them for roles in project management, technical sales, supply chain management, and other positions where a dual understanding is essential. The program is offered jointly by the Black School of Business and the School of Engineering at Penn State Behrend. This major provides a program of study that is at the intersection of business and engineering. The program’s mission is to provide students with a cross-functional systems view of the business and technical worlds and to provide them with the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as a liaison between the two. The curriculum includes a set of core courses in both business and engineering that provide a foundation in both disciplines. Students then choose a module of courses in a specific area of interest. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in a wide range of fields, including technical sales, product management, supply chain management, and project management. The curriculum emphasizes the development of critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, and it provides students with the opportunity to apply their knowledge through a senior capstone project.
Accredidation: The Black School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interdisciplinary Science and Business
Requirements: The Interdisciplinary Science and Business (ISB) degree, offered by the School of Science and the Black School of Business, allows students to prepare for careers in the 21st-century business and technology environment. This program provides students with a solid foundation in the physical and life sciences and a thorough understanding of the business principles needed to manage modern technology. Graduation requirements include 121 credits, and students must complete coursework in science, business, and engineering. For more information, please contact the B.S. in Interdisciplinary Science and Business program at 814-898-6105 or email behrend-science@psu.edu.
Concentration: Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Bioinformatics, Chemistry, or Environmental Science
Description: The Interdisciplinary Science and Business (ISB) major, which is only available at Penn State Behrend, combines training in science with business and market knowledge. This major is perfect if you want to apply your scientific knowledge to a career in business, such as in laboratory management, technical sales, product development, or marketing for high-tech or pharmaceutical firms. To add depth to your study, you’ll choose a module—a specific area of science—to study. You can choose from Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Bioinformatics, Chemistry, or Environmental Science. You’ll also take business courses in accounting, finance, marketing, and supply chain management. This well-rounded curriculum will give you a competitive edge in a variety of industries.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Business
Requirements: International Business is a secondary major. To graduate with a major in International Business, a student must also complete a primary major in the Smeal College of Business. Entrance to the International Business major occurs at the same time as entrance to the primary Smeal major. To be eligible for the International Business major, a student must be enrolled in the Smeal College of Business or the Division of Undergraduate Studies. Students must have completed 29-59 cumulative credits at Penn State and have a cumulative grade-point average of 3.20. In addition to the GPA and credit requirements, students must also: 1. Complete or be currently enrolled in the following entrance-to-major courses: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30, MATH 110 or MATH 140, STAT 200 or SCM 200. 2. Demonstrate proficiency in a contemporary foreign language. 3. Submit an application for the major.
Description: The International Business (IB) major provides students with a broad business background and a focused study of the international business environment. To succeed in this major, students must have a strong interest in understanding other cultures and desire to live and work in the global marketplace. The curriculum includes one year of study in a foreign language (or equivalent proficiency), a study-abroad experience, and a second major in one of the functional business areas (Accounting, Business Economics, Finance, Interdisciplinary Business with Engineering Studies, Management, Management Information Systems, Marketing, or Project and Supply Chain Management). Students receive an excellent education that prepares them for a variety of careers in the international business arena, as well as graduate study in business or international affairs.
Accredidation: The Black School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, financial need, and community service

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Politics
Requirements: Entrance to Major: In order to be eligible for entrance to the International Politics major, a student must: 1. attain at least a C (2.00) cumulative grade-point average for all courses taken at the University; and 2. have at least third-semester classification (a minimum of 44 credits). For a first-year student to be eligible for admission to the College of the Liberal Arts, an applicant must have a high school diploma or its equivalent and have completed the following units: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry or higher math), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of a single world language.
Concentration: International Relations, International Political Economy, and National Security
Description: The major in International Politics is intended for students who wish to focus their study of political science on international and comparative politics. Students develop an understanding of the relationship between domestic and international politics, and the factors that influence how states and non-state actors interact with one another. The major provides a broad foundation in the study of international relations and comparative politics, while also allowing students to specialize in one of three areas: International Relations, International Political Economy, or National Security.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Italian
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Italian major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and completed or be currently enrolled in IT 3 or IT 10.
Description: This major is designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of Italian language, literature, and culture. Italian language courses at the basic and intermediate levels are designed to develop students' proficiency in speaking, writing, reading, and listening, while the more advanced literature and culture courses are designed to broaden students' perspectives on Italy's role in the world and to strengthen their skills in critical thinking and literary/cultural analysis. Students who major in Italian develop skills that are useful for careers in international business, diplomacy, and law, as well as for those who wish to pursue graduate study in Italian literature and culture.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Japanese major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits and be enrolled in or have completed no more than 60 credits; (2) have completed JAPNS 1, JAPNS 2, and JAPNS 3; (3) have earned at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The Japanese major is designed to help students reach a high level of proficiency in the Japanese language, and a broad understanding of Japanese culture. Core courses in the major are language-focused, and provide students with a solid foundation in the four skills of speaking, listening, reading and writing. Other courses in the major explore Japanese literature, culture, and linguistics. Many students combine a Japanese major with a second major in a different field. Our students have recently combined Japanese with such majors as Anthropology, Biology, History, Information Sciences and Technology, International Politics, Linguistics, and Marketing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Jewish Studies
Requirements: This program currently has no additional requirements for entrance to the major. For Penn State's admissions requirements, visit the Admissions website. First-year admission to Penn State is based on several factors, including: High school coursework, Grades, Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) – optional through Fall 2025.
Description: Jewish Studies is an interdisciplinary field that allows students to explore the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people from their origins to the present. The program is designed to give students a broad knowledge of the Jewish experience and to develop their skills in critical thinking, research, and writing. Students take courses in a variety of fields, including history, philosophy, religious studies, Hebrew language and literature, and the social sciences. The major is flexible and can be tailored to meet students' interests and career goals. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers, including law, education, journalism, social work, and the clergy, as well as for graduate study in Jewish Studies and other fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Journalism major, a student must: (1) have completed COMM 160 with a grade of C or better; (2) have completed at least 27.5 cumulative credits; and (3) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Concentration: Broadcast Journalism, Digital and Print Journalism
Description: The Journalism major provides students with a broad-based education in the traditions and practices of the profession. The program emphasizes the role of journalism in a democratic society and the importance of ethical and professional standards. Students learn to gather, verify, and present information across multiple platforms, including print, digital, and broadcast media. The curriculum is designed to help students develop strong writing and reporting skills, as well as an understanding of the legal and ethical issues facing journalists today. In addition to core journalism courses, students may choose from a variety of electives to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals.
Accredidation: The Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Kinesiology major, a student must have: 1) attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better: BIOL 110 GN(4), KINES 100(3), KINES 101(3), PSYCH 100 GS(3) and one of the following: BIOL 161 GN(3) or BIOL 141 GN(3).
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Applied Exercise and Health, Exercise Science, Movement Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Kinesiology offers several options to provide students with a variety of career paths. Students choose from one of the following: Applied Exercise and Health, Exercise Science, and Movement Science. All of the options require a common core of Kinesiology courses and a capstone experience. All options also require a grade of C or better in all Kinesiology courses (KINES and KINES prefix courses) and in several other required courses. The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology (KINES) degree provides a comprehensive foundation for understanding the biological and social sciences, the humanities, and the arts as they relate to human movement. Students explore the effects of physical activity on human health and performance. Kinesiology provides a background for careers in health-related fields, such as physical therapy, occupational therapy, medicine, chiropractic, and physician assistant. It also prepares students for careers in sports-related fields, such as athletic training, exercise physiology, strength and conditioning, and sports management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Labor and Human Resources
Requirements: To be eligible for first-year admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Labor and Human Resources at Penn State, applicants must meet the university's general undergraduate admission requirements. These include the completion of specific high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics, 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of a single world language. Admission decisions are primarily based on a student's academic record in high school, including grade point average (GPA) and the rigor of the curriculum.
Department: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Labor and Human Resources (LHR) major is a multidisciplinary program that focuses on the world of work. LHR students develop a broad understanding of the workplace, the people who work there, and the organizations that employ them. The program is designed for students who are interested in people and the world of work and who want to learn about how to improve the lives of workers and the effectiveness of organizations. Students in the LHR major learn about the history of work and labor, the legal and regulatory framework that governs the workplace, and the economic and social factors that shape the workplace. They also develop skills in areas such as human resource management, labor relations, conflict resolution, and organizational behavior.
Accredidation: The Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) has acknowledged that Penn State Behrend’s Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science in Labor and Human Resources degree programs fully align with SHRM’s HR Curriculum Guidebook and Templates.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Labor and Human Resources
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Labor and Human Resources major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 cumulative credits; (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00; and (3) have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: LHR 100.
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Labor and Human Resources is designed for students who want a more technical and quantitative program than the Bachelor of Arts. Like the Bachelor of Arts, this major is a multi-disciplinary program that provides students with a foundational understanding of the world of work, including the relationship between employers and employees, the legal and social context of work, and the management of human resources. Students learn about the economic, social, and political forces that shape the workplace and the lives of workers. The program prepares students for careers in human resource management, labor relations, and related fields in both the public and private sectors. The B.S. degree requires more coursework in quantitative methods and business-related subjects than the B.A. degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Landscape Architecture in Landscape Architecture
Requirements: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (B.L.A.) is a five-year professional degree program, fully accredited by the Landscape Architecture Accreditation Board (LAAB). Admissions to the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture program are handled through the Undergraduate Admissions Office. To be eligible for entrance to the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture major, a student must: (1) have completed the admission requirements of the University and the College of Arts and Architecture; (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher.
Description: Landscape architecture is the art of design, planning, or management of the land, arrangement of natural and man-made elements thereon through application of cultural and scientific knowledge, with concern for resource conservation and stewardship, to the end that the resultant environment serves a useful and enjoyable purpose. The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (B.L.A.) is a five-year professional degree program. The first year of the program is common to both the B.L.A. and the B.S. Landscape Architecture programs. The professional B.L.A. degree prepares students for licensure.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Latin American Studies major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. For admission to the University, undergraduate applicants must submit an application, official high school transcripts or a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR), and have completed specific high school units including 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a single World Language.
Description: The Latin American Studies major is designed to provide students with a broad and comprehensive view of Latin American cultures, politics, and societies. Its primary purpose is to help students learn about the complex histories, diverse populations, and varied contemporary issues of Latin America and the Caribbean. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, allowing students to explore the region through courses in history, political science, literature, anthropology, sociology, and other fields. Students are required to develop proficiency in either Spanish or Portuguese, and they are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Latin America to gain firsthand experience. The major prepares students for careers in international business, government service, education, journalism, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in various disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Law and Society
Requirements: Entrance to Major: No additional requirements for admission to this major. For more information about the admission process, students should visit the Undergraduate Admissions website.
Description: The Law and Society major is an interdisciplinary program of study that allows students to explore the nature and function of law in its social context. Students will examine the role of law in shaping social, political, and economic life, as well as the ways in which social forces influence the development and implementation of law. The major is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in the liberal arts, while also offering them the opportunity to focus on specific areas of interest related to law and society. Students will develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication that are essential for success in a variety of careers, including law, public service, and social advocacy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Letters, Arts, and Sciences
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Letters, Arts, and Sciences major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 27.5 credits; (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00; and (3) submit a proposal for the major. The proposal must be developed in consultation with a faculty advisor. The proposal must include: (1) a statement of the student's goals; (2) a list of the courses that will be used to meet the requirements for the major; and (3) a rationale for how the courses will help the student meet their goals.
Description: The Letters, Arts, and Sciences (LAS) major is a multidisciplinary, student-designed program. It is for students who want to develop a program of study that is not available through existing majors. It is intended to allow students to pursue a broad-based, theme-oriented program of study in the liberal arts. Through their choice of courses, students will explore a specific topic or theme from the perspectives of several different disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
