Requirements: Requirements for admission to the University as a first-year student include a high school diploma or equivalent and the completion of the following high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics, 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of the same world language. Penn State is test-optional through fall 2025.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguists examine how language is structured, how it is acquired, how it is used by individuals and in society, and how it changes over time. The Linguistics major provides students with a strong foundation in the core areas of linguistic analysis: phonetics (the study of speech sounds), phonology (the study of sound systems), morphology (the study of word structure), syntax (the study of sentence structure), and semantics (the study of meaning). Students also have the opportunity to explore various subfields of linguistics, such as psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, historical linguistics, and language acquisition.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Management
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Management major, students must: 1. obtain a cumulative grade-point average (GPA) of 2.00 or higher; 2. complete and earn a grade of C or better in: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H or ESL 15, MATH 110 or MATH 140, and STAT 200 or SCM 200.
Description: The Management major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills needed to manage people and processes in a variety of organizations. The major focuses on the development of leadership, strategic thinking, and organizational design skills. Students will learn how to motivate employees, build effective teams, manage change, and develop and implement strategies to achieve organizational goals. The curriculum includes courses in human resource management, organizational behavior, strategic management, and international management. Management majors are prepared for a variety of careers in business, government, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in business or related fields.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. The Business programs at Penn State Harrisburg, Penn State Abington, Penn State Altoona, and Penn State Erie, The Behrend College, are also accredited by AACSB International. In addition, the Business programs at Penn State Berks, Penn State Schuylkill, and Penn State Scranton are accredited by the Accreditation Council for Business Schools and Programs (ACBSP).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Management Information Systems
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Management Information Systems at Penn State, first-year applicants must submit an online application (via Penn State’s MyPennState portal or the Common App) and a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are optional through the Fall 2025 application cycle. Penn State does not require letters of recommendation, a resume, or a writing sample as part of the undergraduate application process. While an optional personal statement is available within the application, it is not required.
Description: Management Information Systems is a multi-disciplinary major that focuses on the use of information technology to support business processes and decision-making. MIS is the study of technology’s role in organizations and how technology can be used to solve business problems and create new business opportunities. Students in the MIS major learn about the design, development, and implementation of information systems that support the strategic goals of an organization. The curriculum includes courses in business processes, database management, systems analysis and design, and data communications. Graduates of the MIS major are prepared for careers as business analysts, systems analysts, IT consultants, and database administrators.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marketing
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Marketing major, students must: 1) attain a cumulative grade-point average of 3.20 or higher; 2) complete the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30, MATH 110 or MATH 140, MGMT 301, MKTG 301, and SCM 301; and 3) have completed at least 44 but no more than 59 cumulative credits at Penn State. High school requirements for admission include 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science/Social Studies, and 2 units of a single World Language.
Description: The Marketing major provides students with analytical and interpersonal skills to understand customer needs and provide solutions. Marketing starts with understanding the needs and values of customers, and then developing and delivering products and services that fulfill those needs. Successful marketing professionals must understand the psychology of consumer behavior, use research and data analytics to identify market opportunities, and manage the communication and delivery of the firm's value proposition. The major is designed to allow students to choose a variety of tracks for their careers, such as brand management, professional selling, business-to-business marketing, and retail management.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Materials Science and Engineering major, a student must: 1. Have completed the following entrance-to-major courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211. 2. Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00. General application requirements include the completion of the Penn State application or Common App, the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR), and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT), which are optional through the fall 2025 semester.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Materials Science and Engineering is a versatile and intellectually stimulating field of study that focuses on the design, development, and application of materials for various industries. It combines principles from physics, chemistry, and engineering to understand the structure, properties, processing, and performance of materials such as metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. The undergraduate program in Materials Science and Engineering is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of materials science and the practical skills necessary to solve real-world engineering problems. Students learn how to manipulate the structure of materials at the atomic and microscopic levels to achieve desired properties, and how to select the best materials for specific applications. The curriculum includes a balance of core courses in materials science, mathematics, and physics, as well as specialized courses in areas such as electronic materials, biomaterials, and nanomaterials. Students also have the opportunity to engage in hands-on laboratory experiences and research projects, working closely with world-class faculty and state-of-the-art facilities.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
ScholarshipType: Academic achievement, financial need, and diversity

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. General freshman admission requirements include 15 secondary school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and algebra 2), 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of a single world language. For entrance to the Mathematics major, a student must have: 1) attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) completed MATH 140 and MATH 141 with a grade of C or better.
Description: This major provides a program of instruction for students who plan to work in business, industry, or government, or to pursue graduate study in mathematics or a related field. The B.A. degree is a flexible program that includes a wide range of elective courses and a foreign language requirement. It is particularly suitable for students who wish to combine a strong background in mathematics with a second major in a field that also has a Bachelor of Arts program, such as Economics or a foreign language. It also provides an excellent background for students who wish to pursue a career in law or business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Mathematics major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed MATH 140 and MATH 141 with a grade of C or better. General first-year admission requires a high school diploma or equivalent and the completion of specific high school units including English, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, and World Language.
Concentration: Actuarial Mathematics Option, Applied and Industrial Mathematics Option, Computational Mathematics Option, General Mathematics Option, Graduate Study Option, Systems Analysis Option
Description: The B.S. degree in Mathematics is designed to provide a broad foundation in mathematics and to allow students to specialize in one of several areas. The program aims to prepare students for careers in industry, government, or education, as well as for further study in graduate or professional school. This major is a program of instruction in mathematics that provides a degree of specialization in one of several areas. The program is flexible and can be adapted to many different career goals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: 1. A minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.60. 2. Completion of the following courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211. General freshman admission requires the submission of an official high school transcript or equivalent.
Description: Mechanical Engineering is one of the broadest engineering disciplines. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices, including tools, engines, and machines. Mechanical engineering is also one of the most flexible engineering disciplines. Mechanical engineering students will learn about the fundamentals of mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer, and they will apply these principles to the design and analysis of mechanical systems. They will also learn about materials science, manufacturing processes, and control systems. The program provides students with a strong foundation in mathematics and the physical sciences, as well as the communication and teamwork skills necessary for success in the engineering profession. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing, as well as for further study in graduate school.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at Penn State Berks is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at Penn State Harrisburg is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at Penn State Scranton is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering Technology
Requirements: To be eligible for the Mechanical Engineering Technology major, a student must have earned a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 and completed MET 107, MET 111, MATH 022, and MATH 026 or MATH 040 or MATH 041 or MATH 081 or MATH 140. General first-year admission requirements for Penn State Behrend include 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (algebra, geometry, trigonometry), 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of a single world language.
Description: Mechanical engineering technology is the application of engineering principles and modern technology to the design, development, and manufacture of products and systems. The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering Technology (MET) program at Penn State Behrend emphasizes the application of technical knowledge to solve engineering problems. Students learn about materials, design, manufacturing, and thermal-fluid systems. The program prepares graduates for careers in industries such as automotive, aerospace, energy, and manufacturing.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering Technology at Penn State Behrend is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical Engineering Technology and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Media Studies
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Media Studies major, a student must: 1. have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. have completed at least 29.1 credits.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Concentration: Film Strategy, International Media, Media Effects, and Society and Culture
Description: The Media Studies major provides a liberal arts education that focuses on the study of media. The program is designed to help students understand the history and role of media in society, to examine the artistic and social value of media products, and to develop an understanding of the impact of media on individuals and cultures. The major emphasizes the study of media history, theory, and research, as well as the analysis of media content and its social, cultural, and political implications. Students can choose to focus their studies in areas such as: Film Strategy, International Media, Media Effects, and Society and Culture. Media Studies students develop the skills for a variety of careers in the media industries, including media research, media management, and media production. The major also prepares students for graduate study in media-related fields, law, and the social sciences.
Accredidation: The Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Meteorology and Atmospheric Science
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must have achieved a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 and have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements: MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211. General high school requirements for freshman admission include 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry/pre-calculus), 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies/arts/humanities, and 2 units of a single world language.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: Atmospheric Research and Applications Option, Environmental Meteorology Option, General Meteorology Option, Weather Forecasting and Communications Option, Weather Risk Management Option
Description: Meteorology is a profession that uses scientific principles to explain, understand, and forecast the behavior of the earth's atmosphere and its interactions with the earth's surface and the oceans. This discipline utilizes the tools and concepts of physics, chemistry, and mathematics to study the earth's atmosphere and its relationship to the environment. Students in the meteorology and atmospheric science major will develop a strong background in these sciences and learn to use sophisticated computer and analytical tools to explore and understand the complex systems that govern our weather and climate. Students choose from five specialized options that provide more in-depth training in areas of atmospheric research, environmental meteorology, weather forecasting and communications, weather risk management, and a general meteorology option for those who wish to maintain a broad background in the field. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in weather forecasting, environmental consulting, atmospheric research, and other fields that require a deep understanding of the atmosphere and its impact on society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Microbiology major, a student must: 1) attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2) completed MICRB 201(3) or MICRB 202(2) and earned a grade of C or better. Freshman Students: Information on the Penn State admission process for first-year students can be found on the Admissions section of the Bulletin. Transfer Students: Information on the Penn State admission process for transfer students can be found on the Admissions section of the Bulletin.
Description: Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, archaea, fungi and protozoa. This discipline includes fundamental research on the biochemistry, physiology, cell biology, ecology, evolution and clinical aspects of microorganisms, including the host response to these agents. The Microbiology major is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in the life sciences, with a focus on the biology of microorganisms. The curriculum includes a core of courses in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics, followed by advanced courses in microbiology, immunology, and virology. Students in the major have the opportunity to participate in research projects in the laboratories of faculty members in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Middle Level Education
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Middle Level Education major, a student must: 1. Attain at least a 3.00 cumulative grade point average. 2. Complete at least 48 units of transferable college-level credit. 3. Pass the Basic Skills Requirement. 4. Complete ENGL 15 GWS or ENGL 30 GWS, 3 credits of literature, and MATH 200 and MATH 201. 5. Complete EDPSY 14.
Concentration: English/Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies
Description: The Middle Level Education major prepares students to teach in grades four through eight. In addition to a common core of courses in child development, adolescent development, and educational theory and practice, students choose one of four areas of concentration: English/Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, or Social Studies. Successful completion of this major leads to the Bachelor of Science degree and eligibility for the Pennsylvania Department of Education’s Instructional I certificate for Middle Level (grades 4-8).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mining Engineering
Requirements: Entrance to Major (ETM) Requirements: In addition to the University requirements for entrance to a major, the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences requires that students complete MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better. Students may spend their first two years at any Penn State campus and then finish the final two years at University Park or Fayette.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Mining engineering is a diverse field that involves the extraction of critical minerals and resources from the earth. These resources are the building blocks of our society and are essential for everything from building infrastructure and technology to producing energy. In our mining engineering program, you will learn the fundamental principles of engineering and apply them to the design, construction, and operation of mines. You will explore topics such as rock mechanics, ventilation, mineral processing, and environmental sustainability. Our program also emphasizes the importance of safety, ethics, and social responsibility in the mining industry. You will have the opportunity to work on real-world projects and gain hands-on experience through internships and co-op programs. Mining Engineering (MNGE) is a discipline that involves the extraction and processing of mineral resources from the earth. These resources include everything from metals and coal to industrial minerals and aggregates. Mining engineers play a vital role in ensuring that these resources are extracted safely, efficiently, and sustainably. The Mining Engineering major at Penn State is one of the oldest and most respected programs of its kind in the United States. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the physical sciences and engineering, as well as specialized knowledge in mining-related topics. The program’s educational objectives are to: apply their strong foundation in engineering, science, and mining in a variety of careers; effectively use their mining engineering education in a professional or managerial capacity; exhibit professionalism, safety consciousness, and a commitment to environmental and social responsibility; and engage in life-long learning and maintain their technical competence.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mining Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Mining and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.
ScholarshipAmount: more than $300,000 available annually through the department
ScholarshipType: Departmental scholarships, merit-based and need-based awards

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: In addition to the application for admission to the University, students must also submit a School of Music application and complete an audition on a band or orchestral instrument, piano, organ, or voice. Entrance to the major occurs upon completion of at least 29.1 credits, with a minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA and a successful performance audition.
Concentration: Music Performance, Music Studies, Music Technology
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Music is a flexible program of study designed for students who wish to pursue a broad liberal arts education with a major in music. This degree is often chosen by students who wish to double major in music and another subject. The curriculum provides a foundation in music theory, history, and performance, while allowing students to choose one of three options to tailor the degree to their interests.
Accredidation: The Pennsylvania State University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music
Requirements: Entrance to the Bachelor of Music (B.M.) major requires a successful performance audition on a standard orchestral or band instrument, piano, organ, classical guitar, or voice. Audition requirements are available on the School of Music website. In addition to the audition, students must also complete the University application for admission. Students are admitted to the program only after a successful audition has been completed and they have been admitted to the University.
Concentration: Performance Option, Composition Option, Music History and Literature Option, Music Theory Option
Description: The Bachelor of Music (B.M.) degree is designed for students who want to become professional performers (both instrumental and vocal), composers, and/or teachers of music at the collegiate level, and/or who want to pursue graduate study in music. It offers professional-level training in performance, composition, music history, and music theory. The curriculum is intended to provide a solid foundation in musical performance and academic studies, with the flexibility to meet the individual needs and interests of students. The Bachelor of Music degree is the professional music degree in the United States and is recognized as the appropriate undergraduate preparation for graduate studies in performance, composition, and other areas of music.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music Education in Music Education
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Music Education program, applicants must first apply for undergraduate admission to Penn State. Once the University application is submitted and a Penn State ID number is received, applicants must submit the School of Music supplemental application to schedule an audition. Required components for the School of Music application include a successful performance audition on a primary instrument or voice, an interview with music education faculty, and a brief essay (statement of intent) explaining the applicant's choice of music education as a career. A resume of musical background and activities is also required as part of the supplemental application.
Concentration: Choral, Instrumental, or General Music Education
Description: The Bachelor of Music Education (B.M.E.) degree is a professional degree that qualifies students for a Pennsylvania Level I Professional Certificate (K-12). In addition to professional and general education requirements, students must select an option in Choral, Instrumental, or General Music Education. Each option provides a curriculum designed to prepare students to teach in all areas of music. All students must complete a semester of student teaching (12 credits) following the successful completion of all other required coursework.
Accredidation: The Penn State School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Musical Arts in Musical Arts
Requirements: Entrance to the Musical Arts major requires a successful audition on an instrument or voice. In addition to the audition, students must submit a personal statement (maximum 500 words) describing their interest in the Bachelor of Musical Arts degree, as well as two letters of recommendation from music professionals. For some students, an interview or a portfolio review may be required.
Description: The Bachelor of Musical Arts (B.M.A.) is a professional degree that provides a more flexible curriculum than the Bachelor of Music degree. In addition to a rigorous musical core, it provides the opportunity to explore an outside area of interest, which could be a minor or a second major. Like the B.M. and B.M.E. degrees, the B.M.A. requires an audition and provides for weekly lessons and participation in the school's premier ensembles. This degree is often chosen by students who are interested in pursuing double majors, or by students who are interested in fields such as arts administration, music therapy, or music law. The B.M.A. requires the same core music theory and history courses as the B.M. and B.M.E. degrees, but it provides for 16-22 credits of an outside area of study.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Musical Theatre
Requirements: Admission to the Musical Theatre option is based on an audition. Potential students must first be admitted to the university and then audition for the program. The audition process involves a pre-screen submission including a resume, headshot, and performance videos. Candidates who pass the pre-screen are invited to a final audition consisting of singing, acting, and dance components.
Description: This professional program is designed to prepare students for careers in musical theatre. The curriculum provides balanced and integrated training in the three primary disciplines of musical theatre: acting, singing, and dance. The program is committed to the development of the individual artist and to the exploration of musical theatre as a collaborative art form. Successful completion of the program leads to the Bachelor of Fine Arts degree. This program is intensive and requires a high degree of commitment and discipline. In addition to rigorous studio training, students have the opportunity to participate in a wide variety of performance activities, including mainstage productions, studio projects, and workshops.
Accredidation: The School of Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Nuclear Engineering major, students must satisfy the following requirements: 29-55 cumulative credits (one semester in residence at Penn State); 2.60 cumulative grade-point average; and completion of MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better.
Description: Nuclear engineering is a multidisciplinary field with primary focus on the synergistic use of nuclear processes. These processes include the fission of heavy nuclei for energy production, the fusion of light nuclei for energy production, and the use of ionizing radiation in various applications. Since nuclear processes are fundamentally different from chemical or mechanical processes, the field is based on a distinct set of principles. Nuclear engineering requires a strong foundation in mathematics and the basic sciences. This foundation is used to develop the specific topics of nuclear engineering including nuclear physics, radiation interaction with matter, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, and nuclear materials. These topics are integrated into the design and analysis of nuclear systems. Students apply their knowledge through the use of sophisticated computer modeling and experimental facilities. Nuclear engineers are employed in the design, construction, and operation of nuclear power plants, as well as in the research and development of new nuclear technologies. They also work in the fields of radiation medicine, environmental protection, and national security.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Nuclear and Radiological Engineering Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nursing
Requirements: Admission to the Nursing major is competitive. Review factors include the high school grade-point average and high school coursework. Review of applications for the Nursing major begins in early November. First-year students who select the Nursing major on their application will be reviewed for admission to the College of Nursing. High school students are required to have: 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry or higher math), 3 units of science, and 3 units of social studies, humanities, or the arts. In addition, two units of the same world language other than English are required.
Department: Ross and Carol Nese College of Nursing
Concentration: General Nursing Option, Second Degree Option, RN to B.S.N. Option
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (B.S.N.) degree is a program of professional study that includes a broad foundation in the liberal arts and sciences and a concentration in nursing science. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for professional nursing practice and for graduate study in nursing. Students are prepared to provide nursing care to individuals, families, and communities in a variety of health care settings. The curriculum also emphasizes the development of clinical judgment, communication, and leadership skills. Graduates are eligible to take the National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses (NCLEX-RN) for licensure as a professional registered nurse.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice program and post-graduate APRN certificate program at The Pennsylvania State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Sciences
Requirements: First-year students who meet the university admission requirements are admitted directly into the major. High school unit requirements include: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (Algebra, Geometry, and Trigonometry), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, Arts, or Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language. Penn State is currently test-optional through the Fall 2025 semester. To be eligible for entrance to the Nutritional Sciences major, a student must have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Dietetics, Applied Sciences, Basic Sciences
Description: This major is for students who are interested in the roles of diet and nutrition in health and disease throughout the life cycle. The Nutritional Sciences major has three options: Dietetics, Applied Sciences, and Basic Sciences. The Dietetics option is for students who want to become a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN). It is a Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD), which is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND). This option prepares students for a supervised practice program (i.e., dietetic internship) to meet the requirements for the RDN credential. The Applied Sciences option is for students who want to work in community nutrition, public health, food and nutrition industries, or pursue careers in health care, such as nursing or physician assistant. The Basic Sciences option is for students who want to focus on the biological and physical sciences to prepare for research careers or graduate school, or for careers in health care, such as medicine or dentistry.
Accredidation: The Dietetics option is a Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD), which is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Organizational Leadership
Requirements: For information about the Penn State application process, please visit the Office of Undergraduate Admissions website. To be eligible for entrance to the Organizational Leadership major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The Organizational Leadership (OLEAD) major is a multidisciplinary program of study that provides students with a broad-based foundation in leadership theory and practice. The program focuses on the essential skills required for effective leadership in a variety of organizational settings. Students will explore leadership from several perspectives, including the individual, the group, the organization, and society. The program emphasizes the development of critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, as well as an understanding of the ethical and social dimensions of leadership. Graduates of the program will be prepared for leadership roles in business, government, non-profit organizations, and other professional settings.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Organizational Leadership
Requirements: Penn State reviews applications for first-year and transfer admission based on a variety of factors, including high school GPA, high school coursework, and standardized test scores (if submitted). For transfer students, the primary consideration is the student’s academic record at previous colleges or universities. High school students are expected to complete specific units of study, including English, Social Studies, Science, Arts/Humanities, and Mathematics (Algebra 1, Algebra 2, and Geometry/Trigonometry).
Description: Organizational Leadership is an undergraduate major for students interested in leadership. The program provides a broad-based education in the foundations of organizational leadership. The social sciences, humanities, and professional fields are represented in the curriculum. The major is specifically designed for those who are in or who aspire to leadership positions in organizations. Students learn about the social, psychological, and business aspects of leadership, including organizational behavior, ethics, diversity, and conflict resolution. The program also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills.
ScholarshipType: Academic achievement, financial need, and community involvement

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Petroleum and Natural Gas Engineering
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; completed MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better. General undergraduate admission also requires the completion of specific high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of social studies, 3 units of science, 3 units of math (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), and 2 units of a single world language.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: Petroleum and natural gas engineers are involved in all phases of exploiting hydrocarbon deposits. They help decide how to drill the wells and how to best produce the oil and gas. They also design and install the equipment needed for production and transportation. In addition to these technical roles, petroleum and natural gas engineers are also involved in the economic and environmental aspects of the industry. The curriculum at Penn State is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and engineering, followed by specialized courses in drilling, production, and reservoir engineering. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research and internships, which can provide them with valuable experience in the field.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Petroleum and Natural Gas Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Petroleum and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. complete the following entrance to major course with a grade of C or better: PHIL 1 or PHIL 2 or PHIL 12 or PHIL 13; 2. have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Concentration: General Philosophy Option, Ethics and Social-Political Philosophy Option
Description: Philosophy is the oldest and most fundamental of the intellectual disciplines. It is the study of the most basic principles of existence, knowledge, and value. Because philosophy is a central part of a liberal education, it is an excellent major for students who want a broad-based education that will prepare them for a variety of careers. The Philosophy major is designed to provide students with a broad background in the history of philosophy, as well as an opportunity to focus on specific areas of interest. The major is also designed to develop the student’s ability to think critically and to communicate clearly and effectively.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Physics major, a student must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and completed MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and PHYS 212 and earned a grade of C or better in each of these courses. General first-year admission requirements include the completion of specific high school units: 4 units of English, 3 units of mathematics (algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of science, 3 units of social studies, and 2 units of a single world language. Applicants must also provide high school transcripts or a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Concentration: Acoustics Option, Electronics Option, General Physics Option, Medical Physics Option, Nanotechnology/Materials Option, Physics Computing Option
Description: Physics is the study of the fundamental laws of nature that govern the behavior of matter and energy from the smallest scales of subatomic particles to the largest scales of the entire universe. It is the most fundamental of the sciences and provides the foundation for our understanding of the physical world. The Bachelor of Science degree in Physics provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the physical world, as well as the mathematical and analytical tools necessary to describe it. The program is designed to prepare students for graduate study in physics or related fields, or for careers in industry, government, or education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Planetary Science and Astronomy
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and 2. have completed MATH 140, MATH 141, PHYS 211, and PHYS 212, and earned at least a grade of C in each of these courses.
Description: The Planetary Science and Astronomy major is a flexible program for students interested in the Earth, the solar system, and the universe. The major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the physical sciences and mathematics and a broad introduction to the fields of astronomy and planetary science. The curriculum includes a core of courses in astronomy, geosciences, physics, and mathematics. Students can choose from a wide range of electives in astronomy, geosciences, and other sciences to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals. This major is appropriate for students who intend to pursue careers in the aerospace industry, planetariums and science museums, and government agencies, as well as for those who plan to pursue graduate study in planetary science, astronomy, or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Plant Sciences
Requirements: Entrance to the Plant Sciences major requires a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average. For first-year admission, Penn State requires a completed application and high school transcripts. The university is test-optional for the 2024 and 2025 application cycles, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required but may be submitted for consideration.
Concentration: Agroecology, Horticulture, Plant Science
Description: Plants provide the fundamental basis for life on Earth as the source of food, fuel, fiber, and medicine. They also provide the aesthetic beauty in our gardens and landscapes. Plant Science is the study of how plants grow and how they can be used to improve the world. In the Plant Sciences major, you'll learn about the science and technology of plant production, the use and management of plants in the landscape, and the improvement of plants and their products. You can focus your studies by choosing from one of three options: Agroecology, Horticulture, or Plant Science. Students who graduate with a major in Plant Sciences can find careers in many different areas of the plant sciences, including: agribusiness and production, landscape management and design, research and development, teaching and extension, public and private gardens, and government agencies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Political Science major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. completed PLSC 1, PLSC 3, PLSC 7, or PLSC 14 with a grade of C or better. For the B.A. degree in Political Science, a minimum of 123 credits is required.
Description: Political science is the study of how people govern themselves—at the local, state, national, and international levels. It involves the study of political institutions (such as parliaments, courts, and the presidency), political behavior (such as how people vote or why they join social movements), and public policy (how governments deal with issues like the environment or the economy). It also includes the study of political theories that help us understand the nature of justice, power, and democracy. The major is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the discipline and to allow them to develop specific interests in one or more of its subfields. Through their coursework, students will learn how to analyze political events, think critically about political issues, and communicate their ideas clearly and effectively.
ScholarshipType: Academic selection, financial need, and diversity-based scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Political Science
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Political Science major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29 credits; (2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00; (3) have completed and earned a grade of C or better in at least two of the following: PLSC 1, PLSC 3, PLSC 7, PLSC 14; and (4) have completed and earned a grade of C or better in 3 credits of GH, GS, or GHW.
Concentration: B.S. Option A: Theory/Law; B.S. Option B: American; B.S. Option C: Comparative/International; B.S. Option D: General
Description: Political Science is the study of nature, causes, and consequences of collective decisions and actions taken by groups of people and the cultures and institutions that structure power and authority. In other words, Political Science is the study of politics, government, and public policy, whether at the local, state, national, or international level. Political Science students learn to understand how and why governments make decisions and why people act the way they do in political contexts. They also learn how to evaluate these decisions and actions according to different criteria, such as justice, efficiency, and democracy. The Bachelor of Science degree in Political Science is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in political science while also emphasizing the development of analytical and quantitative skills. The B.S. degree is especially well-suited for students who are interested in careers in government, public policy, or law, and for those who plan to pursue graduate studies in political science or a related field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Polymer Science and Engineering
Requirements: For the Materials Science and Engineering major (which offers an emphasis in Polymer Science and Engineering), first-year applicants must meet Penn State's general undergraduate admission requirements, including submission of a high school transcript or equivalent and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). For students seeking entrance to the major, specific requirements include the completion of CHEM 110, MATH 140, MATH 141, and PHYS 211 with a grade of C or better and a minimum cumulative grade-point average (GPA) of 2.00. Additionally, Penn State is test-optional through the Fall 2025 semester, meaning standardized test scores are not required for admission.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Concentration: Polymer Science and Engineering
Description: The Materials Science and Engineering (MatSE) major provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the relationships between the structure, properties, processing, and performance of materials. This knowledge is essential for the design and development of new materials with tailored properties for specific applications. The program is designed to provide students with a broad based foundation in the five major classes of materials: metals, ceramics, polymers, electronic and photonic materials, and composites. Students learn how to apply principles from chemistry, physics, and engineering to solve problems related to the selection, design, and use of materials. Throughout the curriculum, there is an emphasis on the role of materials in addressing societal challenges in areas such as energy, health, and sustainability. In addition to core courses, students have the opportunity to take technical electives in areas of interest, such as biomaterials, nanotechnology, and computational materials science. The program also includes a capstone design project, where students work in teams to solve a real-world materials-related problem.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering at University Park is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Premedical-Medical
Requirements: To be considered for the Premedical-Medical program, a student must be in their final year of high school. In addition to completing the Penn State application, a student must submit an official SAT or ACT score (the SAT/ACT requirement is not optional for this program). Admission to this program is highly selective. The most successful applicants have: A minimum combined SAT score of 1470 (Evidence-based Reading and Writing + Math) OR a composite ACT score of 32; Rank in the top 10 percent of their high school graduating class; and Significant volunteer or work experience in a healthcare setting. After an initial review, a select group of applicants will be invited to complete the second phase of the application process, which includes an additional application, three letters of recommendation, and a personal statement.
Description: This program is a special, accelerated program for students who have high potential for being successful in medical school. It is an cooperative program between The Pennsylvania State University and the Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University. In the first three years, the students complete the requirements of the Eberly College of Science for the Premedical-Medical (PMM) major. After the third year, the students transfer to Sidney Kimmel Medical College. After the successful completion of the first year of medical school at Sidney Kimmel Medical College, the Bachelor of Science degree in Premedical-Medical is awarded by Penn State. After the successful completion of the remaining three years of medical school, the M.D. degree is awarded by Sidney Kimmel Medical College. This accelerated program allows students to complete their formal education in seven years instead of eight.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Premedicine
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and 2) complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, CHEM 113, MATH 140, MATH 141.
Description: This major is a multidisciplinary program in the Eberly College of Science for students who want a broad education in the sciences and a deeper understanding of the relationship between the sciences and the practice of medicine. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for the pursuit of a medical or other health-related professional degree. It includes a strong core in the sciences and math and also includes humanities and social sciences to give students a comprehensive education for medical school. Students have the opportunity to delve deeper into one of several disciplines through the choice of elective credits in the major. The major also helps students prepare for medical school entrance exams. Students learn the basic principles and foundational information for careers in many health-related professions including medicine, osteopathy, dentistry, optometry, and podiatry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Design in Professional Photography
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Professional Photography major, a student must: 1. attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; 2. satisfy any other entrance requirements for the major. Administrative Enrollment Controls are initiated when student demand exceeds the capacity of a program's faculty or facilities. Students must have completed a certain number of credits and have a specific grade point average for admission.
Description: The Professional Photography major provides a program of study in the professional and creative aspects of photography. It is designed to prepare students for careers as professional photographers in a variety of fields, including commercial, editorial, and fine art photography. The curriculum focuses on developing technical skills in digital imaging, lighting, and camera operation, as well as fostering creative vision and critical thinking. Students have the opportunity to work in state-of-the-art facilities and gain hands-on experience through studio projects and real-world assignments. The program also emphasizes the business and professional aspects of the photography industry, including portfolio development, marketing, and business management.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Project and Supply Chain Management
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the Bachelor of Science in Project and Supply Chain Management, students must submit an application through MyPennState or the Common App, and provide a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Penn State is test-optional for students applying through the fall 2025 semester. For entrance to the major, students typically must complete specific prerequisite courses, including MATH 110 or MATH 140, STAT 200 or SCM 200, and ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H, with a grade of C or better, and meet minimum cumulative GPA requirements.
Description: The Project and Supply Chain Management (PSCM) major provides students with the opportunity to develop the quantitative and people skills necessary to design and operate complex management systems. The major provides students with a combination of project management and supply chain management. In today's competitive business environment, project management and supply chain management skills are critical to the success of most companies. In addition to the logistics and materials management components of supply chain management, the major also includes the management of the 'upstream' and 'downstream' flows of materials and services to and from the customer. Project management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements. Project management is used for everything from large-scale construction projects to software development to the implementation of new business processes. The PSCM major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to be successful in either of these fields.
Accredidation: AACSB International

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Psychology major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; completed PSYCH 100 with a grade of C or better; and completed one of the following with a grade of C or better: STAT 200, SOC 1, or PSYCH 100. Applicants must also meet general high school unit requirements, which include 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior—the biological, emotional, cognitive, and social processes that underlie what people do and say. Psychology is also a profession, which involves the application of knowledge, skills, and techniques to human problems. The B.A. degree is a broad-based degree that provides students with a solid foundation in the field, while also offering the flexibility of a liberal arts education. Students learn about the research methods used by psychologists and the application of psychological principles to real-world problems. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the liberal arts and to prepare them for a variety of careers in fields such as human services, business, and education, as well as for graduate study in psychology or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR) and meet specific high school unit requirements: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry or higher math), 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies/Arts/Humanities, and 2 units of a single World Language. For formal entrance to the Psychology B.S. major, students must complete PSY 100, STAT 200 or PSY 200, and one additional 200-level PSY course (such as PSY 212, PSY 221, or PSY 231) with a grade of C or better, and maintain a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Concentration: Life Sciences, Business/Applied
Description: The Psychology major focuses on the scientific study of biology, behavior, and mental processes of humans and animals. This includes learning, memory, perception, and development as well as child and adult psychopathology, and the social and biological bases of behavior. Students gain a better understanding of their own behavior and the behavior of others and develop a range of skills for the workplace or graduate school. Those seeking a B.S. degree in psychology will study how psychology is used in a variety of ways. This degree includes two options: Life Sciences and Business/Applied. The Life Sciences option prepares students for careers or further study in areas such as health psychology, clinical psychology, and neuroscience. The Business/Applied option prepares students for careers or further study in areas such as industrial/organizational psychology and human factors. For both options, there is an emphasis on the use of quantitative and research methods.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Public Policy major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy provides students with the foundational tools to analyze, implement, and evaluate policy at the local, state, national, and international levels. Drawing from several social science disciplines, the curriculum includes courses in political science, economics, and sociology, as well as specialized courses in policy analysis, implementation, and evaluation. Students in the major develop a strong background in both quantitative and qualitative research methods, and learn to apply these tools to solve real-world problems. The program also emphasizes the importance of ethics and leadership in public service. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector, as well as for graduate study in public policy, public administration, law, and other related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: be enrolled in the College of Health and Human Development or the Division of Undergraduate Studies. have completed the following: ENGL 15 or ENGL 30H; and 3 credits from the following: STAT 200, PSYCH 200, or SOC 7.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Commercial Recreation and Tourism Option, Community Recreation Option, Outdoor Recreation Option, Professional Golf Management Option
Description: This major is designed to prepare students for professional, supervisory, and management positions in various park, recreation, and tourism agencies and organizations. The program provides students with a broad understanding of the recreation, park, and tourism field and allows them to specialize in one of several options. Students learn to design, manage, and deliver recreation and leisure services in a variety of settings, including municipal, state, and federal park and recreation agencies; commercial recreation and tourism enterprises; and non-profit organizations. The program focuses on understanding the human, social, and environmental impacts of recreation and leisure activities and on developing the skills needed to manage these activities effectively.
Accredidation: The Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management program is accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Parks, Recreation, Tourism and Related Professions (COAPRT).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Rehabilitation and Human Services
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average; and 2. have at least third-semester classification (at least 29.1 credits). For information on the Penn State admission process, please visit the Undergraduate Admissions website.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Rehabilitation and Human Services (RHS) degree program is designed to help students learn the knowledge and skills they will need to work in a variety of help-giving professions. These include positions in mental health, social services, and rehabilitation. RHS professionals work with individuals of all ages and all types of disabilities and disadvantages. This includes people with physical, mental, emotional, or cognitive disabilities; people with addictions; people who have been in the criminal justice system; people who are homeless; and people living in poverty. RHS majors learn to help others reach their personal, social, and vocational goals, and to help improve their quality of life. The degree is also an excellent foundation for students who want to go on to graduate school in several different fields (e.g., counseling, social work, physical or occupational therapy, etc.).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission at Penn State, first-year applicants must submit an application (either via MyPennState or the Common App) and their official high school transcripts (Self-Reported Academic Record). For the 2025-26 academic year, Penn State is test-optional, meaning students may choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores for consideration.
Description: Religious Studies is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the diversity of religious practices and beliefs from around the world and throughout history. Scholars of religious studies use a variety of methods to understand how religion shapes and is shaped by human culture, society, and politics. The Department of Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies offers a major and minor in Religious Studies. Students who major in Religious Studies will develop a deep understanding of the world's religions and the skills to analyze religious texts, rituals, and institutions. They will also gain a broad perspective on the role of religion in human life and the challenges and opportunities of living in a religiously diverse world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Risk Management
Requirements: Entrance to the Risk Management major occurs during the spring semester of the student's sophomore year. A student must have: (1) attained at least a 3.20 cumulative grade point average (this GPA is subject to change each year); (2) completed or be currently enrolled in all entrance-to-major courses; (3) completed at least 44 cumulative credits at Penn State; and (4) submitted an application for the major through LionPATH. The following entrance-to-major courses must be completed with a grade of C or better: MATH 110 or MATH 140, ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15 or ENGL 30, MGMT 301, MKTG 301, STAT 200 or SCM 200.
Concentration: Actuarial Science, Enterprise Risk Management, and Real Estate
Description: The Risk Management major provides students with the choice of three options: Actuarial Science, Enterprise Risk Management, and Real Estate. Actuarial Science involves the application of mathematics and statistics to the design of insurance and benefit systems. Professional actuaries help organizations evaluate the financial impact of future contingent events. Enterprise Risk Management involves the identification, assessment, and management of various risks facing organizations, including corporate liability, property loss, and employee benefits. Real Estate involves the study of the development, financing, management, and marketing of land resources. Learning outcomes for the program include: 1. Students will understand and be able to apply the risk management process to analyze and manage the risks faced by organizations and individuals. 2. Students will understand the role of insurance and other risk transfer mechanisms in managing risk. 3. Students will be able to apply quantitative methods to assess and measure risk. 4. Students will understand the legal and regulatory environment of risk management and insurance. 5. Students will be able to communicate risk management concepts effectively.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International. The Actuarial Science option is recognized as a Center of Actuarial Excellence (CAE) by the Society of Actuaries (SOA).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Russian major, a student must have: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average; 2. completed at least 29.1 credits. For the B.A. degree in Russian, a minimum of 120 credits is required. For Penn State's general admission requirements, please visit the Undergraduate Admissions website.
Description: The Russian major provides a well-rounded education in the language, literature, and culture of Russia and the Russian-speaking world. In addition to gaining proficiency in the language, students develop an understanding of Russian history and society through the study of its literary and cultural traditions. A degree in Russian prepares students for a variety of careers in both the public and private sectors, including government service, international business, law, journalism, and education. It also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in Russian or related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Science
Requirements: To be considered for first-year admission to Penn State, applicants must submit the online application and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Penn State is test-optional through the fall 2025 semester; first-year applicants can choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. For students already enrolled at the university, entry to the Science (SCIBC) major requires a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average and at least 29.1 credits.
Concentration: Biological Sciences and Health Professions, General Science, and Legal Studies, Government Service, Public Policy
Description: The Science major is an interdisciplinary degree that allows students to design a curriculum that meets their individual goals. The curriculum includes a core of courses in the life and physical sciences, as well as a selection of advanced courses in a variety of scientific disciplines. The major is designed to provide students with a broad base of knowledge in the sciences, while also allowing them to specialize in a particular area of interest. Students in the major can choose from one of three options: Biological Sciences and Health Professions, General Science, and Legal Studies, Government Service, Public Policy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Secondary Education
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Secondary Education major, a student must: 1) have completed at least 27.1 credits and have a cumulative grade-point average of 3.00; 2) have completed CI 280 and EDPSY 14 with a grade of C or better; 3) provide evidence of 80 hours of volunteer or paid service with learners of the age group the candidate plans to teach; 4) submit a completed Entrance-to-Major application; and 5) provide evidence of having completed at least 6 credits of college-level mathematics, 3 credits of college-level English literature, and 3 credits of college-level English composition.
Concentration: Biological Science Option, Chemistry Option, Earth and Space Science Option, English Communication and Composition Option, Environmental Education Option, General Science Option, Mathematics Option, Physics Option, Social Studies Option
Description: This major is designed to provide students with the necessary professional and subject matter preparation to satisfy the requirements for teacher certification in Pennsylvania. It also provides the basis for graduates to seek certification in other states. The curriculum includes a strong component in general education; a depth of knowledge in one or more subject matter areas; and a component in professional education which includes course work and multiple field experiences, including a student teaching internship.
Accredidation: The programs are approved by the Pennsylvania Department of Education and are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Security and Risk Analysis
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Security and Risk Analysis major, students must: 1) have completed the following entrance-to-major requirements with a grade of C or better: IST 140, SRA 111, MATH 110 or MATH 140, and STAT 200 or SCM 200; and 2) have achieved a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. Incoming first-year students are admitted directly into the College of Information Sciences and Technology as pre-major students.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Concentration: Information and Cybersecurity, Intelligence Analysis and Modeling
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Security and Risk Analysis (SRA) degree program is designed to prepare students for careers in the growing field of security and risk management. The SRA major provides students with a theoretical and practical understanding of how to protect people, information, and assets. The curriculum includes courses on risk analysis, security technologies, law and policy, and the social and ethical implications of security measures. Students in the SRA major choose one of two options: Information and Cybersecurity, which focuses on the technical aspects of security, such as network security, cryptography, and digital forensics; or Intelligence Analysis and Modeling, which focuses on the analytical aspects of security, such as threat assessment, intelligence gathering, and risk modeling.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Social Work in Social Work
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to the Social Work major, a student must: 1. Have completed 32.1 or more credits. 2. Have a cumulative GPA of 2.50 or higher. 3. Have completed SOC 1 or SOC 5 with a grade of C or better. 4. Have completed or be enrolled in SW 200W with a grade of C or better. 5. Complete an application for entrance to the B.S.W. program.
Description: The Bachelor of Social Work (B.S.W.) degree program is designed to prepare students for entry-level generalist social work practice. Social workers help individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities to enhance or restore their capacity for social functioning and create societal conditions favorable to this goal. The Social Work program is based on the belief that social workers must have a broad liberal arts education and a firm grounding in the social and behavioral sciences. The curriculum provides students with the knowledge, values, and skills necessary to practice social work in a variety of settings, such as child welfare, health care, mental health, aging, and corrections. The program also prepares students for graduate study in social work and related fields.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Social Work program at Penn State is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: Incoming first-year students are admitted directly to the major. For more information about the admission process, students should visit the Undergraduate Admissions website.
Description: Sociology is the scientific study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. Since all human behavior is social, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob; from organized crime to religious cults; from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture; and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sports. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge. Sociology provides many distinctive perspectives on the world, generating new ideas and critiquing the old. The field also offers a range of research techniques that can be applied to virtually any aspect of social life: street crime and delinquency, corporate downsizing, how people express emotions, welfare or education reform, how families differ and flourish, or problems of peace and war. Because sociology addresses the most challenging issues of our time, it is a rapidly expanding field whose potential is increasingly tapped by those who craft policies and create programs. Sociologists understand social inequality, patterns of behavior, forces for social change and resistance, and how social systems work. Sociology is an exciting discipline with expanding opportunities for a wide range of career paths. The major is designed to provide students with a broad education that will prepare them for a variety of professional careers as well as for graduate study in sociology and other fields, such as law, medicine, social work, business, public policy, and public health.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sociology
Requirements: Incoming freshmen at University Park are admitted directly into the College of the Liberal Arts. For University-wide admission policies, please consult the Undergraduate Education section of this Bulletin. To be eligible for entrance to the Sociology (SOCBS) major, a student must have: attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Concentration: social data analytics; community and environment; or health and family
Description: The B.S. degree in Sociology provides a more specialized program of study in the field than the B.A. It is designed to prepare students for graduate study or for careers in areas that require more advanced research skills and a broader knowledge of certain subfields of sociology. Sociology is the study of how people create, maintain, and change social structures and how these structures, in turn, affect them. Students choose an area of specialization from the following: social data analytics; community and environment; or health and family. They learn how to use both qualitative and quantitative research methods to examine the ways that race, class, gender, and age influence how people interact with one another and with social institutions like the family, the media, the legal system, and the economy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Spanish major, a student must: 1) have completed at least 29.1 cumulative credits; 2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00.
Concentration: Applied Spanish; Literature, Culture, and Linguistics; Spanish for the Professions
Description: The Spanish major is designed to help students develop a high level of proficiency in the Spanish language and a broad understanding of the cultures and literatures of the Spanish-speaking world. The program offers a variety of courses in language, literature, linguistics, and culture, and students are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Spain and Latin America. The Spanish major provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue careers in education, government, business, international relations, or any field where proficiency in Spanish and cultural sensitivity are valued. It also prepares students for graduate study in Spanish or other related disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Special Education
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Special Education major, a student must: (1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; (2) have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 3.00 (and maintain it); (3) have completed with a grade of C or better: CI 295 (or equivalent), EDPSY 10 or 11, EDTHP 115, ENGL 15 or 30H, MATH 200; (4) have completed at least 6 credits of university-level English literature and composition and 6 credits of university-level mathematics; (5) documentation of at least 80 hours of volunteer or paid education work with people with disabilities.
Description: The Special Education (SPLED) program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to teach learners with disabilities in a variety of settings. The program leads to a Bachelor of Science degree and a Pennsylvania teaching certificate for Special Education PreK-12. The program is committed to a data-based approach to instruction and provides students with multiple opportunities to work with learners with disabilities in classrooms and other settings. Students in the program develop skills in assessment, instruction, and management that allow them to meet the diverse needs of learners with disabilities. The program also emphasizes the importance of collaboration with families and other professionals.
Accredidation: The Special Education program is approved by the Pennsylvania Department of Education (PDE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Requirements: For admission to the University, students must submit a high school transcript or equivalent and meet specific high school unit requirements, including 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language. For formal entrance to the Statistics (B.S.) major, students must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and have completed MATH 140, MATH 141, and either STAT 200 or STAT 250 with a grade of C or better in each of these courses.
Concentration: Actuarial Option, Applied Statistics Option, Graduate Study Option, Statistical Computing Option
