Description: The Statistics major provides students with a strong foundation in the mathematical theory of statistics, while also emphasizing the practical application of statistical methods to real-world problems. Students will learn how to collect, analyze, and interpret data, and how to communicate their findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. The curriculum includes courses in probability, mathematical statistics, applied statistics, and statistical computing. Students also have the opportunity to take elective courses in specialized areas such as biostatistics, data science, and environmental statistics. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including finance, healthcare, government, and technology, as well as for graduate study in statistics, biostatistics, or other related disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Supply Chain and Information Systems
Requirements: To be eligible for entrance to the Supply Chain and Information Systems (SCIS_BS) major, students must: 1. have completed 44-59 cumulative credits at Penn State (this includes current-semester credits in progress). 2. have completed with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, ENGL 15, ENGL 30H, or ESL 15, MATH 110 or MATH 140, and STAT 200 or SCM 200. 3. have achieved a minimum cumulative grade-point average (GPA).
Description: The Supply Chain and Information Systems (SC&IS) major is a multidisciplinary program that provides students with a core of knowledge in supply chain management and information systems. This major is designed to prepare students for professional careers in the design and management of complex business processes that involve the flow of materials, information, and capital. The SC&IS major focuses on the integration of manufacturing and service operations, logistics, purchasing, and information technology. Students learn how to analyze and design supply chains, manage inventories, plan production, and utilize information systems to improve organizational performance.
Accredidation: The Smeal College of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Telecommunications
Requirements: Entrance to the Telecommunications and Media Industries major (formerly Telecommunications) requires that a student have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average and have completed COMM 100, COMM 160, or COMM 180 with a grade of C or better. For the B.A. degree, a minimum of 120 credits is required, including at least 42 credits in the major. Penn State is test-optional for first-year applicants through the fall 2025 semester, meaning standardized test scores are not required for admission.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The Telecommunications major prepares students for careers in the management, programming, and public policy aspects of the electronic media (broadcasting, cable, and the Internet) and the telecommunications industry (telephony and data networking). The program provides students with a strong foundation in the history, technology, and economics of these industries, as well as the legal and regulatory framework within which they operate. Students also explore the social and psychological effects of media on individuals and society. The curriculum is designed to help students develop the critical thinking, communication, and analytical skills needed for professional success in a rapidly changing media environment.
Accredidation: The Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre
Requirements: Entrance to the Theatre major requires a successful audition or interview for all students. This is in addition to the University’s application for admission. To be eligible for entrance to the Theatre major, a student must have completed at least 18 scholarship credits at Penn State and earned at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The B.A. degree in Theatre provides a broad-based, liberal arts foundation for students who want to study theatre as a humanist and artistic discipline. Theatre at Penn State is designed to provide professional training for a limited number of students in several performing and technical areas of theatre. At the same time, it provides courses in all aspects of theatre for other students who want a broad-based liberal arts education or who want a theatre background in preparation for other careers. The program offers students an opportunity for extensive participation in all areas of theatre production and for concentrated study in theatre history, dramatic literature, and theory.
Accredidation: The School of Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Theatre program at Penn State is by interview or audition. This is in addition to the standard Penn State undergraduate application. Applicants must first apply for admission to Penn State through MyPennState or the Common App and then complete a secondary artistic review process via the School of Theatre, which includes submitting a portfolio, resume, personal statement, and participating in an audition or interview depending on the specific concentration (Acting, Musical Theatre, Design and Technology, or Stage Management).
Concentration: Acting, Design and Technology, Musical Theatre, Stage Management
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Theatre is a professionally oriented program that provides rigorous training for students who seek to work in the professional theatre. The program offers several options: Acting, Design and Technology, Musical Theatre, and Stage Management. Each option provides a deep immersion in its specific area of study while providing a broad understanding of the art of theatre. Students are also expected to develop a high level of professional discipline. Students in all options are expected to participate in the production program of the School of Theatre.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Turfgrass Science
Requirements: For the Bachelor of Science degree in Turfgrass Science, a minimum of 120 credits is required. In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. 2. completed and earned a grade of C or better in: BIOL 110, CHEM 110, TURF 235.
Description: Turfgrass Science is the study of the grasses, soils, water, and pests (weeds, insects, diseases) involved in the culture of turfgrasses used on golf courses, athletic fields, home lawns, and other areas. The Turfgrass Science major is designed for students who want to prepare for careers in turfgrass management, including golf course management, athletic field maintenance, professional lawn care, and sod production. The program provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences, including biology, chemistry, and soil science, and then builds on this foundation with specialized courses in turfgrass management, including turfgrass species and cultivars, turfgrass physiology, soil-water-plant relationships, and pest management. Students also have the opportunity to participate in internships and other hands-on learning experiences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science degree in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences (VBSC) provides students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences. For the B.S. degree in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences, a minimum of 124 credits is required. To be eligible for entrance to the major, a student must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. Additionally, each student must earn at least a grade of C in each of the following courses: BIOL 110, BIOL 220W, BIOL 230W, VBSC 50, VBSC 211, and MICRB 201. General first-year application requirements for Penn State include a high school diploma or equivalent and the following high school units: 4 English, 3 Mathematics, 3 Science, 3 Social Studies, and 2 World Language.
Description: This major is a preprofessional program for students who intend to continue their education in veterinary, medical, or other health-related professional schools, or in graduate programs in the biomedical sciences. The major provides a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences. In the junior and senior years, students may select courses from a variety of biomedical and animal health-related areas. Students are encouraged to work with faculty on research projects and to gain clinical experience.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts
Requirements: For the Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts, students must apply to the University and also submit a portfolio through the School of Visual Arts Slideroom. Portfolios are reviewed once a year for admission to the program in the following fall semester. To be eligible for entrance to the Visual Arts major (B.A.), a student must: 1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; 2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00; 3) have completed ART 1, ART 20, ART 30, ART 40, ART 50, and ARTH 111 or ARTH 112 with a grade of C or better.
Department: School of Visual Arts, College of Arts and Architecture
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Visual Arts is intended for students who want a general education in the arts while also pursuing a minor or a second major in another field. The program is flexible and offers students a broad-based studio art experience. Students are encouraged to develop their own personal vision through a variety of media and to integrate their studio work with their academic studies. The degree is particularly appropriate for students who are interested in careers in art-related fields where a broad knowledge of the arts is beneficial.
Accredidation: The School of Visual Arts is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Wildlife and Fisheries Science
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must satisfy the following requirements: 1. have completed 29-59 cumulative credits; 2. have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. For first-year students, admission is based on high school records and optional standardized test scores. Students must have a minimum of 15 units in required subject areas: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Concentration: Fisheries Option, Wildlife Option
Description: This major is designed to provide students with the biological and physical science background needed to understand and manage wildlife and fisheries resources. Students may choose one of two options: Fisheries or Wildlife. The Fisheries Option provides students with a strong background in the ecology, management, and conservation of fish and other aquatic organisms. The Wildlife Option provides students with a strong background in the ecology, management, and conservation of birds, mammals, and other terrestrial organisms. Graduates are prepared for careers with state and federal agencies, non-governmental organizations, and private industry, as well as for graduate study in wildlife and fisheries science and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Women's Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Women's Studies major, students must be enrolled in the College of the Liberal Arts or the Division of Undergraduate Studies and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher.
Description: Women's Studies is an interdisciplinary program that explores the experiences, history, and perspectives of women and the ways in which gender as a category of analysis and a social system shapes human lives. Students learn to use feminist lenses to analyze social, cultural, and political issues and to understand the intersections of gender with race, class, ethnicity, sexuality, and nation. The curriculum emphasizes the development of critical thinking, research, and communication skills and provides students with a broad liberal arts education that prepares them for a wide range of careers in fields such as law, medicine, social work, education, public policy, and business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in World Languages Education
Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: achieve a minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.00; complete at least 48 degree-applicable credits; complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: ENGL 15 or ENGL 30, 3 credits of literature (GH) from the University-approved list, EDPSY 14 or PSYCH 100, and 6 credits of quantification (GQ); provide documentation of at least 40 hours of volunteer or paid experience with learners of the age group the candidate plans to teach; complete a speech-and-hearing screening (at no cost to the student); complete an interview with a World Languages Education faculty member; and complete a dispositional assessment.
Concentration: French Option, German Option, Latin Option, Russian Option, Spanish Option
Description: This major is designed to prepare students for the teaching of world languages (French, German, Latin, Russian, and Spanish) in grades K-12. The program includes work in the language, literature, and culture of the target language, as well as course work in education and a variety of field experiences, including student teaching. Successful completion of the program, along with passing scores on required state tests, leads to the Pennsylvania Instructional I certificate for teaching the target language.
Accredidation: The College of Education's teacher education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Business Administration
Requirements: To apply for the Associate in Science in Business Administration, you must have a high school diploma or its equivalent (GED). High school students may apply for admission; however, they may not begin their studies until they have graduated from high school. Transfer students may also apply; however, any credit earned at another institution will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
Description: The 60-credit Associate in Science in Business Administration degree is designed to help you build a solid foundation in the world of business. You'll gain a comprehensive understanding of business functions and how they relate to one another, including marketing, management, finance, and accounting. The program is specifically designed to prepare you for entry-level positions in business or for further study in a baccalaureate program.
Accredidation: AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business)

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Criminal Justice
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Associate in Science in Criminal Justice degree program, a student must be a high school graduate or have earned a General Education Development (GED) certificate or its equivalent.
Description: The Associate in Science degree in Criminal Justice provides a broad-based education in the criminal justice system. The program is designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills for entry-level positions in the criminal justice field, or for further study in a baccalaureate program. Students will learn about the major components of the criminal justice system, including law enforcement, courts, and corrections. They will also explore the causes of crime and the various ways in which society responds to criminal behavior. The curriculum includes courses in criminal law, criminology, and the administration of justice, as well as general education courses in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences.

ProgramName: Associate in Arts in Letters, Arts, and Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed application, including the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR) or official high school transcripts. Penn State is test-optional for undergraduate admission; students may choose whether or not to include SAT or ACT scores as part of their application.
Description: The Associate in Arts in Letters, Arts, and Sciences is a multi-disciplinary, theme-oriented, student-designed program. It is intended to offer students the opportunity to design a program of study that is unique to their own educational and professional goals. This program is particularly appropriate for students who wish to pursue a broad-based education in the liberal arts or who have specific career goals that are not met by more traditional programs.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Human Development and Family Studies
Requirements: For the Associate in Science degree in Human Development and Family Studies, a minimum of 60 credits is required. To be eligible for entrance to the Human Development and Family Studies major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Adult Development and Aging Option, Life Span Developmental Services Option, Life Span Human Services Option
Description: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) major focuses on how people develop physically, emotionally, and socially within the context of the family, community, and society. Students in the HDFS major will learn about human development across the lifespan and how to help individuals and families improve their quality of life. The HDFS associate degree is a 60-credit program that provides students with a foundational understanding of human development and family studies and is designed to prepare students for entry-level positions in human service settings or to continue their education in a baccalaureate degree program.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Information Sciences and Technology
Requirements: Admission to the Information Sciences and Technology (ISTAS_AS) major is based on the admission requirements for Penn State. Students who meet the University's minimum requirements for admission are eligible to enroll in this major.
Concentration: Baccalaureate-Oriented Option; Generalized Business Option; Individualized Option; Networking Option
Description: The Associate in Science in Information Sciences and Technology (IST) degree is a two-year program that provides students with a foundational knowledge of the information technology field. The program is designed to prepare students for entry-level positions in areas such as help desk support, network administration, database management, and web development. It also provides a solid foundation for students who wish to pursue a baccalaureate degree in Information Sciences and Technology or a related field. The curriculum focuses on the intersection of information, technology, and people, emphasizing problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills. Students will learn how to design, implement, and manage information systems that meet the needs of organizations and individuals.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Labor and Human Resources
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to an associate degree, an applicant must have a high school diploma or a General Education Development (GED) credential. For the Associate in Science degree in Labor and Human Resources, a minimum of 60 credits is required.
Description: The Labor and Human Resources (LHR) major is a multidisciplinary program that focuses on the world of work. The Associate in Science degree in Labor and Human Resources provides students with a foundational understanding of the employment relationship, including its legal, social, and economic dimensions. Students explore how employers, employees, and labor organizations interact in the workplace and the broader society. The curriculum combines courses in labor and employment relations, human resources, and the social sciences to provide students with a well-rounded education. Graduates of the program are prepared for entry-level positions in human resources, labor relations, and related fields, or for further study at the baccalaureate level.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Nursing
Requirements: Admission to the program is through the Penn State Undergraduate Admissions Office. To be considered for admission, you must have high school units in: English (4), Social Studies/Arts/Humanities (3), Science (3), Math (3, including algebra). You must have also completed one unit of high school biology and one unit of high school chemistry.
Department: Ross and Carol Nese College of Nursing
Description: The Associate in Science in Nursing (A.S.N.) degree program is designed for students who want to enter the nursing profession as quickly as possible. This four-semester program (plus one summer) provides the knowledge and skills necessary for the graduate to function as a registered nurse in a variety of settings. Upon completion of the program, graduates are eligible to take the National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses (NCLEX-RN).
Accredidation: The Associate in Science in Nursing (A.S.N.) program at The Pennsylvania State University at the Altoona, Fayette, Mont Alto, and Schuylkill campuses located in Altoona, Uniontown, Chambersburg, and Schuylkill Haven, Pennsylvania is accredited by the: Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN).

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Occupational Therapy Assistant
Requirements: General admission criteria are used to assess students' eligibility for the OTA program. High school grades in units of study are used to determine eligibility for admission. Prospective students must also complete 15 hours of observation in at least two different occupational therapy settings and submit a completed Clinical Observation Form with the application.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Associate in Science degree in Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA) prepares students to work as occupational therapy assistants under the supervision of occupational therapists. OTAs help people of all ages who have physical, developmental, social, or emotional challenges to lead independent, productive, and satisfying lives. The curriculum combines general education, biological and social sciences, and occupational therapy courses. Students learn through classroom instruction, laboratory activities, and clinical fieldwork experiences. Graduates are eligible to sit for the national certification examination for the occupational therapy assistant administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). After successful completion of this exam, the individual will be a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA). Most states require licensure in order to practice; however, state licenses are usually based on the results of the NBCOT Certification Examination.
Accredidation: The Occupational Therapy Assistant programs at Penn State Berks, Penn State DuBois, Penn State Mont Alto, and Penn State Shenango are accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA).

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Physical Therapist Assistant
Requirements: Entry to the PTA program is a two-step process: (1) Entry to Penn State; (2) Entry to the Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) Program. Students must first be admitted to Penn State. Once admitted, students will then apply for entry to the PTA program. Entry into the program is based on: 1) High school grades or college grades (if 18 or more college-level credits are completed); 2) SAT or ACT scores (if applicable); 3) Documentation of observation in a physical therapy setting; 4) A program application.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: Physical Therapist Assistants (PTA) provide physical therapy services under the direction and supervision of a physical therapist. PTAs implement components of patient care, obtain data regarding the treatment provided, and collaborate with the physical therapist to modify care as necessary. PTAs assist the physical therapist in the treatment of individuals with medical problems or other health-related conditions that limit their ability to move and perform functional activities in their daily lives. The goals of physical therapy are to improve mobility, restore function, reduce pain, and prevent disability. PTAs are employed in many settings, including hospitals, outpatient clinics, home health agencies, nursing homes, and schools.
Accredidation: The Physical Therapist Assistant programs at Penn State DuBois, Penn State Fayette, Penn State Hazleton, Penn State Mont Alto and Penn State Shenango are accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Radiologic Sciences
Requirements: Admission to the program is based on high school record (GPA) or, for transfer students, college academic record. Enrollment in the Radiologic Sciences program is limited, and students must be aware that admission to the University does not guarantee admission to the clinical component of the program. Admission to the clinical component is a separate process.
Concentration: Radiography, Diagnostic Medical Sonography
Description: The Radiologic Sciences major is a multi-option, clinical program. This degree program is designed to prepare students for careers as radiologic technologists or diagnostic medical sonographers. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the physical and biological sciences and includes extensive clinical experience. Students learn to use sophisticated imaging equipment to produce images of the human body that help physicians diagnose and treat medical conditions. The program emphasizes patient care, radiation protection, and professional ethics.
Accredidation: The Radiography option is accredited by the Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology (JRCERT). The Diagnostic Medical Sonography option is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (CAAHEP) upon the recommendation of the Joint Review Committee on Education in Diagnostic Medical Sonography (JRC-DMS).

ProgramName: Associate in Engineering Technology in Biomedical Engineering Technology
Requirements: Entrance to the Biomedical Engineering Technology major (2ET) requires that the student has: 1) completed MATH 22 or is eligible for MATH 26 or higher, and 2) completed CHEM 110. For the Associate in Engineering Technology degree in Biomedical Engineering Technology, a minimum of 68 credits is required.
Description: This major is a clinical-based program that provides students with the technical and clinical knowledge required to support medical technology in a clinical environment. Biomedical Engineering Technology is a multi-faceted field. It is the application of engineering and medical sciences to the use, repair, and maintenance of medical equipment in a clinical environment. Students learn how medical devices interface with the human body and how to determine if the equipment is operating safely. The curriculum provides a thorough knowledge of many types of medical equipment, including heart-lung machines, kidney dialysis machines, cardiac monitors, and other equipment used in the hospital. The clinical experience, which is an integral part of the program, provides students with an opportunity to work and learn in a hospital setting. The A.E.T. degree in Biomedical Engineering Technology is a terminal degree that qualifies graduates for employment in the biomedical engineering technology field.
Accredidation: The Associate in Engineering Technology in Biomedical Engineering Technology at Penn State New Kensington is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Biomedical Engineering Technology and Similarly Named Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Associate in Engineering Technology in Electrical Engineering Technology
Requirements: Penn State identifies and reviews a number of factors when making an admission decision. These include your high school grades and curriculum, your standardized test scores (optional), your class rank (if available), and other factors like your application essay and involvement in activities.
Description: This program is designed to provide students with a broad foundation in the principles of electrical and electronic systems. The curriculum includes courses in DC and AC circuits, digital electronics, microprocessors, and control systems. Students gain practical, hands-on experience in laboratory settings, where they learn to design, test, and troubleshoot electrical and electronic components and systems. The program also emphasizes the development of communication and problem-solving skills, preparing graduates for a variety of technical roles in the electrical and electronics industries. Career opportunities for graduates include positions in manufacturing, power generation and distribution, telecommunications, and field service.
Accredidation: The Associate in Engineering Technology in Electrical Engineering Technology at Penn State Harrisburg, Penn State Berks, and Penn State York is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Electrical/Electronic(s) Engineering Technology and Similarly Named Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Associate in Engineering Technology in Mechanical Engineering Technology
Requirements: Students must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. High school unit requirements include: 3 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of Science, and 5 units of other subjects. This program is currently only available at the Penn State Berks and Penn State DuBois campuses. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are not required for students applying for admission through the Fall 2025 semester.
Description: Mechanical Engineering Technology is a broad-based program designed to prepare students for a wide variety of entry-level positions in manufacturing, design, testing, and field service. Students learn to use the latest computer software for design and analysis and participate in a hands-on laboratory experience. The program provides a foundation in the fundamentals of engineering materials, manufacturing processes, applied thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and the design of machine elements. In addition, the program includes courses in mathematics, science, and communication. Graduates are prepared to work as engineering technicians in a wide range of industries or to continue their education in a baccalaureate degree program in mechanical engineering technology or a related field.
Accredidation: The Associate in Engineering Technology in Mechanical Engineering Technology at Penn State Berks, Penn State DuBois, Penn State Erie, The Behrend College, Penn State New Kensington, and Penn State York is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Mechanical Engineering Technology Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Associate in Engineering Technology in Nanotechnology
Requirements: For admission to the University, an applicant must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. To be eligible for admission to the Nanotechnology major, students must have a grade-point average of 2.0 or higher.
Description: The Associate in Engineering Technology in Nanotechnology degree program provides students with a strong foundation in the principles of nanotechnology and its applications in various industries. The program is designed to prepare students for careers as technicians in the semiconductor and other micro- and nanotechnology-related fields. Students will learn about the science and technology behind the fabrication and characterization of nanoscale materials and devices. The curriculum includes a hands-on capstone semester at University Park, where students gain experience in the state-of-the-art Penn State Nanofabrication Facility. Graduates are equipped with the skills necessary to work in research and development, manufacturing, and quality control.
Accredidation: The Associate in Engineering Technology in Nanotechnology at Penn State Altoona is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria. The Associate in Engineering Technology in Nanotechnology at Penn State Erie, The Behrend College, is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria.

ProgramName: Associate in Science in Wildlife Technology
Requirements: There are no additional entrance requirements for this major.
Description: Wildlife Technology is a two-year program that leads to an associate degree. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work as technicians in many fields of wildlife and fisheries management. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, as well as specialized training in wildlife and fisheries management techniques. The program emphasizes field-oriented training and provides students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in the use of specialized equipment and techniques used in the management of wildlife and fisheries resources. Graduates of the program are qualified for employment as wildlife technicians, fisheries technicians, biological technicians, and other related positions with state and federal agencies, as well as with private organizations and consulting firms. The program also provides a foundation for students who wish to pursue a baccalaureate degree in wildlife and fisheries science or a related field.
Accredidation: The Associate in Science in Wildlife Technology at Penn State DuBois is accredited by the North American Wildlife Technology Association (NAWTA).

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in a major that is not Accounting and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher. Admission into the Accounting minor is competitive. Students must have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, and (MATH 110 or MATH 140).
Description: The Accounting minor is designed for students in Smeal College of Business majors (other than Accounting) and for students in other Penn State colleges who want to supplement their major with a background in accounting. The minor provides students with a foundational knowledge of financial and managerial accounting, which can be useful in various business-related careers. Students will gain an understanding of how accounting information is used by internal and external stakeholders to make informed decisions.

ProgramName: Minor in Addictions and Recovery
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must have completed at least 45 credits and be in good academic standing.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Addictions and Recovery (ADREC) minor is intended for students who wish to gain knowledge about the biological, psychological, and social aspects of substance use and behavioral addictions. In addition to gaining a foundational understanding of the etiology and development of addiction, students will be introduced to several key areas within the field, including prevention, treatment, and recovery. The curriculum is also designed to help students think critically about the legal and socio-cultural impacts of substance use and addiction in the United States. While the ADREC minor is open to all students, it is particularly well-suited for those pursuing careers in the health and human services (e.g., healthcare, public health, social work, counseling, human development, criminal justice).

ProgramName: Minor in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Any student enrolled in a major at Penn State may apply for the Aerospace Engineering minor. Some prerequisites may be required. To be admitted to the minor, students must have a grade of C or better in AERSP 311 and AERSP 313. Some courses may require prerequisites. Students may apply for admission to the minor through the LionPATH 'Update Academics' tool.
Description: The Aerospace Engineering minor is designed for students in related engineering, science, and mathematics majors who wish to acquire an understanding of the principles of aerospace engineering. The minor is designed to provide a student with a basic foundation in the three primary areas of aerospace engineering: aerodynamics, aerospace structures, and astronautics. Additional courses in these and related areas (including flight dynamics and control, rotorcraft, etc.) may be used to round out the minor. The program is intended to provide a basic understanding of the fields that would enable the student to pursue a career in the aerospace industry or to pursue graduate studies in aerospace engineering.

ProgramName: Minor in African American Studies
Requirements: A student must be at least a fifth-semester standing to apply for a minor in the College of the Liberal Arts. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. The minor requires a minimum of 18 credits.
Description: The African American Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, culture, and experiences of African Americans and people of African descent throughout the Diaspora. Students can choose from a variety of courses in the humanities, social sciences, and arts to explore topics such as race, social justice, and the African American experience in a global context. The minor is designed to complement any major and provides students with a strong foundation for careers in fields such as education, law, social work, and public policy.

ProgramName: Minor in African Studies
Requirements: For a minor in African Studies, a minimum of 18 credits is required. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed at least one African Studies course.
Description: The African Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a multi-disciplinary understanding of the history, politics, societies, and cultures of Africa and its diaspora. Students take courses in a variety of fields, including history, political science, literature, art history, and anthropology. The minor provides students with the tools to analyze the complex issues facing the African continent today, as well as the historical and cultural contexts in which these issues have emerged. The minor is also designed to help students develop skills in research, writing, and critical thinking that will be useful in a variety of careers.

ProgramName: Minor in Agribusiness Management
Requirements: At least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and at least third-semester classification are required for admission. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the supplement 400-level courses must be taken from the Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education.
Description: The minor in Agribusiness Management is designed for students in other majors who are interested in the management of businesses that are part of the food and fiber system. It provides a basic understanding of the unique problems and opportunities associated with the agribusiness sector. Students learn about the economic environment in which agribusinesses operate and are introduced to the management, marketing, and financial functions of these businesses.

ProgramName: Minor in Agronomy
Requirements: Admission to the minor is by permission of the minor adviser. Students are required to have a 2.00 or higher grade point average to be admitted to the minor.
Description: The Agronomy minor is for students who wish to augment their major with a selection of courses that will provide them with a better understanding of the science of crop production and its importance in our society. The minor is flexible, allowing students to tailor their choices to their interests or to specific needs for their future career. Students who complete the minor will have an understanding of the relationship between soils and crops, and how to manage them to ensure high productivity and quality in an environmentally sustainable way. Employment opportunities for students with an Agronomy minor include: farm management; technical and sales representatives for the seed, fertilizer, and agricultural chemical industries; state and federal agencies such as the USDA-Natural Resources Conservation Service and Department of Environmental Protection; and private environmental and agricultural consulting firms.
ScholarshipType: Academic achievement, financial need, and/or professional interests

ProgramName: Minor in American Studies
Requirements: A student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average to be accepted into a minor. A student may not declare a minor until they have attained at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits). A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To graduate with this minor, at least 6 credits of the 18 credits for the minor must be at the 400-level.
Description: American Studies is the study of the culture(s) of the United States. Its focus is on the ideas, values, institutions, and aesthetic forms that have been important in the American experience. This interdisciplinary minor allows students to pursue their interests in American history, literature, art, and society. Students are encouraged to develop a program of study that reflects their individual interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Minor in Animal Science
Requirements: To be eligible to declare a minor, a student must have completed at least 1 semester of University enrollment and be in good academic standing (2.00 or higher cumulative GPA).
Description: The Animal Science minor is designed for students who wish to supplement their major with a basic understanding of the livestock and poultry industries and the scientific principles of animal production. This minor provides an opportunity for students to focus on a specific species or to gain a broad overview of the animal sciences.

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major program.
Description: Anthropology is the study of human biological and cultural diversity across time and space. It is a broad field that includes archaeology, biological anthropology, and cultural anthropology. The minor in Anthropology is designed to provide students with a broad overview of the field and to allow them to explore specific areas of interest in more depth. Students can choose to focus their coursework in one of the subfields or take a more general approach. The minor can complement a wide range of majors, including those in the social sciences, humanities, and natural sciences.

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have at least a 2.0 GPA. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor.
Description: The Arabic minor is designed to provide students with a good functional command of spoken and written Modern Standard Arabic. The program is intended to accommodate both students who have no prior knowledge of Arabic and those who have some background. The minor is a great option for students in a variety of majors (International Affairs, Political Science, History, Journalism, etc.) who wish to add an Arabic language and culture component to their primary field of study. Students who complete the minor will have developed a solid foundation in the Arabic language and will have gained an understanding of the culture and history of the Arabic-speaking world.

ProgramName: Minor in Architectural History
Requirements: To be admitted to a minor, an undergraduate student must be enrolled in a major and must have completed at least 18 credits at Penn State or have transferred at least 18 credits to Penn State.
Description: The Architectural History minor is intended for students who wish to complement their major field of study with an emphasis on the history of the built environment. It is particularly appropriate for students who are majoring in such fields as architecture, landscape architecture, history, art history, anthropology, and classics. The minor provides a foundation in the history of architecture from the ancient world to the present, and it allows students to pursue more specialized interests in various periods and themes.

ProgramName: Minor in Architecture
Requirements: The minor is open to all students, except those in the pre-architecture and architecture majors. Entry into the minor requires a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better. A student enrolled in this minor must receive a grade of C or better in all courses required for the minor, as specified in 12.A of the Senate Rules and Regulations. At least 6 credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor program in which the student is enrolled.
Description: The minor in Architecture is designed for students who are interested in the built environment and who wish to develop an understanding of the history, theory, and practice of architecture. It is intended to provide students with a broad overview of the discipline and to complement their major field of study. The minor is not a professional degree and does not lead to licensure as an architect.

ProgramName: Minor in Art
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be at least 3rd-semester standing and have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade point average.
Description: The Art minor is designed to provide students with the opportunity to integrate the creative and conceptual aspects of art making with their major field of study. The minor provides a basic foundation in the history of art and introduces students to a variety of studio art practices. Students will have the opportunity to explore a variety of media including drawing, painting, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, photography, and new media. Students who complete the Art minor will have a better understanding of the role of art in society and the importance of creative thinking in any field of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Art History
Requirements: At least six (6) credits of the minor must be unique from the 400-level courses required for the student's major program, or any other minor. To graduate with the minor, students must complete the requirements as specified by the program. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. A student may not declare a minor until they have been accepted into a major. Application for a minor is made in LionPATH.
Description: The Art History minor is intended for students who want to learn how to analyze the world of images and the built environment. Students are taught to look carefully, to think critically, and to write clearly. The minor helps to prepare students for careers in museums and galleries, as well as for graduate work in art history and related fields such as history, literature, or museum studies. In addition, art history provides a useful background for students entering professional fields such as law, business, or medicine.

ProgramName: Minor in Asian Studies
Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor after they have achieved at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits).
Description: The Asian Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a multi-disciplinary understanding of the history, cultures, and contemporary societies of Asia. Students take courses in a variety of fields, including history, literature, philosophy, religion, and the social sciences. The minor provides a strong foundation for students who are interested in pursuing careers in international business, law, government, or education, or who plan to do graduate work in Asian Studies or related fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Astronomy and Astrophysics
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative GPA and have completed MATH 140 and MATH 141 with a grade of C or better. At least 18 credits are required for the minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the student's major degree requirements.
Description: The Astronomy and Astrophysics minor is intended for students who want to gain a broader and deeper understanding of the universe. The minor is designed for students in any major who have completed the necessary prerequisites in physics and mathematics. Students will learn about the physical processes that govern the universe, from the formation of planets to the evolution of stars and galaxies.

ProgramName: Minor in Astrobiology
Requirements: To be eligible for the Minor in Astrobiology, a student must be enrolled in a baccalaureate degree program. Requirements for a minor must be completed in conjunction with a major degree program. A student must complete at least six credits of the minor at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by University Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor earned by the student.
Description: Astrobiology is a multidisciplinary field focused on the origin, evolution, and distribution of life in the universe. It involves research on the habitability of environments in our solar system and beyond, the search for biosignatures, and the study of the history of life on Earth. The Astrobiology minor is designed to provide students with a broad overview of the field and to provide them with the necessary background to pursue graduate studies in astrobiology or related fields. The minor is open to students in any major, but it is particularly well-suited for students in the sciences, engineering, and the social sciences.

ProgramName: Minor in Bioethics
Requirements: Students must be in at least their third semester at Penn State and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher. Some minors have additional requirements; however, this minor does not.
Description: Bioethics is a field of study that addresses the ethical issues that arise in the practice of medicine and the biomedical sciences. This minor is designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the ethical, social, and legal dimensions of health care and the life sciences. The Bioethics minor provides students with the opportunity to explore a variety of topics, including the physician-patient relationship, end-of-life care, reproductive ethics, research ethics, and justice in health care. This minor is particularly well-suited for students who are planning careers in medicine, nursing, other health-related professions, law, or public policy.

ProgramName: Minor in Biology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed BIOL 110 and have a 2.00 or higher GPA. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits must be upper-level (400-level) courses.
Description: The minor in Biology is designed to provide students with a broad background in the biological sciences. It includes foundational courses in biology and allows students to choose from a variety of upper-level courses in areas such as genetics, ecology, physiology, and cell biology.

ProgramName: Minor in Business
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the minor, a student must be enrolled in a major outside of the Smeal College of Business and have a cumulative GPA of 2.00 or higher.
Description: The Business minor is designed for students who are not in a Smeal College of Business major or a business major at other Penn State locations. The minor provides a broad overview of the world of business and provides students with the fundamental knowledge of accounting, economics, finance, management, and marketing. The minor is intended to provide students with a basic understanding of business to complement their major field of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Business Law
Requirements: To be eligible for the minor, students must have completed BLAW 341 with a grade of C or better and have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher.
Description: The Business Law minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the legal framework within which businesses operate. The minor is intended for students who wish to supplement their major field of study with a more in-depth knowledge of business law. This minor can be particularly beneficial for students planning careers in business, management, accounting, or for those who plan to pursue legal studies.

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Requirements: Students may apply for the minor in the Eberly College of Science after they have earned at least 45 credits and have been admitted to a major. Students must apply for the minor no later than the end of the second week of the semester in which they plan to graduate. For the minor in Chemistry, a minimum of 18 credits are required. At least six credits of the 18-20 credits for the minor must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits for the minor must be unique from the course requirements for a student’s major.
Description: The minor in chemistry is designed to provide students with a broad background in chemistry. It is especially suitable for students in other science majors and for students in engineering or the health sciences.

ProgramName: Minor in Chinese
Requirements: For the minor in Chinese, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. Some courses may require prerequisites.
Description: The Chinese minor is designed for students who want to develop a proficiency in Chinese language and gain a basic understanding of Chinese culture and literature. Students will develop their language skills through a series of language courses and will also choose from a variety of courses in Chinese literature, linguistics, and culture. The minor is a valuable addition to a major in any field, particularly for students interested in international business, government, or education.

ProgramName: Minor in Civic and Community Engagement
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have a 2.00 GPA and should submit an application. In the application, students state their goals for the minor and propose a series of courses and a public scholarship project to meet those goals.
Description: The interdisciplinary minor in Civic and Community Engagement (CIVCM) provides students from any major with the opportunity to extend their learning beyond the classroom through civic engagement and community-based research. Students in the minor work with faculty and community partners to address real-world issues and challenges through collaborative projects and research. The minor is designed to help students develop the skills, knowledge, and habits of mind necessary for active and effective citizenship in a diverse and democratic society. The minor is open to students in all majors and can be customized to align with students' academic and professional goals.

ProgramName: Minor in Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies
Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor after they have completed at least 3 credits of CAMS courses. To apply, students must have a minimum 2.00 grade-point average. A range of 18-24 credits is required for the minor. At least 6 credits must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with a basic familiarity with the history, literature, and archaeology of the cultures of the ancient Mediterranean world (including the Near East, Egypt, Greece, and Rome). Students are encouraged to develop their interests in particular areas of the ancient world through their choice of courses. The minor is intended to be flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their own interests.

ProgramName: Minor in Communication Arts and Sciences
Requirements: Admission to the minor is through the Liberal Arts Undergraduate Studies Office. A student's enrollment in the minor is normally done through LionPATH. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State.
Description: The Communication Arts and Sciences minor is for students who want to develop their understanding of how people use symbols, both verbal and nonverbal, to shape their relationships, communities, and cultures. The minor provides students with the opportunity to study communication in a variety of contexts, including interpersonal, small group, organizational, and public settings. Students will learn to analyze and evaluate communication processes and to develop effective communication strategies for diverse audiences. The minor is a valuable addition to many majors, as it provides students with the communication skills that are highly valued by employers in a wide range of fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Communication Sciences and Disorders
Requirements: Students with at least third-semester standing (min 29.1 credits) may be admitted to the minor by submitting an application in LionPATH. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The minor in Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the biological, physical, social, and psychological processes of communication and its disorders. This minor is particularly useful for students interested in human services, education, and health-related fields, but it is not a prerequisite for graduate study in CSD. Students will learn about the normal development of speech, language, and hearing, as well as the types of communication disorders that can occur across the lifespan.

ProgramName: Minor in Comparative Literature
Requirements: At the start of their junior year, students can declare their minor in LionPATH. To be eligible to declare a minor, a student must be enrolled in a major and have completed at least 30 credits. A student who wishes to declare the minor in Comparative Literature should consult with the Director of Undergraduate Studies in the Department of Comparative Literature and must submit an application for the minor in LionPATH. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To be eligible for the minor, a student must have a minimum overall grade point average of 2.00 in the courses required for the minor.
Description: The Minor in Comparative Literature is designed for students who want to study literature and culture from a global perspective. The minor provides students with the opportunity to study literature across national, linguistic, and cultural boundaries, as well as the relationship between literature and other media, such as film, music, and the visual arts. Students can explore a wide range of topics, including world literature, literary theory, translation studies, and the history of ideas. The minor is an excellent complement to a major in a foreign language, English, or any other field in the humanities, social sciences, or arts. It helps students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills that are valuable in a variety of careers.

ProgramName: Minor in Computer Science
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have completed CMPSC 121 or CMPSC 131 with a grade of C or better. A student must be in a major which does not require Computer Science (CMPSC) or Computer Engineering (CMPEN) for graduation.
Description: The Computer Science minor is designed to provide students in other majors with the opportunity to develop a solid foundation in computer science. The minor provides students with a background in programming, data structures, algorithms, and computer systems. The minor is available to all students except those in the Computer Science major.

ProgramName: Minor in Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Requirements: At least 4th semester standing is required. To be admitted, students must have a grade of C or better in ENTR 310.
Description: The Minor in Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIENT) is designed to provide students with a set of skills and a way of thinking that will help them to be more innovative and entrepreneurial in their careers. The minor is open to all undergraduate students at the University. The curriculum is designed to help students understand the innovation process, from the initial spark of an idea through to the development of a business model and the implementation of a new product, service, or process. Students will also learn how to manage innovation within established organizations and how to start and grow new ventures.
Accredidation: AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business

ProgramName: Minor in Creative Writing
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. For a minor in Creative Writing, a minimum of 18 credits is required.
Description: The Creative Writing minor is designed to help students who want to develop their own creative voices in poetry, fiction, nonfiction, and/or playwriting. It allows students to focus on a particular genre or to take courses in several genres. Students take workshops at the introductory, intermediate, and advanced levels. Students also take several literature courses as part of the minor, in order to gain experience in reading and analyzing poetry and prose as writers. For most of these workshops, the only prerequisite is the previous level of workshop; for the advanced workshops, however, students must submit a manuscript for the instructor's approval.

ProgramName: Minor in Criminology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have completed CRIM 100 with a grade of C or better and have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Description: The Criminology minor is designed to provide students with a social science perspective on the study of crime and the criminal justice system. It offers a selection of courses that explore the nature and causes of crime, the behavior of people in the criminal justice system, and the functions and operations of the system itself. The minor is intended for students who want to complement their major with a focus on crime and justice-related issues.

ProgramName: Minor in Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations
Requirements: Students must have completed 29.1 credits and be enrolled in a Penn State major to apply for this minor. A student may apply for the minor in LionPATH. For more information, please contact the IST Office of Undergraduate Academic Advising. To graduate with a minor, students must satisfy the requirements for the minor, including at least 6 credits at the 400 level. In addition, a student must complete at least six credits of the minor in courses that are not being used to satisfy the requirements of the student’s major. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Description: The Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations minor is intended to provide students with the fundamental knowledge and skills to analyze and evaluate cyber threats, and to develop and implement effective security measures. Students will learn about the technical, organizational, and human aspects of cybersecurity, including network security, cryptography, risk management, and incident response. The minor is open to students in all majors who are interested in developing expertise in cybersecurity and its applications in various domains.

ProgramName: Minor in Dance
Requirements: Students are eligible to apply for the dance minor after they have completed 6 credits in dance from the following: DANCE 170, DANCE 231, DANCE 241, DANCE 251, DANCE 261. An audition is required for entry into the minor. For a minor in Dance, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10.
Description: The Minor in Dance is intended for students who wish to pursue a program of study in dance while majoring in another field. The minor provides students with a broad-based foundation in dance through a curriculum that includes dance technique, history, and composition. The minor is available to all students in the University who are not majoring in dance.

ProgramName: Minor in Digital Arts
Requirements: Students must apply for entrance to the minor no later than the beginning of their junior year. To apply, students must have completed ART 110S or GD 100 with a grade of C or better. Applications are submitted through the Digital Arts Minor faculty committee. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits must be at the 400-level.
Description: The Minor in Digital Arts is designed to provide students with an introduction to the concepts and techniques of digital art. Students will explore the use of digital technology as a creative tool through courses in digital imaging, video production, and 2D and 3D animation. The minor is open to all students at the University who are interested in developing their skills in digital art.

ProgramName: Minor in Digital Media, Arts, and Technology
Requirements: At least 6 credits of the minor must be separate from any other certificate, major, or minor and the student must have at least a 2.00 grade-point average to be certified for the minor.
Department: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College
Description: The Digital Media, Arts, and Technology (DIGIT) minor is a multi-disciplinary program that provides students with the opportunity to explore the intersection of the arts, humanities, social sciences, and technology. It is designed to prepare students for the 21st-century workplace, which increasingly requires individuals who can bridge the gap between technical expertise and creative expression. Students in the minor will learn to think critically about the role of technology in society, while also developing the practical skills necessary to create and communicate in a digital world. The minor is open to students in all majors and is particularly well-suited for those who are interested in pursuing careers in areas such as web design, digital marketing, social media management, game design, and digital storytelling.

ProgramName: Minor in Earth Science and Policy
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must be enrolled in a baccalaureate program and have completed at least 30 credits at Penn State or another accredited institution.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Earth Science and Policy minor is designed to provide students with an opportunity to study the intersection of Earth science and public policy. The program is intended for students who wish to develop a better understanding of how Earth science information is used in the policy-making process and how policy decisions can affect the environment and the management of Earth resources. The minor is open to students in all majors who have an interest in the interface of Earth science and policy.

ProgramName: Minor in Earth Systems
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the supplement must be at the 400 level. Entrance to Minor: Students can apply for admission to the minor after they have achieved at least fifth-semester standing.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Earth Systems minor is designed to introduce students to the Earth as a system of interacting components: the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere. Students will learn about the physical, chemical, and biological processes that occur within and between these components, how they have changed over time, and how they are being affected by human activities. The minor provides a foundation in the physical and biological sciences and their application to understanding the Earth's environment.

ProgramName: Minor in East Asian Studies
Requirements: A student may apply for the minor in the department or through the office of the minor adviser. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. To graduate with a minor in Asian Studies, students must have at least 18 credits in Asian Studies, with at least 6 credits at the 400 level.
Description: The Asian Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a broad-based knowledge of Asian cultures, history, and societies. It is especially useful for students who are planning careers in international business, government, or education, or who are simply interested in learning more about a region of the world that is becoming increasingly important in the global community. The minor is flexible, allowing students to choose courses that focus on a particular country or region, or that explore broader themes across the Asian continent. Students are encouraged to study an Asian language as part of their minor program, although language study is not required.

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits must be at the 400 level. Prescribed Courses: ECON 102 Introductory Microeconomic Analysis and Policy (3 credits), ECON 104 Introductory Macroeconomic Analysis and Policy (3 credits). Supporting Courses and Related Areas: Select 12 credits of ECON courses (excluding ECON 489, 495, 496) (12 credits).
Description: The minor in economics is designed for students who want to develop a basic understanding of economics. The minor provides students with an introduction to the fundamental principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics and allows them to explore more advanced topics in economics.

ProgramName: Minor in Education and Public Policy
Requirements: To graduate with a minor, students must satisfy the requirements for the minor, including at least 6 credits at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. A student must complete at least 18 credits of course work. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. In addition, the student must select at least 6 credits from a set of approved courses in Education Policy Studies and at least 6 credits from a set of approved courses in other related disciplines such as political science, sociology, or economics.
Description: The Minor in Education and Public Policy (EPP) is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the research and theories used to understand and analyze how education and public policy intersect. Students in the minor will have an opportunity to examine both the historical and contemporary relationships between education and policy from various perspectives. Students will develop an understanding of how policies are developed and implemented, and they will explore the impact of policy on educational systems and individuals. The EPP minor is an interdisciplinary minor, drawing from the fields of education, sociology, political science, and economics. It is open to students in all majors who are interested in developing a deeper understanding of the role of policy in education.

ProgramName: Minor in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a major that provides a sufficient background in mathematics and physics. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The minor in Electrical Engineering is designed to provide students in related engineering and science majors with the opportunity to gain a significant background in the basic concepts and techniques of electrical engineering. The minor includes 12 credits of required course work and at least 6 credits of elective course work from a broad range of 300- and 400-level EE courses. The minor allows a student to gain both breadth and depth in areas such as control systems, communication systems, digital systems, electronic circuit design, electromagnetics, and power systems.

ProgramName: Minor in Energy and Sustainability Policy
Requirements: Students must apply for admission to the minor after they have earned at least 18 credits at Penn State and have been admitted to a major.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The minor in Energy and Sustainability Policy is designed for students who want to develop a broad understanding of the energy industry and the policy and sustainability issues that it faces. The program provides a foundation in the physical science of energy, the economics of energy markets, and the policy and ethical considerations that shape energy and sustainability decisions. Students will learn about the history of the energy industry, the current energy landscape, and the challenges and opportunities for a sustainable energy future. The minor is available to students in all majors at the University.

ProgramName: Minor in Energy Business and Finance
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must have completed at least 30 credits at Penn State with a minimum grade point average of 2.00. In addition, students must have completed ECON 102 GS(3) and MATH 110 GQ(4) or MATH 140 GQ(4) with a grade of C or better. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The minor in Energy Business and Finance (EBF) provides students with a basic understanding of the energy and environment industries. Many graduates from our minor go on to work in the energy industry, either for energy companies or in firms that provide consulting, banking, and legal services to the energy industry. The minor is also popular for students in the liberal arts and science fields who want more exposure to the business and economics of the energy industry. It provides students with basic skills in financial and economic modeling of the energy and environment industries and an understanding of the business and policy environment in which these industries operate.

ProgramName: Minor in English
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be taken at the 400-level.
Description: The minor in English consists of 18 credits in English, at least 6 of which must be at the 400 level. Because of its flexibility, the minor is an excellent way for students in other majors to develop their interests in literature and writing while preparing for any profession that requires strong communication and analytical skills. The Minor in English may be taken at any Penn State campus where the requirements can be met.

ProgramName: Minor in Entomology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a baccalaureate program at the University. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. To graduate with a minor, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the student's major degree requirements and at least six credits of the minor must be completed at the University at the 400-level.
Description: The entomology minor is designed for students who want to complement their major field of study with a focus on the biological and ecological aspects of insects. Insects are the most diverse group of animals on Earth and play critical roles in ecosystems, agriculture, and human health. This minor provides students with a foundational understanding of insect biology, including their anatomy, physiology, evolution, and classification. Students also explore the interactions between insects and their environment, as well as their impacts on human society, through courses in insect ecology, pest management, and specialized topics. The minor is flexible, allowing students to tailor their course selection to their specific interests and career goals in fields such as biology, environmental science, agriculture, and public health.

ProgramName: Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation
Requirements: For a minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits of the 18 must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. To be awarded the ENTI minor, students must complete at least 18 credits from the following lists, including: 9 credits of Core Courses, and 9 credits of Cluster Courses. Students may apply for the ENTI minor in LionPATH. Students are encouraged to apply as soon as they have decided to pursue the minor, but no later than the end of the second week of the semester in which they intend to graduate.
Concentration: Arts Entrepreneurship Cluster, Bio-tech Cluster, Digital Entrepreneurship & Innovation Cluster, Food and Bio-innovation Cluster, Hospitality Management Cluster, New Media Cluster, New Ventures Cluster, Social Entrepreneurship Cluster, Technology-Based Entrepreneurship Cluster
