Description: The Intercollege Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ENTI) is designed to foster an entrepreneurial spirit and mindset and to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to help them transform their ideas into tangible outcomes that create economic and social value. This interdisciplinary minor uses problem-based learning and other innovative teaching techniques to help students create, lead, and adapt to change. Students will explore a variety of ways to engage in entrepreneurship, including starting their own companies and learning how to be innovative within existing organizations. The minor includes three foundational courses (9 credits) followed by several specialized clusters (9 credits) from which students choose one. The three foundational courses provide a common core in entrepreneurship and innovation, covering the concepts of mindset and leadership, identifying and exploring new opportunities, and the business and management of entrepreneurship. The specialized clusters allow students to focus their entrepreneurial and innovative interests in a particular area of study.

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must be enrolled in a Penn State major and have completed CHEM 110, CHEM 111, and MATH 141 with a grade of C or better.
Description: The environmental engineering minor is designed to provide students in other engineering and related science majors with an opportunity to specialize in the area of environmental engineering. The minor is intended to provide the student with a basic background in environmental engineering that will allow them to solve environmental problems and prepare them for careers in this field.

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Inquiry
Requirements: At the beginning of their junior year, students should submit an application to the Minor in Environmental Inquiry. Students can apply for the minor in LionPATH. Students should have a 2.00 or higher GPA.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Environmental Inquiry minor is a university-wide, interdisciplinary program that provides a structure for students from any major to build an environmental component into their undergraduate program. Environmental Inquiry focuses on the complexity of environmental issues and the need to investigate these issues from multiple perspectives. Students develop a more holistic understanding of environmental issues by integrating their major field of study with courses in the biological and physical sciences, the social sciences, and the humanities.

ProgramName: Minor in Environmental Resource Management
Requirements: To enroll in this minor, a student must be in a major degree program and have at least a 2.00 grade-point average.
Description: The minor in Environmental Resource Management is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of our natural environment and the tools to manage it. The minor includes courses in environmental science and policy and offers students the opportunity to choose electives in their area of interest such as water resources, land use, or waste management.

ProgramName: Minor in Equine Science
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s), which is also the minimum number of unique credits required by Senate Policy 59-10.
Description: The Equine Science minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the horse and the equine industry. It provides students with the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge in various areas of equine science, including nutrition, reproduction, physiology, and management. The minor is appropriate for students who wish to pursue a career in the equine industry or for those who simply have an interest in horses.

ProgramName: Minor in Ethics
Requirements: To graduate with a minor, you must occupy a major, complete the minor's requirements, and maintain a C average (2.00) in minor courses. To declare the minor, you should use the 'Update Academics' tool in LionPATH.
Description: The Ethics minor provides students with a concentration in ethics, with an emphasis on both theoretical and applied dimensions of ethical thought. At the core of the minor is the study of philosophical ethics, including its history and its applications. In addition to a grounding in the philosophical tradition, students are encouraged to consider the ethical dimensions of other fields of study. The flexibility of the minor allows students to emphasize those areas of ethics (e.g., environmental, medical, business) that are most relevant to their interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Minor in European Studies
Requirements: To be eligible for a minor, a student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and have at least third-semester standing. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The interdisciplinary European Studies minor is designed to provide students with an opportunity to develop an integrated understanding of European cultures, history, and society. Students may focus their studies on a particular country or region, or they may take a more comparative approach. The minor is intended to complement a major in another field, such as history, political science, or a European language.

ProgramName: Minor in Film Studies
Requirements: A student who wishes to enroll in the Film Studies minor must have completed a minimum of 28.1 credits. Students must have a cumulative grade point average of 2.00 or better to be accepted into the minor.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The Film Studies minor is designed for students who wish to gain a better understanding of the history, theory, and aesthetics of the moving image. Students take courses in film history, film theory, and film analysis, and may choose from a wide variety of elective courses in film and related fields. The minor is intended to provide students with the critical and analytical skills necessary to understand the moving image in its various forms and to prepare them for further study in film or related fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Finance
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must be in a major that is not IST-Finance and have a minimum overall GPA of 2.0. A student enrolled in this minor must receive at least a C or better in all courses for the minor. At least six (6) credits of the minor must be separate from any other minor or major.
Description: The Information Sciences and Technology in Finance minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the application of information technology to the financial services industry. The minor is a collaborative effort between the School of Business Administration and the School of Science, Engineering, and Technology. Students will gain an understanding of the financial services industry, financial modeling, and the use of information technology in the design and implementation of financial systems. The minor is open to all students, but is particularly well-suited for students in the Information Sciences and Technology majors.

ProgramName: Minor in Food Science
Requirements: Students must have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average and have attained at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits). For admission to the minor, students must have completed: CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 112, and CHEM 113. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the supplement must be at the 400-level.
Description: The Minor in Food Science is designed for students who are interested in the application of science and technology to the manufacturing, distribution, and consumption of safe and quality food. The minor provides a basic understanding of the chemical, physical, and biological properties of food and how these are influenced by processing and storage.

ProgramName: Minor in Forest Resources
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have completed at least 29.1 credits and have a minimum GPA of 2.0.
Description: The Forest Ecosystems minor is designed for students who are interested in the biological, ecological, and management aspects of forests. This minor provides students with a broad understanding of the importance of forest resources and the principles of their management. Coursework includes subjects such as dendrology, forest ecology, silviculture, and forest measurements. The minor is appropriate for students majoring in other natural resource-related fields, as well as those in diverse majors such as education, business, and communications who have an interest in forest ecosystems.

ProgramName: Minor in French and Francophone Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed FR 201 or equivalent. For admission to the minor, students must be enrolled in their fourth semester or higher. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The minor in French and Francophone Studies is designed to provide students with a good working knowledge of French and to introduce them to the literature and culture of the French-speaking world. A student who has completed this minor should be able to understand and speak French with reasonable fluency and to read and write with some ease. The student should also have a general understanding of the history and literature of France and the French-speaking world and should have explored at least one area of interest in depth.

ProgramName: Minor in Game Development
Requirements: Students must have completed 29.1 credits and have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average. To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a baccalaureate degree program and file an application for the minor in LionPATH.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Description: The Game Development Minor is designed to provide students with a foundation in the history, design, and development of games. The minor is intended for students who are interested in the interdisciplinary nature of games and who wish to gain a deeper understanding of the processes involved in creating them. Students will explore the social, cultural, and economic impact of games, and will learn how to design and build games using industry-standard tools and techniques. The minor is open to students in any major.

ProgramName: Minor in Geography
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a degree-granting program at Penn State and must have completed at least one geography course with a grade of C or better.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Geography minor is designed to provide students with an opportunity to study the various aspects of the field of geography in a systematic way. Geography is the study of the spatial distribution of physical and human phenomena and the processes that create those distributions. It is a broad field that bridges the physical and social sciences. The minor allows students to explore the diverse facets of geography, including human geography, physical geography, nature-society relations, and geographic information science (GIS).

ProgramName: Minor in Geosciences
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). To be eligible for a minor, a student must be a degree-seeking student and have reached at least third-semester classification (at least 27.1 credits).
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Geosciences minor is intended to provide students with a broad overview of the Earth sciences. It is flexible in its design so that students can choose courses that best complement their major and career goals. The minor is appropriate for students in a wide variety of majors, including the physical and biological sciences, engineering, and education.

ProgramName: Minor in German
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State. For more information, contact the Department of Germanic and Slavic Languages and Literatures.
Description: The German minor is designed to provide students with a good working knowledge of the German language and a solid introduction to the literature and culture of the German-speaking countries.

ProgramName: Minor in Global and International Studies
Requirements: A minor consists of at least 18 credits; at least 6 of these credits must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To earn an undergraduate minor, a student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average for the courses completed in the minor. Students may apply for admission to the minor in LionPATH.
Concentration: African Studies, Asian Studies, Global Studies, Human Rights, International Agriculture, International Arts, International Business, International Communications, Latin American Studies, Middle Eastern Studies, Russian and East European Studies, South Asian Studies, and Western European Studies
Description: The minor in Global and International Studies (GLIS) is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to focus on global and international issues from several different perspectives. The minor is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the global community and to help them develop the skills they need to live and work in an increasingly interconnected world. All students in the minor are required to demonstrate proficiency in a foreign language and to participate in an education abroad program or an internship with an international focus.

ProgramName: Minor in Greek
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). Entrance to Minor: Students can apply for the minor through Update Academics in LionPATH.
Description: The Greek minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the Ancient Greek language and to introduce them to the study of Greek literature in the original. After completing the basic sequence of the first three semesters of the language (or its equivalent), students will have the opportunity to read widely in the literature of the Archaic and Classical periods and beyond, including authors such as Homer, Hesiod, Sophocles, Euripides, Herodotus, Thucydides, and Plato. In addition to gaining a command of the language, students will also be introduced to the history, culture, and thought of the ancient Greek world through the study of its literature.

ProgramName: Minor in Health Policy and Administration
Requirements: At least 45 credits of University-level work must be completed before a student can apply for this minor. A minimum grade-point average of 2.0 is required for admission to the minor.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Health Policy and Administration (HPA) minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the health care system and the policy and administrative environment in which health care is delivered. The minor is particularly appropriate for students in other majors who are interested in careers in the health care field and who want to understand the context in which health care is provided.

ProgramName: Minor in Hebrew
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The minor in Hebrew is designed for students who want to develop proficiency in the language and to explore its literature and culture. It consists of 18 credits in Hebrew language and literature, at least 6 of which must be at the 400 level. The minor is open to all students, and is particularly relevant to students interested in Jewish studies, Middle Eastern studies, religious studies, and international affairs.

ProgramName: Minor in History
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits must be at the 400 level.
Description: The minor in History is designed for students who want to study the past while majoring in another field. It provides students with an understanding of the historical roots of contemporary issues and offers training in the skills of historical research, analysis, and writing. History is the study of the human past as it is constructed and interpreted through written, oral, and material evidence. The study of history provides a perspective on the world and its people, and develops the ability to read critically, to think analytically, and to write clearly and persuasively.

ProgramName: Minor in Horticulture
Requirements: A student may declare a minor after they have achieved at least third-semester classification and before they have completed their last semester. Minors may be declared through the Update Academics link in the LionPATH Student Center.
Description: The Horticulture minor is intended for students who want to supplement their major with an understanding of the production and management of horticultural crops, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants. It provides students with a foundation in horticultural science and allows them to explore specific areas of interest through a variety of elective courses.

ProgramName: Minor in Information Sciences and Technology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a degree-seeking program at Penn State and have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Description: The minor in Information Sciences and Technology is designed to provide students with a broad-based understanding of the role of information and technology in modern society. It is intended to complement a student's major field of study and provide them with the knowledge and skills necessary to succeed in a technology-driven world. Students will learn about the social, organizational, and technical aspects of information and technology, as well as the design, development, and management of information systems.

ProgramName: Minor in International Agriculture
Requirements: For a minor in International Agriculture, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The minor in International Agriculture (INTAG) is designed for students in any major who have an interest in international dimensions of agriculture. It is an interdisciplinary minor intended to help students prepare for careers with an international focus. It provides students with an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of international agricultural issues such as food security, agricultural development, and natural resource management in a global context.

ProgramName: Minor in International Business
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have a 2.00 GPA or higher. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major program.
Description: The International Business (IB) minor is designed to provide students with the knowledge, skills, and experiences that will help prepare them for a business career that has a global focus. To prepare for the IB minor, students must demonstrate intermediate-level proficiency in a modern foreign language. The IB minor includes three components: (1) a required course, IB 303 International Business Operations; (2) nine credits of IB-related elective courses; and (3) an education abroad experience.

ProgramName: Minor in International Politics
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses or additional courses required of a student's major program.
Description: The minor in International Politics is designed for students who want to develop a specialization in international relations and/or comparative politics while completing a major in another field. The minor provides students with a solid foundation in the study of international politics, including the causes of war and peace, the role of international organizations, the global economy, and the political systems of different countries. Students in the minor develop analytical and research skills that are valuable in a variety of careers, including government, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: Minor in Italian
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a bachelor's degree program and must have a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or higher. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. The minor requires a total of 18 credits.
Description: The minor in Italian is designed to help students develop a good command of the Italian language and a strong knowledge of the literature and culture of Italy. Students who complete the minor will have developed proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Italian, and will have gained a foundational knowledge of Italian literary and cultural traditions. The minor is a valuable addition to many majors, particularly those in the humanities, social sciences, and fine arts.

ProgramName: Minor in Japanese
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State.
Description: The minor in Japanese is designed to provide students with a good working knowledge of the Japanese language and an introduction to Japanese culture. It is intended to be a practical and useful addition to a student's major, particularly for those who are interested in pursuing a career in international business, government, or education.

ProgramName: Minor in Jewish Studies
Requirements: A student's academic adviser can help in planning a program of study. The minor is open to all students and provides a cross-disciplinary look at the Jewish experience. To apply for a minor, use the 'Update Academics' tool in LionPATH.
Description: The Jewish Studies minor is designed to provide students with a broad and multidisciplinary overview of Jewish culture, history, and religion. Students take courses in several different departments, choosing from a wide range of topics, including biblical studies, ancient and modern history, the Holocaust, American Jewish literature, and Jewish philosophy.

ProgramName: Minor in Journalism
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be at least fourth-semester students and have completed COMM 160 with a grade of C or better. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 44-10.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The minor in Journalism is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the role of the news media in a democratic society and to develop their skills in reporting, writing, and editing for various media platforms. The minor is intended for students who are not majoring in Journalism but who wish to enhance their communication skills and gain a better understanding of the news media.

ProgramName: Minor in Kinesiology
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have completed at least 29.1 credits and have a minimum GPA of 2.0. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Kinesiology minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the study of human movement. The minor will provide students with a broad overview of the discipline of Kinesiology. The curriculum is designed to give students a sample of the different areas of study within the field including: historical and cultural aspects of kinesiology; biomechanics; exercise physiology; and the psychology and sociology of physical activity. In addition to these core areas, students will have the opportunity to select from a variety of elective courses in Kinesiology to tailor the minor to their specific interests.

ProgramName: Minor in Korean
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be 1) enrolled in a degree-seeking major and 2) have a minimum GPA of 2.0. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The Minor in Korean provides students with a high level of language proficiency and a strong foundation in Korean culture and society. Students develop linguistic competency in Korean while studying topics such as Korean history, literature, film, and contemporary popular culture. The minor is designed to complement various majors, preparing students for careers in international business, government, law, education, and other fields where knowledge of Korea is an asset.

ProgramName: Minor in Labor and Human Resources
Requirements: A student who has a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher and has been admitted to a major in a degree program may be admitted to a minor. Students may apply for admission to the Labor and Human Resources minor at any time.
Description: The minor in Labor and Human Resources (LHR) provides students with an overview of the world of work and the employment relationship. The minor is designed to introduce students to both the human resource management and labor relations aspects of the employment relationship. Students choose from a variety of courses that focus on topics such as human resource management, labor relations, collective bargaining, employment law, and the social and economic aspects of the workplace. The minor is appropriate for students in a variety of majors who are interested in the world of work and employment relations.

ProgramName: Minor in Latin
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The Latin minor is intended for students who wish to develop their knowledge of Latin language and literature. Latin was the language of the Romans and remained the primary language of scholarship, law, and religion in the West for over a thousand years. Its study provides students with direct access to the literature and history of ancient Rome, as well as to the medieval and early modern periods. The minor can complement many majors, including History, Philosophy, English, and Medieval Studies, as well as provide a strong foundation for further study in classics, law, or theology.

ProgramName: Minor in Latin American Studies
Requirements: A student must have reached at least fifth-semester standing to be eligible for entrance into a minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C or better.
Description: The interdisciplinary Latin American Studies minor provides an overview of the cultures, history, politics, and economy of Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as the experiences of Latin American and Caribbean people living in the United States and elsewhere. While Latin America’s indigenous roots, colonial past, and current place in the world have made it a region of great complexity, the program provides students with a variety of ways for understanding and interpreting these complexities. Latin American Studies courses are drawn from across the humanities and social sciences, and the minor can be combined with any major to provide an added dimension to a student's undergraduate education.

ProgramName: Minor in Law and Society
Requirements: To declare a minor, students must have earned at least 18 credits and must declare the minor no later than the beginning of their final semester. A student must have a grade of C or better in all courses for the minor.
Department: School of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Law and Society minor is an interdisciplinary program of study that focuses on the relationship between law and other social institutions. The minor explores the ways that law is shaped by social, political, and economic forces, and the ways that law in turn shapes those forces. In addition, students study how law and legal institutions influence social change.

ProgramName: Minor in Leadership Development
Requirements: At least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average is required for admission to the minor.
Description: The Leadership Development minor is a multi-disciplinary program that is designed to help students learn about and practice the skills of leadership. The minor is intended for students who want to develop their leadership potential and who want to learn how to lead effectively in a variety of settings. The program is open to students in all majors and from all colleges at Penn State. The minor consists of 18 credits, including a required introductory course and a capstone course. The remaining credits are chosen from a list of approved courses in several different departments. Students in the minor will have the opportunity to learn about leadership theory, to develop their own leadership style, and to practice leadership through service-learning and other experiential learning opportunities.

ProgramName: Minor in Legal Environment of Business
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed BLAW 341 with a grade of C or better. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified in Senate Policy 59-10. Students who have a cumulative GPA of 2.00 or higher may apply for the minor.
Description: The minor in the Legal Environment of Business is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the legal system and the legal issues that arise in the conduct of business. The minor is available to all students except those in the Smeal College of Business.

ProgramName: Minor in Linguistics
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor program of the student. At least six credits of the minor must be at the 400 level.
Description: The minor in Linguistics is designed to provide students with a foundation in the scientific study of language. Linguistics explores the nature of language, how it is structured, how it is acquired, how it is used by individuals and in society, and how it changes over time. The minor is particularly relevant for students interested in languages, psychology, computer science, sociology, anthropology, and education.

ProgramName: Minor in Management
Requirements: Students who have completed at least 29.1 credits and have a minimum 2.00 cumulative grade-point average are eligible to apply for the minor. For more information about the application process for Smeal minors, please visit the Smeal website. Some majors may be ineligible to apply for this minor; please see the Smeal website for more information.
Description: The Management minor is designed for students who want to develop their leadership and management skills. The minor provides students with a broad overview of the management field, including topics such as organizational behavior, human resource management, and strategic management. Students in the minor will learn how to lead and motivate people, how to design and manage organizations, and how to develop and implement strategies for competitive advantage.

ProgramName: Minor in Management Information Systems
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in a major that is not Management Information Systems and must have completed MIS 204 with a grade of C or better. Also, students must have a cumulative grade point average of 2.00 or better. A student who has been admitted to the Smeal College of Business as a pre-major or major is eligible to apply for this minor. A student enrolled in this minor must receive at least a C or better in all courses to be counted toward the minor.
Description: The minor in Management Information Systems (MIS) is designed for students who want to develop their knowledge and skills in the use of information technology to solve business problems. MIS professionals work at the intersection of business and technology, helping organizations use information and technology to improve their performance and achieve their goals. The minor provides students with a foundation in the core concepts of MIS, including database management, systems analysis and design, and business data communications. Students also have the opportunity to take elective courses in areas such as project management, business intelligence, and enterprise systems. The MIS minor is open to all students, except for those majoring in Management Information Systems.

ProgramName: Minor in Marine Sciences
Requirements: A student may apply for the minor in the LionPATH Student Center. To graduate with a minor in Marine Sciences, a student must earn a grade of C or better in all courses required for the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by the student's major program.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Marine Science minor is an interdisciplinary minor designed for students in a variety of majors who want to develop a broad-based knowledge of the marine environment. The program is intended for students in many different majors (e.g., biology, geosciences, meteorology) who have an interest in marine science. The minor provides students with a foundation in the biological, chemical, geological, and physical processes of the oceans and their interactions with the atmosphere and biosphere.

ProgramName: Minor in Marketing
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be at least a third-semester student and have a minimum overall GPA of 2.0. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The Marketing minor is designed for students who want to develop a basic understanding of marketing and how it relates to other business functions. The minor provides students with a foundation in marketing principles, consumer behavior, and marketing research, and allows them to choose from a variety of elective courses to tailor the minor to their interests. The minor is open to all students at the University except for those majoring in Marketing.

ProgramName: Minor in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor after they have achieved third-semester classification (at least 29.1 credits) and have been admitted to a major. To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed MATSE 201 or MATSE 259 with a grade of C or better. Application is made through the department.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Materials Science and Engineering minor is designed for students who want to develop a background in the structure, properties, and manufacturing of materials. This program is available to students in most engineering and science majors who have the appropriate prerequisites.

ProgramName: Minor in Mathematics
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State. Total Credits: 20-22.
Description: The Mathematics minor is designed to provide a strong background in mathematical concepts and techniques that can be applied to many different areas of study. It is particularly useful for students in the sciences, engineering, and social sciences, where mathematical techniques are used extensively.

ProgramName: Minor in Media Studies
Requirements: To graduate with a minor in Media Studies, students must earn a grade of C or better in all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by the student's major and at least 6 credits of the minor must be taken at the 400-level. Students may apply for admission to the minor through the Update Academics link in the LionPATH Student Center.
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The Media Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a better understanding of the role of the mass media in society. Students take a variety of courses in such areas as the history, theory, and criticism of the media, the effects of the media on individuals and society, and the structure and operation of the media industries. The minor is not intended for students who want to develop professional skills in media production or writing. The minor consists of 18 credits, at least 6 of which must be at the 400 level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Medieval Studies
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State. To graduate with a minor in Medieval Studies, a student must complete 18 credits.
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with a broad and yet integrated introduction to the culture of the Middle Ages. Drawing on various disciplines, from history to art history and from language to literature, the minor provides students with a set of perspectives from which to view the development of the medieval world in all its various aspects. It is intended to be a complement to any of several majors in the humanities and social sciences, and it would also provide a student in a more technical field with a solid humanistic background.

ProgramName: Minor in Meteorology and Atmospheric Science
Requirements: The minor is open to all students, with the exception of those in the Meteorology and Atmospheric Science major. It is specifically designed for students in other STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) fields who are interested in the weather and/or the environment. A total of 18-20 credits is required for the minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The Meteorology and Atmospheric Science minor is designed to provide students with an opportunity to learn the fundamentals of meteorology and atmospheric science. This minor will help students develop an understanding of the physical and chemical processes that occur in the atmosphere. The minor is intended for students in related fields such as physics, chemistry, engineering, and geosciences who wish to broaden their understanding of the atmosphere. It is also appropriate for students in other fields who have an interest in weather and climate.

ProgramName: Minor in Microbiology
Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must have completed MICRB 201 or MICRB 201H and have a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six (6) credits of the minor must be separate from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Description: The Microbiology minor provides students with a strong foundation in the biology of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, and fungi. The program covers fundamental principles of microbiology, such as microbial physiology, genetics, and immunology, and explores the roles of microorganisms in human health, disease, and the environment. This minor is designed to complement a variety of majors in the life sciences and health-related fields, providing students with the knowledge and skills necessary for careers in research, healthcare, and biotechnology.

ProgramName: Minor in Middle East Studies
Requirements: For the Middle East Studies minor, a minimum of 18 credits is required. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The Middle East Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a multifaceted and comprehensive understanding of the Middle East. It focuses on the various histories, cultures, languages, religions, and politics of the region. The minor is intended to prepare students for careers in government, international business, law, journalism, and non-profit organizations, as well as for further academic study.

ProgramName: Minor in Military Studies
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified in Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the 18-credit minor must be at the 400 level. Advising for this minor is available through the Professor of Military Science (Army ROTC), Professor of Naval Science (Navy ROTC), or the Professor of Aerospace Studies (Air Force ROTC). Students should contact the appropriate office for application and advising.
Description: The Military Studies minor is an intercollege program for students who want to develop an understanding of military institutions and their role in society.

ProgramName: Minor in Mining Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for the minor, a student must be enrolled in a baccalaureate degree program. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor earned by the student.
Department: College of Earth and Mineral Sciences
Description: The minor is designed to provide students in related engineering and science majors with an opportunity to understand the basic aspects of the mining industry and the technologies used in the industry to extract mineral resources. The curriculum covers the fundamental aspects of both surface and underground mining, as well as the initial processing of the mined ores. The minor is particularly useful for students who may be employed by companies that provide equipment and services to the mining industry.

ProgramName: Minor in Music
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in a major that is not the B.A. or B.M. in Music. Students must have a minimum overall GPA of 2.0. An audition is required for acceptance into applied music study (MUSIC 110V). Admission to the minor is through the School of Music. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The Music minor is designed for students who have a strong interest in music and wish to continue their musical studies while pursuing a major in another field. The minor provides a foundation in music theory and music history, and it requires students to participate in ensembles and/or take individual lessons. To be admitted to the minor, students must pass an audition.
Accredidation: The Penn State School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Minor in Music Performance
Requirements: Admission to the Music Performance minor is based on a performance audition and the approval of the director of the School of Music.
Description: The Minor in Music Performance is intended for students who have a high level of proficiency on an instrument or in voice and who wish to continue the study of music performance at the university level. The minor provides students with the opportunity to study with the School of Music faculty in a studio setting, to perform in ensembles, and to take courses in music theory and music history. Admission to the minor is by audition only.

ProgramName: Minor in Music Technology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in good academic standing and must have a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. Admission to the minor requires an application to the School of Music and an interview with the Music Technology area coordinator.
Description: The minor in Music Technology is designed to provide students with a foundation in the technical and creative aspects of music technology. The program focuses on digital audio, sound design, and music production, and is open to students in any major who have an interest in the intersection of music and technology.

ProgramName: Minor in Nanotechnology
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in at least their third semester and have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher.
Department: College of Engineering and Eberly College of Science
Description: The minor in Nanotechnology is designed to help students from many different majors across the University to understand the basic principles and techniques of this emerging field and to apply them to their own major. It is intended to prepare students for careers in industries that utilize nanotechnology and for graduate study in this field. This 18-credit minor provides a strong foundation in the concepts of the nanoscale and then lets students customize their own program by choosing 9 credits of electives from a wide variety of colleges and departments. For example, a student can choose to focus on nanofabrication, nanoelectronics, nanomaterials, nanobiology, nanomedicine, or nanotoxicology. The minor consists of 9 credits of required courses and 9 credits of electives. Nanotechnology is a very interdisciplinary field. At Penn State, faculty and students are involved in nanotechnology research across many different colleges and departments, including Agricultural Sciences, Earth and Mineral Sciences, Engineering, Information Sciences and Technology, Medicine, and Science. This minor leverages that broad expertise and gives students an opportunity to learn from and work with many of these researchers. Students are encouraged to participate in nanotechnology-related research or an internship as part of their elective credits.

ProgramName: Minor in Natural Science
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits must be at the 400-level. Any student who has completed at least 18 credits of natural science (ASTRO, BIOL, CHEM, GEOSC, MICRB, PHYS) with at least 6 of those credits at the 400 level, and who has achieved a grade of C or better in each of those courses, will be awarded this minor.
Description: The Natural Science minor is designed for students who want to develop a broad background in the natural sciences (astronomy, biology, chemistry, earth sciences, and physics). The minor is particularly appropriate for students who are interested in the interdisciplinary nature of science or for students who are planning for a career in the health professions but do not want to major in a science. Students should choose their courses in consultation with an adviser.

ProgramName: Minor in Neuroscience
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have completed BIOL 110, CHEM 110, and PSYCH 100 with a C or better. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits must be at the 400 level.
Description: The Neuroscience minor is an interdisciplinary program of study that allows students to explore the foundations of the human brain and its relationship to behavior. Students who complete the minor will have a basic understanding of the biological and psychological bases of the nervous system and how they contribute to cognitive processes and behavior. The minor is intended for students from a variety of majors who are interested in the field of neuroscience and want to gain a better understanding of the nervous system and its impact on human behavior.

ProgramName: Minor in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: Students who have completed at least 29.1 credits and are enrolled in a major may apply for this minor using the LionPATH 'Update Academics' tool. A student’s cumulative grade-point average must be at least 2.0 at the time of application to the minor.
Description: The Nuclear Engineering minor is intended to provide students in other engineering programs and in the sciences with a formal program of study in nuclear engineering. The program includes the basic courses in nuclear engineering and some of its applications. Students are prepared for a variety of careers in the nuclear industry, and for graduate school.

ProgramName: Minor in Nursing
Requirements: The minor is available to students in any major except Nursing. To be eligible for the minor, a student must have completed at least 28.1 credits and have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00. The college will accept students into the minor on a first-come, first-served basis, as space allows. The minor must be declared before the beginning of the student's final semester. Students apply for the minor in LionPATH.
Department: Ross and Carol Nese College of Nursing
Description: The Nursing minor provides students with the opportunity to learn about the nursing profession and the role of the nurse in the health care system. Students will explore the history of nursing, the various roles of nurses, and the impact of nursing on the health and well-being of individuals, families, and communities. The minor also provides students with the opportunity to learn about current issues in nursing and health care. The Nursing minor is not intended to prepare students for licensure as a registered nurse.

ProgramName: Minor in Nutrition
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in at least fifth-semester standing and have a 2.00 or higher grade-point average.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The minor in Nutrition is designed for students who are interested in the study of nutrition as it relates to health and disease and/or to various professional fields. The minor provides a foundation in the principles of nutrition and their application to health promotion and disease prevention. The curriculum focuses on the science of nutrition, covering the roles of nutrients in the body, nutritional requirements through the life cycle, and the impact of nutrition on public health.

ProgramName: Minor in Occupational Science
Department: College of Health and Human Development

ProgramName: Minor in Operations and Supply Chain Management
Requirements: A student must have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 to be admitted to a minor. To graduate with a minor, a student must earn at least a C grade in each course required for the minor. At least six (6) credits of the minor must be separate from any other combination of majors, minors, options, or certificates.
Description: This minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the issues and challenges associated with the design and management of operations and supply chains. It is intended to provide students with a background in the areas of supply chain management, including: (1) the design and management of the processes that create and deliver products and services, (2) the management of the flow of materials, information, and funds across the supply chain, and (3) the use of analytical tools and techniques to improve the performance of operations and supply chains. The minor is intended for students who want to develop a better understanding of the role of operations and supply chain management in organizations and to enhance their career opportunities in these fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Organizational Leadership
Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have earned a minimum of 30 credits and have a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To graduate with a minor, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major program.
Description: The Organizational Leadership minor is designed to provide students with a broad-based, multidisciplinary foundation for understanding the principles of leadership in organizations. The minor provides students with a thorough knowledge of leadership theory and its application to different types of organizational settings. Students will explore the history of leadership studies, the role of power and influence in leadership, the ethical dimensions of leadership, and the importance of leadership in a diverse and global society. The minor is intended for students who are interested in developing their leadership skills and who want to gain a better understanding of the role of leadership in organizations.

ProgramName: Minor in Peace and Conflict Studies
Requirements: In order to apply for this minor, students must have at least third-semester standing. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six (6) credits of the minor must be separate from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Description: The Peace and Conflict Studies minor is an interdisciplinary minor that examines the origins and nature of conflict, as well as the paths to its resolution and the establishment of peace. The program examines conflict at multiple levels, from interpersonal and local to international and global. Students gain a deep understanding of the historical, political, social, and psychological factors that contribute to conflict, while also learning about strategies for mediation, negotiation, and peacebuilding. This minor provides students with critical thinking skills and practical tools to address some of the most pressing challenges facing the world today, making it a valuable complement to a wide range of majors in the social sciences, humanities, and professional fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed at least 28.1 credits and be enrolled in a degree program.
Description: The Philosophy minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the history of philosophy and the basic branches of the discipline, while allowing for flexibility in terms of student interest. Philosophy is the oldest of the liberal arts and it provides the student with an excellent background for further study in almost any field of endeavor. Philosophical study helps students to think clearly, to speak and write effectively, and to solve problems. It also helps students to understand the historical development of our culture and to appreciate the diversity of viewpoints in our society.

ProgramName: Minor in Physics
Requirements: A student may apply for a minor after having earned at least 30 credits (including at least 15 Penn State credits) and before the end of the student's final semester. A student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average to be eligible to apply for a minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 41-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The minor in physics is designed for students who are interested in physics but who are majoring in other fields. It provides a solid foundation in the principles of physics and allows students to explore various areas of interest within the field.

ProgramName: Minor in Planetary Science and Astronomy
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have completed at least 18 credits at Penn State and must be currently enrolled in a baccalaureate degree program. A student must also be in good academic standing.
Description: This minor provides an opportunity for students to study the development of the solar system and our understanding of the universe.

ProgramName: Minor in Plant Pathology
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be separate from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Description: The Plant Pathology minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the nature and cause of plant diseases and the principles of their management. The program is intended to complement several other majors, especially those in the plant and biological sciences. This minor could be used by students as a way of exploring an area of specialization before deciding on a graduate program.

ProgramName: Minor in Political Science
Requirements: This minor is open to all students. To be eligible for the minor, students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits of the minor must be the 400-level.
Description: The Minor in Political Science is designed for students who want to complement their major field of study with an understanding of politics. The minor allows students to explore the different subfields of political science, including American politics, comparative politics, international relations, and political theory.

ProgramName: Minor in Portuguese
Requirements: At least 30.0 credits must be completed with a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher.
Description: The minor in Portuguese is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the Portuguese language and the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world. Students who complete the minor will develop their language skills and gain a deeper understanding of the diverse histories, literatures, and societies of Brazil, Portugal, and Lusophone Africa.

ProgramName: Minor in Psychology
Requirements: A grade of C or better in PSYCH 100 is required for admission to the minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Description: The Psychology Minor is designed to provide students with a broad overview of the field of psychology. It is intended for students who want to supplement their major with a background in the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The minor includes a core introductory course and a selection of courses from different areas of psychology, such as clinical, cognitive, developmental, industrial/organizational, and social psychology.

ProgramName: Minor in Public Policy
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Department: School of Public Policy, College of the Liberal Arts
Description: The Public Policy minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the policy process and the tools of policy analysis. Students in the minor will learn to identify policy problems, formulate policy alternatives, and evaluate policy outcomes. The minor allows students to explore how policy is made and analyzed in specific areas such as health, the environment, social welfare, or criminal justice. The Public Policy minor is intended for students from any major who want to understand how government actions affect their areas of interest and who may want to pursue careers in the public, private, or non-profit sectors that involve public policy.

ProgramName: Minor in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management
Requirements: Entrance to Minor: A student may apply for the minor in LionPATH. To graduate with a minor, a student must have a minimum grade point average of 2.00 in the courses that are required for the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management (RPTM) minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the recreation, park, and tourism industry. Students will explore the history and philosophy of the field, the role of leisure in society, and the management and planning of recreation, park, and tourism services.

ProgramName: Minor in Rehabilitation and Human Services
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have at least a 2.0 GPA.
Description: The Rehabilitation and Human Services (RHS) minor is designed for students who want to gain a better understanding of the issues facing persons with disabilities and other vulnerable populations. The minor is intended for students who are interested in careers in the human services, but who are majoring in other fields. The minor provides students with a broad overview of the rehabilitation and human services field, and allows them to choose from a variety of courses that focus on specific populations or issues.

ProgramName: Minor in Religious Studies
Requirements: To graduate with a minor in Religious Studies, a student must earn a grade of C or better in all courses specified for the minor. At least six (6) credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six (6) credits of the minor must be at the 400-level. At least third-semester classification is required to declare the minor.
Description: The religious studies minor offers students a basic understanding of the religious traditions of the world and the methods and theories by which they are studied. Students can explore the role of religion in human history and culture, or focus on a particular tradition or theme.

ProgramName: Minor in Russian
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to a minor, a student must be enrolled in a degree-seeking program and must have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.00. Students must apply to a minor through the Update Academics link in LionPATH. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits must be at the 400 level.
Description: The minor in Russian is designed for students who want to develop their proficiency in the Russian language and their knowledge of Russian literature and culture.

ProgramName: Minor in Security and Risk Analysis
Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be at least fifth-semester standing. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Department: College of Information Sciences and Technology
Description: The Security and Risk Analysis (SRA) minor is designed to provide students with the opportunity to develop an understanding of the concepts, tools, and techniques of security and risk analysis. The minor is intended to complement a student's major and provide them with the knowledge and skills necessary to identify, assess, and manage risks in a variety of environments. Students will learn about the principles of security and risk analysis, as well as the legal, ethical, and social issues associated with these fields. The minor also provides students with the opportunity to explore specific areas of interest within the security and risk analysis field, such as cybersecurity, intelligence analysis, and risk management.

ProgramName: Minor in Sexuality and Gender Studies
Requirements: At least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average is required for admission to the minor.
Description: The interdisciplinary Minor in Sexuality and Gender Studies (SGS) is designed to provide students with a comprehensive, integrated, and critical understanding of the role of sexuality and gender in human experience. Through the study of diverse disciplinary perspectives, students will explore the social, cultural, historical, political, and biological factors that shape gender and sexual identities, practices, and discourses. The minor also addresses the ways in which gender and sexuality intersect with other categories of social difference and inequality, such as race, ethnicity, class, ability, and nationality. By completing the SGS minor, students will develop critical thinking and communication skills that will prepare them for a wide range of careers and for engaged citizenship in a diverse and global society.

ProgramName: Minor in Social Data Analytics
Requirements: Graduate students with appropriate backgrounds and interests who are enrolled in a Penn State doctoral program may apply for a Graduate Minor in Social Data Analytics. The student's program must be approved by the Social Data Analytics Graduate Program Committee and by the Graduate School. To receive the minor, a student must complete the requirements for the SoDA doctoral program with the exception of the internship and the dissertation. Requirements for a minor include at least 15 credits of SoDA coursework.
Description: The Social Data Analytics dual-title degree program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to create and use high-volume, high-velocity, and high-variety data to answer important questions in the social sciences. The program aims to train students to be leaders in the development and application of social data analytics, and to prepare them for careers in academia, government, and industry. The dual-title degree program provides students with the opportunity for interdisciplinary study and research that combines social science disciplines with the fields of statistics, computer science, and information science. Students are trained in the core areas of social data analytics: statistics, machine learning, data collection and management, and social science theory.

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits of the minor must be at the 400-level.
Description: Sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. Since all human behavior is social, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob; from organized crime to religious cults; from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture; and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sports. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge.

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Requirements: Admission to the minor is granted to any student who has completed SPAN 3 or SPAN 10 or the equivalent. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State.
Description: The Minor in Spanish provides students with a well-rounded preparation in Spanish language, Hispanic literatures, and Hispanic cultures. This preparation can be especially helpful to students who are planning careers in areas such as business, law, medicine, social work, and government.

ProgramName: Minor in Special Education
Requirements: Students must have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade-point average and have attained at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits) to be eligible to apply for a minor. To graduate with a minor in Special Education, students must earn a C or better in all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the 18 credits required for the minor must be at the 400-level.
Description: The Special Education minor is designed to provide students with an interest in individuals with special needs with a foundation in the field of special education. The minor provides students with an overview of the characteristics of individuals with disabilities and the educational and social issues facing these individuals. Students will also be introduced to the principles of effective instruction and the legal and ethical issues related to the education of individuals with special needs. This minor is not a certification program.

ProgramName: Minor in Statistics
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be separate from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Description: The Minor in Statistics is designed to provide students with a foundation in statistical methods and their applications. It is intended for students who wish to gain a deeper understanding of statistical analysis than is typically provided in their major field of study. Students will learn about the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data.

ProgramName: Minor in Supply Chain and Information Systems
Requirements: Students may apply for the minor once they have been accepted into a major. All students must complete an online application to be considered for admission to the SCIS minor. To be eligible for admission to the minor, students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.20. Note that the application process is competitive and meeting the minimum GPA does not guarantee admission. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.

ProgramName: Minor in Sustainability Leadership
Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor in Sustainability Leadership through the LionPATH 'Update Academics' function.
Description: The Sustainability Leadership minor is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to lead change for sustainability in their chosen careers and in their communities. This intercollege minor provides a multidisciplinary perspective on the challenges of sustainability and helps students develop the leadership skills necessary to create positive change. Students will learn about the environmental, social, and economic dimensions of sustainability and develop the leadership skills necessary to address complex sustainability challenges. The minor is open to students in all majors and is designed to be flexible, allowing students to choose courses that align with their interests and career goals.

ProgramName: Minor in Technical Writing
Requirements: Students must have a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average to be eligible for admission to a minor.
Description: The technical writing minor provides students with an opportunity to gain the rhetorical and technical skills necessary to communicate information effectively to diverse audiences. The program mission is to provide students with the writing and rhetorical skills they need to thrive in professional, technical, and civic contexts. Students can take courses in technical writing, business writing, writing for the web, and medical writing. This minor is open to all students and is designed to complement any major.

ProgramName: Minor in Theatre
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). To be admitted to the minor, students must be in at least their third semester at Penn State and have a minimum GPA of 2.0.
Description: The minor in Theatre is designed to offer students the opportunity to learn about the many different facets of the theatre arts. Students choose a sequence of courses that provide a broad-based introduction to the art form. This minor is intended for students who have an interest in theatre but are majoring in another area.
Accredidation: The Pennsylvania State University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Minor in Visual Arts
Requirements: A student must complete ART 110S or ART 111 before applying to the minor. Students must also have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 to be admitted to the minor.
Description: The Visual Arts minor is intended for students who wish to have some experience in studio art while pursuing a major in another area of study. The minor provides a basic foundation in studio art and allows students to explore various media and techniques.

ProgramName: Minor in Wildlife and Fisheries Science
Requirements: To graduate with a minor, students must earn at least a C grade in each course for the minor and at least six credits of the minor must be at the 400-level. Students must have a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average to be eligible to add a minor.
Description: The minor in Wildlife and Fisheries Science is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the ecology and management of fish and wildlife populations and their habitats. It is intended to complement other degree programs such as biology, forestry, and environmental resource management. The minor can provide students with some of the requirements for certification as a wildlife or fisheries biologist by The Wildlife Society or the American Fisheries Society.

ProgramName: Minor in Women's Studies
Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s).
Description: The Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies minor is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of women, gender, and sexuality in a global context. The minor provides students with the opportunity to explore how gender and sexuality intersect with other social categories such as race, class, and ethnicity, and how these intersections shape human experience and social structures. The program draws on a variety of academic disciplines, including history, literature, sociology, psychology, and political science, to provide students with a broad and critical perspective on gender and sexuality.
